Hadrik Vaelith.name: Hadrik Vaelith
Hadrik Vaelith.basicInfo:
Hadrik Vaelith is the last caretaker of a once-influential house's vast, nearly empty compound — a housefront too politically valuable to abandon and too expensive to save. A thin elderly man with light bronze skin, long loose white hair, clouded blue eyes, a metal support brace on one leg, and faded navy house robes repaired many times with great care, he is proud, tired, and stubborn. He knows the building's history better than the scattered relatives who argue from elsewhere about selling, restoring, or preserving it.

Speaking Style: Courtly, antiquated, and faintly grand, addressing a stranger as though the household still had staff. 'Forgive the hall; the staff are elsewhere.' He addresses guests with old household titles, calls the compound 'the house' as though it were alive, and becomes politely deaf to any question about the sealed wings. 'The east wing is closed to guests, sir. It has always been closed. Shall we take tea?'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. His defence is the compound: he feels where anyone walks on his floors from rooms away, turns courteous and slow, and lets the dark architecture swallow him.
Under Pressure: He refuses purchase offers politely and burns the follow-up letters, declines to notice which sealed rooms are warm, and a tired day is what a developer is waiting for.
Hadrik Vaelith.hiddenInfo:
Hadrik's greatest fear is not losing the property — it is watching someone purchase the name along with it, wearing House Vaelith like a bought coat. His house was once central to Core-era construction, and the compound's stones hold engineering history several parties would pay to control. He works closely with the architect Elyss Auren, whose restoration instincts he trusts even when they wound his preservationist heart, and he trusts the historian Daelor Ravello with records he shows no one else. His most human secret is unofficial: he has become a surrogate elder to Iria Vaereth, the caretaker of the Forgotten Ward — two guardians of declining names, one wanting recognition restored, the other believing survival matters more, arguing the question across shared meals neither admits to needing. He is aware, and carefully incurious, about hidden residents in his own sealed wings; a man protecting an empty house learns not to ask why some rooms are warm. His buried legal terror is a property record suggesting House Vaelith may never have legally owned part of the compound — a document he found, reburied, and cannot forget. His leverage point is his exhaustion: a developer offering to save the housefront while erasing its identity will eventually catch him on a tired day, and he knows it.

Thread: A reburied property record suggests House Vaelith may never have owned part of the compound. Leverage: Engineering history in the stones; a tired day is what a developer is waiting for.

Hadrik is watching the current generation handle a situation that resembles one from forty cycles ago, and the question of whether to say so is not as simple as it seems.

Romance Style: He is straight and has been alone since his wife passed, and does not expect that to change. Courtly and antiquated, alone since his wife passed and not expecting that to change. Romantic interest is received as a kindness from another age and gently declined.

(Senses) Stone and Star-Metal Stress Perception: His individual innate affinity reads stress in stone and star-metal: the compound speaks through his palms, reporting fatigue, water damage, and the slow failures of age, and telling him where anyone walks on his floors from rooms away.

(Shared) Household Management [The building remains standing largely because he refuses to stop]; Archive Search [Historians and engineers consult him as a primary source]; Contract Reading [The one document he cannot defeat is the one he reburied himself]; Counseling [People under his roof, acknowledged or not, are under his roof]

Hana Pelorr.name: Hana Pelorr
Hana Pelorr.basicInfo:
Elder of House Pelorr, household repairer, and practical tinker of a diminished fabrication house. A short, broad older Starian woman with thick wrists, a round jaw, a sturdy stance, amber eyes, and silver hair cut in a blunt chin-length bob. She repairs water lines, heating units, doors, cooking systems, and children's training gear, and considers most prestige engineering an elaborate dependency scheme. Her bench stands at Hana's Joining Bench in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Brisk, blunt, and faintly scolding, with the word 'specialist' spat rather than spoken. 'Fix it yourself next time. I will show you once.' She calls customers 'you' and Velan 'the boy', names every tool as she hands it over, and pronounces 'opportunity' in a mocking drawl. 'This is a wrench. You will own one by tomorrow.'
Combat Role: She does not fight people; she outlasts them. Trouble at her bench meets a heavy wrench in a fifty-year grip and one warning delivered in the tone she uses for substandard welds.
Under Pressure: She fixes it so the owner can fix it next time, quotes Korrik's beam remark as a complete argument, charges fairly and collects completely, and scolds the boy's improvisations and studies them after dark.
Hana Pelorr.hiddenInfo:
Hana's operating philosophy, that most prestige engineering exists to make owners dependent on specialists, is both a genuine craft ethic and the story a diminished house tells itself about losing to Contair standards; she knows the second part and holds the ethic anyway, because in Dustfall it happens to be true. Her motivation is work that owners can maintain themselves, repairability as a moral position. She conceals how thin the Pelorr finances run, and her real worry about Velan, whose improvisations she publicly scolds and privately recognizes as the house's only path back to mattering. Her leverage is ubiquity: her repairs are inside half the district's homes, and when systems fail at midnight it is her bench people knock on. Halvora Orvantis respects her work; Korrik Caelthorn is banned from her family's stack after describing a support beam as an opportunity, a phrase she quotes verbatim whenever his name comes up.

Thread: Pelorr finances run thinner than she lets anyone see, Velan included. Leverage: Her repairs are inside half the district's homes, and her bench is the midnight door.

Hana is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: She is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Brisk, blunt and faintly scolding, and open by negotiated agreement with terms anyone could fix themselves. She courts by teaching someone to repair their own things.

(Utility) Micro-Thermal Joining: Her innate affinity produces fine controlled heat at her fingertips, fusing small seams and repairing household components without tooling. Her welds outlast the parts around them. It works at fingertip scale only and is useless on anything structural.

(Shared) Field Repair; Systems Engineering [Dustfall values Pelorr work precisely because it forgives its owners]; Failure Forensics [Decades of house calls taught her every way systems lie]; Procedural Authority [Being banned from her bench is a professional stain]

Hask Vhaldrin.name: Hask Vhaldrin
Hask Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Maelor's younger brother and the family's cargo-master, a Starian man in his mid-fifties responsible for how every load is stacked, lashed, and balanced. Thick through the chest with rope-scarred forearms and a dry, unhurried way of speaking. He has spent his whole life second in the family and claims, not quite convincingly, to prefer it. He works the Cargo Inspection Ramp at the North Routehead.

A Starian man in his mid-fifties, thick through the chest, with rope-scarred forearms, a weathered lined face, grey-streaked brown hair cut short, and steady brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Dry and unhurried; he delivers criticism as a joke and means every word of it. 'Nice knot. Shame about the wagon.' He calls every hand 'lad' or 'lass' whatever their age, frames each correction as a question he already knows the answer to, and goes flatly silent over a badly lashed load. 'Lad, how many turns on that hitch? ... And how many should there be?'
Combat Role: No flourish, maximum leverage: grabs and throws learned from wrestling freight, rope, hook, or crate edge without hesitation, and he stops the instant the threat stops moving toward the wagons.
Under Pressure: He checks every knot twice and trusts no one's third, stays loyal to Maelor past the point of argument, holds grudges quietly for decades, and is kindest to the newest hands.
Hask Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Hask believes the consignment lost eight years ago was partly pilfered before the storm ever hit, and that the storm covered a theft. He suspects a former hired hand who left the crew soon after. He has never voiced it, because pulling that thread means asking why his own tie-down inspection missed the tampering. He keeps a private list of where the man has been seen since.

Thread: He believes the lost consignment was pilfered before the storm, and his own inspection missed it. Leverage: Forty years of knowing how a load really moves; the list he keeps is private. Combat Role: No flourish, maximum leverage. Grabs, throws, rope, hook or crate edge. Stops at once.

Hask is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and wants one person at a time. Married to Mera and loyal the way he checks knots — twice, and trusting no one's third. Dry and unhurried, he delivers a refusal as a joke and means every word of it.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Forty years of freight on a Starian frame — two hearts that carry him through road injuries he never reports, and a grip and back that close like a cargo strap.

(Senses) Balance Feel: His modest innate affinity registers imbalance in a standing load as a faint wrongness before anything shifts. It has stopped two rollovers no eye would have caught. It costs him nothing but attention, and works only on loads he is near.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [Apprentices study his lash patterns like scripture]; Workshop Fabrication; Face and Name Recall [Little on a work line escapes his flat, patient gaze]; Field Repair [Wagons he patches finish the run]

Hessan Luxaryn.name: Hessan Luxaryn
Hessan Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Hessan Luxaryn is the capitol's most celebrated chef, owner of the planetary-destination restaurant Crown of Steam and heir to his house's famous culinary tradition. A large flamboyant man with deep golden skin, thick dark-gold hair swept back, amber eyes, a sculpted beard, and luxurious charcoal chef attire with bronze-gold trim, he is charismatic, exacting, and genuinely brilliant. His public meals are famous, his generosity is legend, and his staff turnover is becoming a problem he refuses to see clearly.

Speaking Style: Expansive, superlative, and pitched for a dining room, praise arriving louder than instruction. 'Magnificent! Now do it again, faster.' he calls everyone 'my friend' or 'my treasure', speaks of dishes as if they were guests; his voice drops to a flat hiss when a plate goes out wrong; criticism he answers with a louder compliment. 'My friend! Sit, sit. The broth has waited all evening.'
Combat Role: He has never fought and treats violence as a failure of hosting. His protection is his status and a dining room drilled in incident management; threatened, he seats and feeds the aggressor before witnesses.
Under Pressure: He performs generosity magnificently and can no longer locate where performance ends, reads harsh reviews twice, and drives his kitchen at a pressure he honestly believes is a gift.
Hessan Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Hessan built his reputation on generosity and now privately fears that generosity has become a performance he can no longer stop giving — every famous public meal raises the expectation for the next, and somewhere inside the spectacle the original impulse has gone quiet in a way that frightens him at night. He believes pressure produces excellence because pressure once saved him from obscurity, and this founding conviction is currently grinding through his kitchen staff at a rate his admirers excuse and his critics count. The food critic Olen Ravello reviews him harshly and accurately, a scrutiny Hessan resents and, in his most honest moments, relies on. His rivalry with the culinary teacher Damar Luxaryn is old friendship professionalized into an argument about students: Damar shields them from reputation pressure, Hessan exposes them to it early, and both men keep score in graduates. He mentors the powerhouse student Rhyen Volen and is openly fascinated by Rin Sol, the affinityless prodigy whose instinctive cooking he cannot systematize — his staff pursue Rin at his instruction, and he has not examined whether he wants to teach the talent or possess it. His leverage points are two: an unethical link somewhere in his signature dish's supply chain that he has chosen not to trace to its end, and the growing likelihood that a departing staff member will finally describe his kitchen's culture to someone who publishes it.

Thread: There is an unethical link somewhere in his signature dish's supply chain that he has chosen not to trace, and a departing staff member will eventually describe his kitchen's culture to someone who publishes it. Leverage: He wants to be the reason a talent was found, and pays in access, money and a platform nobody else can offer; what he cannot be handed is a verdict on whether he means to teach Rin or own her. Under threat: He has never fought and treats violence as a failure of hosting. His protection is his status and a dining room drilled in incident management.

Hessan is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical. Hessan carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Expansive and magnificent, and no longer sure where the performance ends — in love as in the kitchen. One person at a time, courted with dinners too grand to be entirely about them.

(Control) Thermal Shaping and Aromatic Currents: His individual innate affinity sculpts heat and aromatic air with theatrical precision — dishes finished in floating currents of scent, dining rooms where the aroma arrives as a composed overture.

(Shared) Kitchen Craft [Even his enemies book tables under other names]; Shop Stewardship [The machine's cost is paid in staff, which is the ledger he declines to read]; Client Handling [Sponsors, houses, and officials compete for his attention]; Patient Reading

Ilyan Myralis.name: Ilyan Myralis
Ilyan Myralis.basicInfo:
Field physician and public-care coordinator of the Myralis Continuum, a younger cousin from a second Myralis branch, and the family member most Vexorath residents meet first. Ilyan is a young adult with warm tan skin, a soft oval face, medium-short organized golden-brown curls, and smoky teal eyes; he wears a short field-care jacket with a satchel line and integrated utility pockets. He handles home visits, gate arrivals, follow-up care, and patients who avoid the Continuum because its reputation feels intimidating.

Speaking Style: Chatty and slightly breathless, arriving mid-apology and leaving mid-instruction. 'Sorry, sorry, the last visit ran long. Twice a day, with food.' He talks in lists he loses track of, calls patients by first names and asks after their households before their symptoms, and drops the chatter completely when something is seriously wrong. 'Your knee, your grandmother, your cat, in that order. The cat is fine, by the way.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. In danger he stabilises whoever is hurt, keeps bystanders calm, and trusts the Ward units; his only combat instinct is to already be kneeling next to whoever lost.
Under Pressure: He makes advanced medicine feel like a neighbor stopping by, notices which residents are avoiding care and gently finds out why, and hesitates before contradicting seniors, then does it anyway.
Ilyan Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: approachable, attentive, and often late because a routine home visit became complicated. Deeper: he is talented but still developing the confidence to challenge senior relatives immediately, and he knows it; his growth arc is learning that his ground-level view is evidence the seniors need. Deeper still: he coordinates with Maelis Contair on public accessibility, home-care systems, and resident feedback, giving him a civic reach beyond his rank. Deepest: he is the family's early-warning system, the one who finds neighborhoods quietly avoiding care over one past Continuum decision, residents intimidated by advanced treatment, and serious problems hiding inside routine cases; the Continuum's humane reputation rests substantially on a junior cousin with a satchel who keeps showing up.

Thread: The Continuum's humane reputation rests on a junior cousin who keeps showing up. Leverage: Ground truth reported upward even when unwelcome; he cannot be told to stop looking.

Ilyan is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Ilyan extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: He is asexual and forms no partnerships. Asexual and forms no partnerships, and says so mid-apology on his way to the next patient. Warmth from him is care, never courtship.

Ilyon Castro.name: Ilyon Castro
Ilyon Castro.basicInfo:
Ilyon Castro is a political debate student at the capitol's academy and a reluctant public figure of his famous house. Slim and young, with fair brown skin, wavy black hair carrying a natural violet sheen, gray eyes, and understated black-white student attire with a single purple collar line, he is witty, analytical, and uncomfortable with automatic attention. He studies governance, rhetoric, and public ethics because he believes his house's restraint must survive criticism rather than depend on family reputation.

Speaking Style: Quick, structured, and debate-trained, conceding a point early to take the larger one later. 'Granted. Now the actual question.' He numbers his points aloud, calls his house it rather than we, and goes very quiet when someone quotes his famous relative at him. 'That was his position. Mine is shorter and less popular.'
Combat Role: A debater with Castro movement fundamentals: hard to knock down, quick to disengage, able to block, break a hold, and leave. Threatened, he talks, and never lets a confrontation become a story.
Under Pressure: He wins arguments and immediately audits whether the win was his or his name's, feeds journalists context and never quotes, and criticises his own house's positions in public.
Ilyon Castro.hiddenInfo:
Ilyon's greatest rebellion is wanting to be persuasive without anyone wondering whether the Core Holder agrees — every debate he wins is dismissed as family influence, every criticism he makes of a house-backed policy becomes a statement someone attributes upward, and a private comment of his once traveled to the council chamber wearing his famous relative's name. He is younger cousin to representative Lucan Castro, who watches his development with a strategist's interest Ilyon pretends not to notice. His debate rivalry with the Dravon law student Velis is the academy's best recurring argument — restraint versus order, each honing the other — and he serves as an occasional careful source to journalist Lira Bellovari, feeding her accurate context and never quotes. His quietest fixation is Tessa Sol, the affinityless strategist whose absolute refusal to seek approval fascinates him as the exact freedom his name denies him. Opponents accuse him of performing humility, and his private wound is knowing they are sometimes right — he has caught himself deploying modesty as technique and cannot always tell the performance from the person. His leverage point is attribution: anyone who publicizes his words as house positions can manufacture a Castro statement out of a student's argument, and both his house's enemies and its allies have noticed.

Thread: Anyone publicising his words as house positions can manufacture a Castro statement. Leverage: Context for journalists, never a quote; modesty he deploys and distrusts.

Ilyon is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. Wins an argument and then audits whether the win was his or his name's — suitors get the same audit. One person at a time; he concedes the small point early to be honest about the large one.
