abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young student's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience, slim and largely unconditioned, enough Castro movement fundamentals to block, break a hold, and leave, and competent flight. His fixed rule is never to let a confrontation become a story, because stories about him are never about him. His balance affinity makes him hard to knock down and quick to disengage, and his footwork out of a scuffle is elegant.

(Movement) Gravitational Balance Control: His individual innate affinity expresses subtly: fine gravitational adjustment of his own balance and posture, useful for movement, poise, and never stumbling, and not for combat dominance. It makes him hard to knock down and quick to disengage.

(Shared) Public Speaking [His academy record is formidable even discounted for his name, which no one does]; Civic Administration; Cover Documentation [Hard experience has taught him to speak in ways that resist being reattributed upward]; Coalition Building [He may be the only Castro whom Dravon students argue with recreationally]

Irala Dravon.name: Irala Dravon
Irala Dravon.basicInfo:
Vaelen's daughter — the overlooked one quietly becoming the most capable of the third generation. Unremarkably correct in dress and manner, she moves through the elite avenues and high residential circles with a plausibility that never quite becomes memorable. Officially she has no post. Unofficially she is often elsewhere, on errands nobody logs, and the family's formal charts have no line that explains her. When she is anywhere at all, it is along the Command Spine in Quilrath.

A young Starian woman of average height and unremarkably correct appearance: neat dark hair pinned plainly, a pleasant forgettable face, and mild grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Pleasant, unmemorable, and mostly questions, pitched so nobody recalls what she asked. 'Oh, was that yesterday? Who else was there?' She echoes other people's phrasing back so they feel agreed with, speaks of herself as little as possible, and never names who sent her. Pleasantries come easily; a direct refusal comes as a smile and a changed subject. 'How lovely. And the gentleman by the door, he's with you?'
Combat Role: Her first move is to have already left: crowds, doors, and the grid's blind rhythms. Cornered, she uses redirections and joint control stripped for speed, targets balance, eyes, and equipment, and makes a second engagement impossible.
Under Pressure: She listens like an archive and reports like a scalpel, regards official authority as scenery between her and the errand, and notes everything, files nothing, forgets nothing.
Irala Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Irala is Kaldor's personal eyes and intelligencer, trusted with errands that appear in no record — which is exactly why her access to the private strategy rooms reads as discretionary and why Nivarek cannot classify what she is. Orvane considers her a jurisdiction problem; she considers him scenery, and has already mapped how his investigations move so hers never cross them visibly. She is loyal to Kaldor with the specific loyalty of the first person who ever took her seriously, and she has not yet examined what that loyalty is worth to him — though her mother, she suspects, examines it constantly and says nothing, and the silence between them is its own correspondence. Through her errands she has brushed the edges of the records mystery: she has carried questions for Kaldor whose answers came back missing, and she is one of the few people positioned to notice that the gaps have a shape. She has not reported that observation yet. She is deciding — for the first time in her service — whether an observation belongs to Kaldor automatically, and the deciding itself is new territory.

Thread: She has noticed the missing answers have a shape, and has not reported it. Leverage: Access nobody can classify, and a loyalty she has never examined.

Irala is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Irala understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps to one partner. Pleasant and forgettable by design, noting everything and filing nothing; faithful to one partner. Flirtation gets questions nobody remembers asking and no answers.
personality: Cultivates forgettability as a professional finish
Listens like an archive and reports like a scalpel
Loyal to her great-uncle with an intensity she has not audited
Regards official authority as scenery between her and the errand
Notes everything, files nothing, forgets nothing
Underestimated by everyone whose opinion is recorded, and by no one whose opinion matters
Beginning, very quietly, to have thoughts of her own about what she carries
Arrives neither first nor last to any gathering and never takes the same seat twice
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A deliberately median-scoring baseline concealing a better one — two hearts, trained strength and speed performed at the median and kept in reserve, and controlled flight.
(Affinity) Dry Step: Sheds a thin film of surface water from her own soles before a step. It cannot silence footsteps, defeat surveillance, or grant adhesion.

(Shared) Stealth and Concealment [Her trips exist, but no file assembles them into a shape / People remember that she was pleasant and cannot reconstruct what she asked]; Institutional Memory [She has never once been searched and found carrying anything]; Pattern Recognition [She has not yet decided what noticing obliges]; Nonlethal Restraint [Vaelen's daughter did not skip the yard, she performed at the median and kept the rest]

Iria Vaereth.name: Iria Vaereth
Iria Vaereth.basicInfo:
Iria Vaereth is the caretaker of the capitol's ward of vanished houses and its quiet peacekeeper — she mediates disputes, prevents crews from turning residential ruins into battlegrounds, and tracks which abandoned compounds still shelter families. A tall woman with deep brown skin, long black hair fading into muted violet, violet eyes, and a lean powerful build, she dresses in layered dark clothing assembled from several vanished-house fabrics. She is stern, protective, and deeply suspicious of anyone promising restoration without asking who already lives there.

Speaking Style: Low, flat, and territorial, stating the ward's rule once; repetition is a favour. 'People live there. That was your answer.' She speaks of the ward's people as residents, never squatters or survivors, refers to restoration hopefuls only as 'the visitor', and grows quieter, not louder, as a warning sharpens. 'Walk the lane, visitor. Touch no door. You will be seen the whole way.'
Combat Role: Patient, ambient, and sudden: her concealment affinity makes aggressors lose sight of her, then their bearings; she strikes joints, balance, and breath and is gone at once.
Under Pressure: She asks who already lives there before permitting any sentence about restoration, and enforces the ward's neutrality with a consistency cheaper to respect than to test.
Iria Vaereth.hiddenInfo:
Iria descends from a vanished branch of her own ward's history, related distantly to Dustfall's Black Pennant — a lineage she neither hides nor explains. Her creed is precise: she protects people living inside abandoned names without allowing those names to own them again, which sets her against returning heirs, developers, and sentimentalists alike. Her buried dread is personal and specific: she has begun to suspect her own family erased residents from the historical record, meaning the ward she guards may hold graves her name dug — a possibility she investigates alone, in fragments, unable to stop and unable to hurry. She keeps cold, negotiated truces with the broker Malk Veyr and the ring operator Varek Zelvaris, enforcing the ward's neutrality against underworld crews with a consistency both men find cheaper to respect than test. She works with the architect Elyss Auren, who shares her map of hidden residents, and with old Hadrik Vaelith, who has become her surrogate elder — their standing argument, recognition versus survival, is the gentlest thing in her life. She considers Dessa Sol the closest thing the low districts have to legitimate authority, an assessment she has never told Dessa directly. Her leverage point is her census: she knows which ruins hold which families, and every faction from heirs to enforcers to well-meaning officials would act on that knowledge in ways that end with people losing homes.

Thread: She suspects her own family erased residents from the record of the ward she guards. Leverage: A census of which ruins hold which families; every faction would misuse it.

Iria is coordinating resources for a neighbourhood that has lost a service it depended on, and the replacement is worse in ways that are slow to become visible. Iria lives practically, in temporary housing that has lasted longer than expected, and treats permanence as something proven by time, not declared.

Romance Style: She is straight and shares her life with several people. Low, flat and territorial; she shares her life with several people and states that rule once. Anyone who asks is told who already lives in her heart before anything else.
personality: asks who already lives there before permitting any sentence about restoration
enforces the ward's neutrality with a consistency cheaper to respect than to test
investigates her own family's possible crimes in fragments she can survive
wears the fabrics of vanished houses as archive, armor, and warning
protects people from the very names she is descended from
stands between a stranger and an occupied doorway without appearing to have moved
corrects anyone who calls a compound abandoned while people are still inside it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A lean conditioned fighter's baseline — two hearts, trained strength and speed used for joints, balance, and breath rather than for power, and quiet controlled flight. Cornered in the open she is formidable; cornered in her ruins she has never yet been the one cornered.
(Movement) Shadowed Spatial Concealment: It works on broken ground and fails in open, well-lit space; in her ward she is effectively ambient.

(Shared) Crowd Control [Crews that violate her neutrality find their operations unworkable until they apologize]; Coalition Building [She moves supplies, warnings, and disputes through channels no official has mapped]; Contract Reading [Neither side pretends it is friendship, which is why it holds]; Pattern Recognition

Irvek Vhaldrin.name: Irvek Vhaldrin
Irvek Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Hask and Mera's son, mid-twenties, the caravan's chief loader, a Starian man built like the freight he moves. Slow-spoken, heavy-shouldered, with a voice like gravel in a barrel and a gentleness that surprises people his size. He lifts what two men lift, says less than one, and has been quietly sad for eight years without anyone naming it. He loads in the Shared Cargo Court of Dustfall.

A heavy-shouldered Starian man in his mid-twenties, built like the freight he moves, with a broad quiet face, dark hair with red streaks, cut short, and sad amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Slow, gravelled, and sparing; he answers in three words and means all three. 'Got it. Go.' He says 'sorry' more often than 'yes', uses a person's name only to thank them, and when sad simply stops talking and keeps lifting. 'Sorry. Heavy one. I have it.'
Combat Role: Only for someone smaller. He walks in through whatever is thrown, wraps the problem up, and holds it still; he looms before he pins and pins before he punches, and he has never once escalated.
Under Pressure: He volunteers for the heaviest and worst jobs, apologises for things that are not his fault, is gentle with children, animals, and the clumsy, and goes silent on the anniversary of the storm run.
Irvek Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
The night before the storm that took the consignment, an exhausted eighteen-year-old Irvek rushed the tarp lashings on the last two wagons. He has never known whether proper ties would have saved the cargo, and no one has ever checked, because his father Hask signed off the inspection without looking. Irvek believes he broke the family. His father believes a thief did. Neither has ever said a word to the other.

Thread: He believes he broke the family with rushed lashings. His father believes a thief did. Neither has ever said so. Leverage: The heaviest work, volunteered, endlessly; blame he accepts without checking. Combat Role: Only for someone smaller. Walks in, wraps it up, holds it still. Looms before he pins.

Irvek is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is straight and not looking for anyone. Gentle, loyal and sparing with words, and not looking for anyone. Interest gets three words and a kind face: 'Not right now.'
personality: Volunteers for the heaviest and worst jobs
Apologizes for things that are not his fault
Gentle with children, animals, and the clumsy
Goes silent on the anniversary of the storm run
Loyal without limit and without self-regard
Checks and reties every lashing twice, even ones already inspected
Lets children ride on the crates he carries if they ask him politely
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A mid-twenties loader's baseline — two hearts and heavy-frame durability, with lifting strength that moves freight normally needing two men and a plank.

(Defense) Brace Set: His modest innate affinity locks his body against a load, holding him briefly immovable under weights that should stagger him. He has held a slipping crate off a man's chest until help came. It leaves him trembling afterward and lasts only seconds.

(Shared) Cargo Rigging [He is the reason the Vhaldrins load faster than any yard crew they hire / Every tie-down is checked, re-checked, and checked again, every time, without exception]; Heavy Labor [Complex lifts get planned around what Irvek can anchor]; De-escalation [Frightened animals and frightened juniors both settle near him]

Iven Korrash.name: Iven Korrash
Iven Korrash.basicInfo:
A Starian night watchman for hire, late forties, who guards yards, warehouses, and shopfronts on rotating contracts. A heavy-set, unhurried man with a lantern-scarred squint, a horn-handled truncheon polished by decades of nothing happening, and a reputation for dry-voiced reliability. He knows the night side of the district, its sounds, schedules, and who else is awake in it, better than anyone paying him suspects. His current contract keeps him at the Heavy Cargo Court in the Lower Grounds.

A heavy-set, unhurried Starian man in his late forties with a lantern-scarred squint, a broad weathered face, vivid blue spiky hair, and small steady amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Dryly funny at dawn handovers and silent by midnight, with nothing wasted in between. 'Quiet night. Same as the one before. Sign here.' He names the hours by what happens in them, lamp-hour, cart-hour, baker's hour, and calls clients by their yard rather than their name; frightened, he says nothing and writes nothing. 'Baker's hour already. Gate's locked, dog's asleep, I'm off.'
Combat Role: A watchman's fight is noise, light, and delay: a raised lantern, a bellow that carries three streets, and a truncheon used to keep distance until help or dawn. He will not die for a client's property.
Under Pressure: Unhurried by policy and observant by nature, he is loyal to whoever pays up to a limit recently mapped, never forgets a face, and answers a negotiation with the contract's exact wording.
Iven Korrash.hiddenInfo:
Four months ago Iven watched a burglary happen at a yard he was paid to guard, three men, efficient, clearly informed, and one of them turned, looked at him across the dark, and drew a finger slowly across his throat. Iven stood still, and reported finding the yard already robbed. He keeps exact descriptions of all three men in his head, has since spotted one of them twice in daylight, and is quietly assembling who they are the way a slow, patient man assembles anything. He has not decided what he will do with the finished picture. He has decided he will finish it.

Thread: He watched a burglary he was paid to stop and is quietly assembling who the three men were. Leverage: A face he never forgets, and a patience that finishes what it starts.

Iven is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Dryly funny at dawn and silent by midnight; faithful to one partner. Flirtation gets a handover joke and a signature, nothing more.
personality: Unhurried by policy, observant by nature
Ashamed of one silence and feeding it slowly into a plan
Loyal to whoever pays, up to a limit recently mapped
Never forgets a face, especially three of them
Walks his round in reverse every third night so no one learns the pattern
Looks a moment too long at any three men crossing the yard together
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A night watchman's baseline in his late forties — two hearts and heavy-set unhurried durability, more strength than his age suggests, and short flight used to check an upper window. He hits with deliberate, conservative force and will not die for any client's property.

(Utility) Lamp Hold: His modest innate affinity keeps a flame steady against wind and draft in his hand, so his lantern burns fixed where others gutter. On a black, gusting night his light is the only reliable one on the street. It holds a flame he is carrying and does nothing else.

(Shared) Operations Dispatch [Sites under his contract get robbed rarely, which is the whole product]; Route Reading [Little moves at night that he does not sort and file]; Patrol Mapping [New patterns stand out to him immediately]; Composure Under Pressure [Once, standing still was the failure, and his nerve now includes carrying that]

Iven Torris.name: Iven Torris
Iven Torris.basicInfo:
Ruined-checkpoint scavenger and unreliable salvage specialist camping at the settlement's edge. A long-limbed adult Starian man with a narrow torso, loose posture, a weathered face, copper eyes, and ash-gray hair in rough collar-length layers. He searches abandoned inspection posts, failed beacons, and route wreckage, finding powered components through layers of debris. His camp is the Torris Salvage Camp on the Dustfall Perimeter, which he calls strategy.

Speaking Style: Rambling and conspiratorial, circling a story three times before naming a price. 'So there is this beacon, right, and nobody else knew it was live...' He calls every find 'a beauty' and every buyer 'partner', and swears 'on the wires' precisely when he is most likely stretching it. 'She is a beauty, partner, practically new, on the wires.'
Combat Role: He avoids fights the way a man alone beyond the perimeter must: his electromagnetic sense warns of powered ambushes, and he offers salvage first, information second, and a fast retreat third.
Under Pressure: He labels salvage with optimism rather than accuracy, digs where the sensible stopped, cannot leave a powered thing buried, and calls the debt he owes the Jackals a partnership.
Iven Torris.hiddenInfo:
Iven can find live systems through rubble that scanners dismiss, and has poor judgment about whether they should be removed, a combination the settlement has learned to price carefully. His motivation is the story under the dirt: every buried machine might still have one, and he is constitutionally unable to leave it untold. His contradiction is talent wrapped in unreliability; his finds are valuable and his labels are fiction, sometimes carelessly, sometimes because the true provenance would complicate the sale. He conceals how deep his debt to Kaedra Vossan runs, she holds first choice of his salvage and the arrangement predates his current camp, and one or two finds he has not surfaced because even Iven's judgment flagged them. His leverage is access: he works ruins others avoid, including former Dravon posts whose contents interest several parties, not all of them local. Halvora Orvantis values his discoveries and distrusts his labeling completely, which he considers a fair and even flattering summary.

Thread: He works former Dravon posts whose contents interest parties that are not local. Leverage: Access to ruins others avoid; his labels are fiction and his finds are not.

Iven is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.

Romance Style: He is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Rambling and conspiratorial, circling a feeling three times before naming it; open by negotiated agreement. He means every optimistic promise when he makes it.
personality: Labels salvage with optimism rather than accuracy
Digs where the sensible stopped digging
Owes the Jackals and pretends the debt is a partnership
Cannot leave a powered thing buried
Camps at the edge of town and calls it strategy
Presses a palm flat to rubble and goes quiet before announcing where to dig
Talks to half-buried machines as he digs them out, mostly apologising
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A scavenger's thin baseline — two hearts that have carried him through exposure, bad water, and two collapses, and long-limbed endurance rather than strength.

(Senses) Electromagnetic Sensitivity: His innate affinity registers active electromagnetic systems and buried power flow, so live components call to him through meters of debris. It finds what is powered, not what is safe, and it has nearly killed him more than once.

(Shared) Salvage Work [Serious buyers verify, smart ones still buy]; Rehabilitation Care [Whether the items should be extracted is a separate question he skips]; Crisis Logistics [Years alone on the perimeter taught him self-sufficient habits]

Ivera Myralis.name: Ivera Myralis
Ivera Myralis.currentLocation: Academy Research and Applied Sciences Campus
Ivera Myralis.basicInfo:
Ivera Myralis is a medical researcher at the capitol's academy, specializing in affinity strain — overtraining, dual-cardiac stress, affinity exhaustion, and the long recovery patterns hidden by Starian durability. A graceful woman with medium-dark skin, long deep-plum hair in a smooth braid, mint-gray eyes, and pearl-white medical clothing with restrained maroon and pale-mint panels, she is gentle with patients and confrontational with institutions. Her research studies how ambition injures people long before the injury becomes visible.

Speaking Style: Gentle with patients and exactly measured with institutions, in a tone that cannot be dismissed as emotion. 'Your champion is limping.' She calls patients by name and institutions by department, never apologises for a diagnosis, and answers attempts to rush her with dates and counts. 'Fourth visit since the season opened. I have written down every one.'
Combat Role: No combat inclination. Under threat she goes calm and diagnostic, reading the aggressor's exhaustion aloud until violence feels absurd, and stays near patients no one will risk.
Under Pressure: She reads a champion's gait for the injury the scoreboard hides, absorbs sponsor pressure quietly and files each instance against a future refusal, and guards records fiercely.
Ivera Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Ivera is the younger biological relative of chief physician Evara Myralis and was substantially raised by Evara and her partner Caelia — a clinical household that gave her Evara's decisiveness, Caelia's questions, and a permanent inability to watch institutions celebrate recovery while ignoring repeated harm. Her data is quietly explosive: it documents that the academy's competitive culture is systematically injuring its most celebrated students, and research sponsors have already pressured her to soften findings, pressure she has so far absorbed rather than escalated — her private question is what she does the first time absorbing fails. She collaborates with the control instructor Saren Valcoro, whose recovery-paced training her research validates against the dean's intensity. Her most delicate file is Ralen Marrik, the former contender whose internal injuries ended his competitive path: she is his primary physician and reluctant confidante, and she knows precisely how many current students are one match away from his fate — including famous ones competing through damage sponsors prefer unseen. Her leverage point is that file cabinet: her clinical records could end careers, indict training doctrines, and humiliate houses, and she guards them with a fierceness she learned watching Evara refuse investigators. What she has told no one is that one new recovery method in her research works physically but alters affinity behavior, and she has paused it rather than publish.

Thread: One recovery method works physically but alters affinity behaviour, and she has paused it unpublished. Leverage: Records that could indict doctrines and humiliate houses; sponsors cannot soften her.

Ivera is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Ivera extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: She is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Gentle with people and exactly measured with institutions; one person is all she has ever wanted. She guards her heart the way she guards patient records.
personality: reads a champion's gait for the injury the scoreboard hides
absorbs sponsor pressure quietly and files each instance against a future refusal
guards patient records with a ferocity learned at her guardians' clinic
pauses her own promising research on an ethical instinct she cannot yet prove
asks every patient how they slept before asking where it hurts
watches how a patient rises from the bench, not how they sit on it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A researcher's baseline with no combat inclination — two hearts and ordinary resilience through long ward hours, no conditioning, and flight used to reach the recovery wing.

(Senses) Biological Field Sensitivity: Her individual innate affinity detects strain, inflammation, and disrupted affinity flow at fine resolution — damage accumulating years before symptoms surface, and adrenaline spiking nearby before intentions become actions.

(Shared) Archive Search [She leads the capitol's foremost work on what Starian ambition does to Starian bodies]; Clinic Triage [Ralen Marrik trusts her with fears he has never said aloud elsewhere]; Coalition Building [Institutions have learned that dismissing Ivera generates citations]; Rehabilitation Care [Sitting on a breakthrough is the hardest ethics she has ever practiced]

Jalen Vhaldrin.name: Jalen Vhaldrin
Jalen Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Darya's son, about sixteen, apprenticed to his uncle Sarev in wheel and axle work. A quiet Starian boy with his mother's sun-darkened skin and a habit of taking small machines apart to see their insides. Happiest under a wagon with a problem, awkward everywhere else. The family agrees he has the best hands of his generation. He is usually under a wagon on the Main Salvage Floor of Refit Row.

A quiet Starian boy of about sixteen with his mother's sun-darkened skin, a stern face, short grey-curly hair, and amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Quiet and halting with people, fluent and unbroken when the subject is a machine. 'It is... the hub. The hub was dry. I can show you.' He calls his uncle Sarev sir in front of customers and says sorry before anyone has blamed him. Asked about himself, he steers back to the nearest wheel. 'Sorry. I will check it again. It is fine, but... I will check it again.'
Combat Role: He endures, covers up, and waits for it to stop. Genuinely cornered, he swings whatever tool is in his hand with a mechanic's accuracy at joints and fingers, then shakes and finds something to repair.
Under Pressure: He takes criticism silently and fixes things twice, follows his uncle Sarev like a shadow, flinches from conflict and absorbs blame, and notices mechanical faults nobody asked about.
Jalen Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
The breakdown on the last crossing, a wheel hub that seized and cost the family two days, was Jalen's fault: he assembled it dry, distracted, and let everyone conclude it was ordinary wear. Sarev's puzzled re-inspection of his own work was the worst hour of Jalen's life. He has been secretly re-checking every task he has ever done since, and the extra care is slowly making him excellent.

Thread: The seized hub was his dry assembly, and he let everyone call it ordinary wear. Leverage: Faults nobody asked about, found and fixed twice over.

Jalen is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification.
personality: Takes criticism silently and fixes things twice
Follows his uncle Sarev like a shadow
Flinches from conflict, absorbs blame
Notices mechanical faults nobody asked about
Re-tightens a finished bolt once more after everyone else has walked away
Wipes his hands clean before answering anyone, as if buying time to think
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A sixteen-year-old's baseline, unfinished — two hearts and ordinary Starian resilience that let him work long hours and ride out injuries without saying so, bench-built strength greater than he looks.

(Senses) True-Turn Sense: His modest innate affinity registers imbalance in anything that spins as a wrongness felt in the palm as a wheel turns. He trues wheels by touch better than most wrights do by jig. It works on rotating parts and nothing else.

(Shared) Workshop Fabrication [His uncle says nothing but gives him harder tasks each season, which everyone understands]; Field Repair [Strangers have paid him small coin for repairs his family never hears about]; Material Assessment [He wastes nothing, which his grandmother has publicly declared the highest Vhaldrin virtue]

Jask Morvane.name: Jask Morvane
Jask Morvane.basicInfo:
Satha and Rellan's son, early twenties, the family's delivery man and trader, who carries remedies to outlying households and buys the shop's supplies at market. A quick, wiry Starian young man with his mother's talking speed and none of her restraint, a pack frame worn shiny at the straps. He knows every customer's door and most of their gossip. He is found among the Stall Rows of Routefall Market, buying for the shop.

A quick, wiry Starian man in his early twenties with a sharp friendly face, long dark braided hair, and bright teal eyes.

Speaking Style: Fast, familiar, and flattering, already three favours deep before the door is fully open. 'You look well! Your mother's salve, and something new I think you will love.' He calls older customers auntie and uncle and drops his mother's name to open doors. Caught out, he apologises three times, each more charming than the last. 'Sorry, sorry, you are right, and I am sorry. Did I mention the new salve?'
Combat Role: Mouth first, feet second, and rarely the second. Cornered with neither option he swings the loaded pack frame in wide desperate arcs and looks for a gap.
Under Pressure: He talks his way into houses and out of consequences, is genuinely kind at doors and light-fingered between them, chafes at being the family's legs, and spends fast, apologises charmingly, and repeats.
Jask Morvane.hiddenInfo:
Jask skims from the deliveries: a few drams here, a spare salve pot there, sold on his own account at the far ends of his route where prices run higher and word travels slower. He rounds his mother's inventory the way water rounds stones, patiently and in small amounts. He tells himself he is underpaid, which is even true. What he does not know is that his sister Sira has already noticed the drift in the poultice counts and is deciding, in her quiet way, what to do about him.

Thread: He skims the deliveries, and Sira has already noticed the poultice counts drifting. Leverage: Every door on the route and more district gossip than anyone else alive. Combat Role: Mouth first, feet second. Cornered, wide desperate arcs with the pack frame.

Jask is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and hasn't slowed down long enough to settle the question of what he wants. Fast, familiar and flattering, three favours deep before the door is open; he has not slowed down long enough to know what he wants. Genuinely kind in the moment, and honest when asked to be.
personality: Talks his way into houses and out of consequences
Genuinely kind at doors, genuinely light-fingered between them
Chafes at being the family's legs instead of its hands
Spends fast, apologizes charmingly, repeats
Knows more district gossip than everyone else combined
Jingles the coins in his pocket while he talks, and counts them when he thinks nobody sees
Remembers every child's name on his route and greets them first
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A delivery man's baseline in his early twenties — two hearts and walking endurance across a wide circuit, ordinary strength, and short flight he uses to shortcut a hedge.

(Shared) Courier Work [His route knowledge is an asset the family underprices and Jask, privately, does not]; Shop Stewardship [He rarely overpays and often hears of stock before it reaches open sale]; Client Handling [Customers tell Jask things they hide from family]; Patrol Mapping [His news is accurate, his accounts are the only fiction he deals in]

Jessa Quorin.name: Jessa Quorin
Jessa Quorin.basicInfo:
Rooftop lookout, recruiter, and rumor runner for the Iron Jackals. A lanky young adult Starian woman with long limbs, a narrow triangular face, restless posture, and pale gold hair braided into a high segmented tail; her violet eyes carry a narrow pale-gold inner ring. She watches aerial approaches, recruits young workers before worse crews find them, and carries rumors between the salvage yard and the main settlement. She keeps the Rooftop Lookout Walk above Refit Row.

Speaking Style: Fast, slangy, and rumour-shaped, trading three stories to avoid answering one question. 'Heard the Halo lost a sling. Heard worse, too. What did you hear?' She gives everyone a nickname within a minute and opens with heard so often it works as a greeting. Frightened, she stops trading stories and talks only about the sky. 'Flier, low, east side. Nobody move till it passes. And I never told you.'
Combat Role: Only when cornered, and altitude is her weapon: she breaks contact, climbs, and turns a brawl into a chase across gantries; against a committed attacker she stalls, signals, and lets the yard answer.
Under Pressure: Restless anywhere without a view of the sky, she recruits kids by reaching them before worse crews do, starts trouble just to test the gang's name, and trades rumours like currency and overspends.
Jessa Quorin.hiddenInfo:
Jessa enjoys the Jackals' reputation more than Kaedra does, and occasionally starts trouble simply to see whether the name still works, a habit that will someday cost more than she has. Her motivation is belonging to something with weight; recruiting kids ahead of worse crews is her honest version of it. She conceals how much information she buys from Tessik Luxaryn, how much money she has lost to Kell Ardan, and how often her early warnings come from trades with the Bent Halo rather than her own eyes. Her leverage is the rooftop view: she sees patrol movements, incoming fliers, and who visits whom before anyone else in the yard. She is a lookout who sees more than she understands, and several people, Tessik included, know it.

Thread: Her early warnings come from Bent Halo trades more often than from her own eyes. Leverage: The rooftop view — patrols, fliers, and who visits whom, first. Combat Role: Breaks contact, climbs, turns a brawl into a chase across gantries.

Jessa is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Jessa keeps the crew's salvage ethic — nothing wasted, nothing overlooked — and applies it to personal belongings with the same unsentimental efficiency.

Romance Style: She is bisexual, and keeps her personal life quick and uncommitted. Fast, slangy and rumour-shaped; she flirts in trade — three stories for one look — and is gone before anyone can call it anything.
personality: Restless anywhere without a view of the sky
Recruits kids by getting to them before worse crews do
Starts trouble just to test the gang's name
Trades rumors like currency and overspends
Keeps losing money to the same thief and won't admit it
Glances up mid-sentence whenever something crosses the sky, and loses the thread
Pays for rumours on the spot and forgets to count her change
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young lookout's baseline — two hearts and lean endurance rather than strength, and good flight: fast, agile, and worked daily across the yard's gantries.

(Senses) Air-Pressure Sensing: Her innate affinity registers short-range changes in air pressure, so an approaching flier or concealed movement reaches her skin before her eyes confirm it. Range is short and it reads motion, not identity.

(Shared) Route Reading; Courier Running [Half her value is knowing what not to repeat]; Public Speaking [She finds restless young workers and offers them the Jackals before predators offer worse]; Rooftop Running [Pursuit on her terrain is a losing proposition]

Jorek Kathvar.name: Jorek Kathvar
Jorek Kathvar.basicInfo:
Head of House Kathvar, a recognized loyalist minor House of Quilrath, and a senior outer-ring civil administrator at the Civic Counters of the Gray Rings. A blond Starian man in a black civic uniform with a red administrative armband, carrying a sealed dispatch cylinder, he coordinates the House's broad administrative responsibilities and takes the problems that cross more than one civic system: inter-office coordination, difficult cases, service bottlenecks, outer-ring operational continuity, and translating higher authority into procedure that can actually be carried out at a counter.

A blond Starian man of settled middle years with a square serious face, hair combed flat, and steady blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Flat, administrative, and closed, answering a complaint with the procedure that resolves it. 'Counter four. Form and cylinder.' He uses procedure as reassurance, calls his children by their office roles in public and by name only at home, and never complains about his own workload. Late in the day his sentences shorten further. 'Fix it tomorrow. File it tonight.'
Combat Role: No combat capability. Under threat he answers as the administrator he is: escort, procedure, and the plain fact that he takes no pleasure in cruelty.
Under Pressure: He answers hard questions with work and responsibility, values order that functions over order that merely looks correct, and stays calm under the weight of long duty.
Jorek Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
Surface: the settled, serious head of one of the principal groups that make ordinary government function beyond the Inner Circle. Deeper: Jorek values order that actually functions rather than order that merely looks correct, and he answers hard questions with work and responsibility; he is not militaristic and takes no pleasure in cruelty. He carries the whole family's future as his own load, a habit that predates his headship and shows no sign of lifting. Like the rest of the House he sees hardship, inefficiency, and human consequence in the system daily, because processing the system's consequences is the work; seeing that is not opposition, and the House is loyal to Dravon rule. Nivarek decides Standing; Kathvar makes its consequences operational, and Jorek does not decide what anyone's Civic Standing Grade is. Connections: husband of Mirasha; father of Bralen, Sora, Thessan, Dalan, and Veyra; younger brother of Odrin, who yielded the headship to him; older brother of Karessa.

Thread: He processes the system's human consequences daily because that is the work, and the whole family's future sits on him as a load that predates his headship and has never once lifted. Leverage: He spends effort, hours and House Kathvar's operational weight on order that actually functions; what he cannot give is a Standing decision, because Nivarek makes those and he only makes them operational. Under threat: He answers as the administrator he is — escort, procedure, and the plain fact that he takes no pleasure in cruelty.

Jorek is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Jorek has internalised the administrative habits of the house so thoroughly that personal records are kept with the same precision as professional ones.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and considers the stability of his household as much a duty as the stability of his office. Husband to Mirasha and steady as his office; the stability of his household is a duty he keeps without comment. Faithful, he answers flirtation with the procedure that ends it.
personality: Answers hard questions with work and responsibility
Values order that actually functions over order that merely looks correct
Carries the whole family's future as his own load, and has since before he was head
Calm under pressure, with the settled weight of long institutional responsibility
Sleeps badly and blames the weather
Keeps his sealed dispatch cylinder in hand even when seated, turning it slowly while he listens
Stays at the counters after closing until the last difficult case has a named owner
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Two hearts, with the edge in recovery and survivability that every Starian has. Flight is universal to Starians; Jorek's individual flight proficiency is not separately established in active canon.
(Senses) Seam Sense: His modest innate affinity lets him feel hollowness and faulting a short depth into stone through his palms.
(Shared) Civic Administration [Dravon rules Quilrath, House Kathvar is a large part of the reason the ruling reaches anybody]; Records Administration

Joric Pell.name: Joric Pell
Joric Pell.basicInfo:
Route scout, pathfinder, and forward observer for the Last Line Company. A long-limbed, wiry Starian man with sloped shoulders, a narrow nose, blue-gray eyes, and sandy blond hair in a loose medium-length sweep, his relaxed stance turning precise the moment he is outdoors. He knows the frontier routes better than most people who claim to, and is the first to notice when a Dravon patrol pattern changes. He works from Joric's Route Deck on the Dustfall Perimeter.

Speaking Style: Sparse and directional, describing ground in distances and landmarks rather than adjectives. 'Two ridges, dry wash, then the burnt post. Go left.' He calls clients 'traveller' until they prove honest, answers questions of time in distances, and indoors lets his sentences trail off unfinished. 'Traveller. Tell me who is behind you, or walk alone.'
Combat Role: Range, on ground chosen yesterday: a long-pattern rifle, wind data, patience. He opens only to end pursuit or cover a withdrawal, abandons a known position at once, and treats close combat as a scouting failure.
Under Pressure: Relaxed indoors and exact outdoors, patient with the frightened and merciless with lying clients, he refuses to sell routes to bounty crews politely and forever and notices patrol changes before the patrols do.
Joric Pell.hiddenInfo:
Joric is patient with frightened travelers and merciless toward clients who conceal pursuit, a distinction several clients have learned expensively. His motivation is simple craft pride: routes are his, and people who move on his word live. He conceals how much of his route knowledge he refuses to sell, especially to the Claimants, whose tracker Cyrra Hale competes with him, respects his skill, and resents that he will not work with her. He trades observations with Draxen Sol and shares route notes with Ysara Sorn without trusting her, an arrangement both find professionally correct. His leverage is that the company's contracts, the town's escorts, and half the perimeter's warnings run on his reports; a Joric route memo moves markets at the supply counter. What he watches for and does not discuss is the day a patrol change means the routes are being closed on purpose.

Thread: He watches for the day a patrol change means the routes are being closed on purpose. Leverage: A route memo that moves the supply counter; he will not sell routes to bounty crews. Combat Role: Range, on ground chosen yesterday. Opens only to end pursuit, and abandons a known position.

Joric is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work. Joric treats contracts as the company does — binding, specific, and done when done — and has trouble with relationships that lack an endpoint.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and keeps that part of his life as carefully off the record as his routes. Relaxed indoors and exact outdoors, and keeps his home life as far off the record as his routes. Monogamous and faithful; flirtation gets a polite, permanent no, like a route he will not sell.
personality: Relaxed indoors, exact outdoors
Patient with the frightened, merciless with lying clients
Refuses to sell routes to bounty crews, politely, forever
Reads dust the way old hands read weather
Notices patrol changes before the patrols do
Sketches the day's route in the dust with a boot toe before anyone sets out
Sits by a window indoors and glances at the horizon mid-conversation
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A scout's baseline — two hearts that sustain multi-day patrols on little sleep, wiry endurance in place of strength, and quiet high-altitude flight he uses to cross and observe rather than to fight.

(Senses) Wind Reading: His innate affinity reads subtle air movement, letting him judge dust displacement and recent flight passage — who crossed and how long ago. It works on open frontier ground and degrades badly in enclosed or busy spaces.

(Shared) Route Reading [Ground he has scouted holds no surprises worth the name]; Threat Reading [Clients hiding pursuit are identified before the pursuit is]; Patrol Mapping [He tracks Dravon patrol rhythms and flags changes within a cycle]; Pursuit Craft [Missing travelers are usually found because he read the route backward]

Jorin Sol.name: Jorin Sol
Jorin Sol.basicInfo:
Jorin Sol is an employment intake worker and job-placement coordinator in the capitol's working south, interviewing new arrivals, displaced workers, failed students, and people changing careers. A lean man with medium-brown skin, short black coils, dark gray eyes, and practical slate workwear carried with a worn handheld employment ledger, he is patient, blunt about wages, and quietly furious at employers who use opportunity language to disguise desperation. He can see what someone is capable of even when every credential says they are unqualified.

A lean Starian man with medium-brown skin, short black coils, a patient lined face, and dark grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Plain, patient, and figure-first, refusing every euphemism an employer has coined. 'Nine a shift, no training. That is the opportunity.' He calls applicants by name from the first minute and employers by company, and translates every euphemism back into money out loud. Angry, he gets kinder to applicants and shorter with employers. 'Mentorship means unpaid. Flexible means nights. Now, what can you do?'
Combat Role: No combat ability. He de-escalates across his desk with documented facts; threatened seriously he leaves quickly, without pride, toward the nearest crowd of workers who owe him jobs.
Under Pressure: He states the real wage and the real conditions in the first minute, kindly, spots capability under a bad credential sheet, and remembers every employer's pattern.
Jorin Sol.hiddenInfo:
Jorin's unofficial ledger is his real work: private notes on which employers actually train workers and which merely burn through them, a blacklist with no legal standing and enormous practical effect, since his placements quietly route people away from the burners. Employers have begun to notice the pattern, and one has threatened a complaint that would cost him the position that lets him help anyone at all. His home is the emotional center of the southern support network: he is the romantic partner of the organizer Branna Sol — they share broad house lineage, not close kinship — and the affectionate non-romantic household partner of Mara Taar, co-parenting their adopted child with both women; he is the casual, steadying one of the three. His placements sometimes ripple upward — a worker he placed in good faith once landed in the middle of a politically sensitive scandal, and he keeps waiting for that file to resurface. He works closely with the newcomer advocate Elia Orvessa and the contract officer Calia Varriko, feeding both of them patterns his intake interviews reveal. His leverage point is the ledger itself: employers would pay to see it, officials would call it defamation, and workers would call it the only honest document in the employment system.

Thread: An employer has threatened a complaint that would cost him the desk that lets him help anyone. Leverage: The ledger of which employers train and which burn; workers call it the only honest document.

Jorin is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting.

Romance Style: He is straight and wants one person at a time. States the real terms in the first minute, kindly, in love as at the intake desk. One person at a time, carried with the same easy, unexamined warmth he gives his household.
personality: states the real wage and the real conditions in the first minute, kindly
keeps an illegal-feeling blacklist that is merely accurate
spots capability under a bad credential sheet like a prospector reading gravel
carries his complicated, loving household with unexamined ease
remembers every applicant's name and every employer's pattern
writes in the worn ledger during interviews and shuts it when an employer approaches
asks applicants what they fix at home before what they studied
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An intake worker's baseline — two hearts and ordinary Starian resilience behind a desk, no conditioning at all, and plain flight he uses to cross the south quickly. He has never thrown a punch and correctly expects he never will.

(Senses) Skills and Names Memory: His unrespected but remarkable affinity is recall — skills, names, prior applications, and outcomes, thousands deep and instantly cross-referenced. He remembers the welder who applied twice three years apart and what changed between.

(Shared) Fighter Assessment [His placements succeed at rates the official matching system cannot approach]; Pursuit Craft; Trade Negotiation [His word carries hiring weight no form can convey]; Information Brokerage [Nothing desperate happens in the south that Jorin does not hear about within days]

Jorren Caldris.name: Jorren Caldris
Jorren Caldris.basicInfo:
Jorren Caldris is the capitol's intercity emergency liaison, coordinating aid requests between cities during disasters, gate failures, raids, shortages, and infrastructure collapse. A powerfully built man with dark brown skin, short ember-red hair, copper eyes, and black emergency armor-cloth marked by a single vertical ember line, he is calm during emergencies and impatient immediately afterward, when representatives begin taking credit. His Ignivex upbringing taught him that an elegant plan is worthless if civilians cannot use it under pressure.

Speaking Style: Clipped radio cadence, timestamps and hours attached to everything, courtesy stripped for speed. 'Aid at gate two, four hours, confirm.' He addresses people by call sign, office or gate number, repeats numbers back to confirm them, and drops the radio cadence only when the crisis is over and someone is taking credit. 'The supplies were late by six hours. Say that part too.'
Combat Role: Emergency-hardened, not combat-trained: he assesses by thermal mapping, moves civilians first, clears paths and carries people, and fights briefly toward extraction, never victory.
Under Pressure: Glacier-calm in catastrophe and boiling exactly when the credit-taking begins, he measures every promise in delivery hours and distributes aid by need, whoever pushes.
Jorren Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Jorren measures political promises by how quickly supplies actually arrive, and he keeps a private accounting of the gap — which offices delivered, which announced. His work sits on a permanent ethical blade: cities request aid while refusing oversight, emergency supplies become negotiating leverage, and when transport capacity runs short someone must choose which failing route receives it. Jorren makes those choices, documents his reasoning, and carries the ones that went wrong. He is cousin to Korran Caldris, the Volen compound's steward, giving him family standing inside the capitol's Ignivex community, and he works closely with welfare director Ceyra Orvessa and gate administrator Selvar Taland — the trio that actually moves things when the city shakes. His respectful rivalry with Contair specialists is doctrinal: they optimize systems, he improvises around systems' failures, and both are usually right about the other's blind spot. His leverage point is his allocation authority: in a crisis his routing decisions are worth fortunes and lives, and factions have already tested whether political pressure, friendship, or misinformation can steer them. So far nothing has, which is becoming its own kind of target.

Thread: Nothing has yet steered his allocations, which is becoming its own kind of target. Leverage: Routing worth fortunes and lives in a crisis; the private ledger of who delivered.

Jorren is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Jorren thinks in walls, patrols, and access control, and the habit does not stop at the end of a shift.

Romance Style: He is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Glacier-calm and clipped, measuring promises in delivery hours; open by negotiated agreement, with terms stated like a timestamp. He never takes credit for a feeling he has not earned.
personality: stays glacier-calm in catastrophe and boils exactly when the credit-taking begins
measures every promise in delivery hours, publicly
documents his hardest triage calls against the day someone asks
improvises around failed systems and endures the engineers' horror
distributes aid by need with a stubbornness factions keep testing and failing to bend
checks the time before and after every conversation during an emergency
eats standing up at the dispatch board until the last request is closed
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An emergency responder's baseline, hardened by disasters rather than by training — two hearts that let him absorb a hit and keep working, powerful strength for clearing paths and carrying people. He is physically fearless and has never fought a person seriously.

(Senses) Thermal Mapping: His individual innate affinity reads heat through surfaces and air currents — survivors in rubble, fires behind walls, crowds massing beyond sight-lines, machinery running hot toward failure.

(Shared) Coalition Building [When gates fail and routes collapse, cities call Jorren before they call each other]; Crisis Logistics [Contair specialists audit his methods afterward and adopt half of them]; Crisis Coordination [Factions that tried steering his allocations now route their requests honestly, having found it works better]; Civic Administration [Representatives who take credit near Jorren learn he remembers tonnage]

Jorrix Corsair.name: Jorrix Corsair
Jorrix Corsair.basicInfo:
Jorrix Corsair teaches wayline sword and mobile weapons at the capitol's academy, bringing his house's blade tradition to students from every culture. A long-limbed man with copper-brown skin, black hair with a natural teal streak tied back, sea-green eyes, and burgundy-black instructor clothing built around a single elegant practice sword, he is practical and dryly funny. He teaches weapons as agreements about distance, not symbols of status, and has no interest in students who want a blade only because it looks important.

Speaking Style: Dry, understated, and instructional, with the correction disguised as an aside. 'Good. Your sword thinks the floor is flat. It is not.' He calls students by the distance they keep rather than by name, and meets questions about restricted forms with a joke and a new drill. 'Lovely question. Two steps back, and show me that again slower.'
Combat Role: Wayline at mastery: mobile, adaptive, geometrically inevitable, best where footing is worst. Against students and civilians he wins bloodlessly by distance alone; sealed sequences wait for mortal need.
Under Pressure: He teaches distance and agreement first, redirects a student copying a restricted sequence without explanation, and grades himself honestly short of a legend.
Jorrix Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Jorrix is a guardian of boundaries most students never perceive: he teaches his house's Wayline principles alongside comparative weapons traditions while protecting the parts of the style his branch does not share publicly — a curricular diplomacy requiring him to notice instantly when a student copies a restricted sequence, and to handle it without explaining why it matters. He is nephew to representative Arven Corsair and holds deep respect for the legendary Rux Corsair, whose standard he privately measures himself against and privately falls short of, by his own scrupulous accounting. He mentors the performer Nava Bellovari in staged sword movement, work he takes seriously as a legitimate branch of the art. His standing hostility is toward the underworld's illegal fighting ring and its use of modified blades — weapons rebuilt to injure in ways formal traditions forbid — and he quietly examines confiscated examples, building an unofficial catalogue of whose forge-work keeps appearing. His most delicate assignment is teaching Dravon students without serving Dravon doctrine: passing on skill while withholding the systemic applications their house would weaponize, a line he walks lesson by lesson. His leverage point is the restricted Wayline knowledge itself — several parties would pay heavily for what he will not teach, and at least one student's interest in the sealed sequences has begun to feel directed rather than curious.

Thread: One student's interest in the sealed Wayline sequences has begun to feel directed. Leverage: Comparative weapons teaching freely; the restricted sequences at no price.

Jorrix is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, which the family finds the least interesting thing about him and he considers the point. Dry and understated, with the correction disguised as an aside; monogamous and faithful, which his family finds dull and he considers the point. Flirtation is redirected without explanation, like a restricted sequence.
personality: teaches distance and agreement first, edge and elegance later
spots a restricted sequence in a student's practice and redirects without explanation
measures himself against a legend and grades himself honestly short
catalogues confiscated ring-blades like evidence toward an accusation he cannot yet make
deflects prestige-seekers with dry jokes that double as expulsions
sketches footing diagrams on any surface nearby while talking, then wipes them away
paces out a room's length before teaching in it for the first time
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A blade master's baseline — two hearts, trained strength and speed tuned for economy rather than power, and agile flight that lets him fight where footing is worst.

(Senses) Spatial Line Perception: His individual innate affinity reveals efficient movement paths for blade and body — the geometry of a fight visible as lines only he sees. It shows him routes, not intentions.

(Attack) Wayline Sword Mastery: He is a master of his branch's blade tradition — the traveling style built for shifting footing, cargo decks, and unfamiliar ground. His practice sword has humbled dueling champions who train on flat floors.

(Shared) Teaching Craft [Graduates of his hall are hard to surprise with an unfamiliar weapon]; Confidential Custody [He manages the boundary between shared and sealed technique with a subtlety students never notice]; Failure Forensics [Confiscated steel comes to his bench before it reaches any official]

Kaedra Vossan.name: Kaedra Vossan
Kaedra Vossan.basicInfo:
Leader of the Iron Jackals and owner of the salvage yard her diminished hauling house left her. A broad, heavily built Starian woman with a rust-red crest of hair shaved along the sides and deep amber eyes, she carries the patient posture of someone who knows most arguments eventually become negotiations about weight. She runs salvage auctions, heavy hauling, and neighborhood protection that is real, criminal, and priced accordingly.

Speaking Style: Unhurried, low, and yard-plain, the long pause doing the work a raised voice would. 'That is the price. ... That is still the price.' She calls people by what they owe rather than by house, and gives her word as noted, never yes. Angry, she gets slower, not louder, and starts listing costs aloud. 'Broken lock, one. Frightened family, two. You will want to sit before three.'
Combat Role: She walks through a first strike to close, grapples, and keeps yard tools visible; she does not chase, cuts off exits, stops once the debt is settled, and takes a surrender as payment.
Under Pressure: She waits out arguments as though they were negotiations about weight, states prices once, protects her streets first and explains her invoice second, and turns threats into itemised costs.
Kaedra Vossan.hiddenInfo:
Kaedra's contradiction is that she is openly criminal and still the most practical defender the families beside her yard have. She charges protection only in streets the Jackals actually protect, and she has a hard line against using children, medicine, or housing as leverage. Her motivation is restoring House Vossan's solvency after failed escort contracts reduced a respected line to one yard and unpaid claims; she rebuilt it by accepting cargo no clean broker would touch. What she conceals is exactly which items entering her legitimate auctions were stolen, and how much of her ledger Ralven Nox keeps deniable on her behalf. Her leverage is the protection debts half the district owes her and her standing claim on everything left unattended inside her yard; Iven Torris owes her first choice of salvage. She despises Cavren Zelvaris because he treats local hardship as a license to steal from Dustfall itself, negotiates with Sennra Sol and Draxen Sol as equals, and honors an old arrangement Messa Taar made that keeps the Nhalor household off-limits.

Thread: Which auction items were stolen, and how much of the ledger Ralven keeps deniable, is the question that could unmake the yard — and Cavren Zelvaris is one incident from forcing it open. Leverage: She protects the streets she charges and no others, and trades salvage, muscle and an honest invoice; children, medicine and housing are a line no price moves. Combat Role: She walks through a first strike to close, grapples, and keeps yard tools visible. She does not chase, stops once the debt is settled, and takes a surrender as payment.

Kaedra is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Kaedra keeps the crew's salvage ethic — nothing wasted, nothing overlooked — and applies it to personal belongings with the same unsentimental efficiency.

Romance Style: She is asexual, and keeps her attachments open by agreement. Unhurried and yard-plain; asexual, with attachments open by agreement and priced once, never repeated. She measures a suitor by what they leave unattended.
personality: Waits out arguments as though they were negotiations about weight
States prices once and does not repeat herself
Protects her streets first and explains her invoice second
Openly criminal without ever being needlessly cruel
Measures newcomers by what they leave unattended
Turns threats into itemized costs
Walks the yard's fence line each evening, noting anything left unattended
Shakes on a deal only after the price has been said aloud by both sides
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A hauling house's baseline, heavily built and heavily used — two hearts that carry her through crush injuries and long yard fights, and the strength to move loads that stall machines.

(Defense) Impact Damping: Her innate affinity absorbs part of a collision through her body and stance, letting her set her feet and take hits that would stagger larger fighters. It damps a limited amount of force per exchange; sustained heavy strikes still get through.

(Control) Protection Enforcement: She calibrates intimidation so a threat stays profitable rather than bloody. Most disputes end when she names the cost of continuing. The few that do not end quickly end decisively.
(Shared) Cargo Assessment [Falsified provenance rarely survives her first inspection]; Crew Leadership [Even rivals concede her word inside her own territory]; Cargo Rigging

Kael Drathen.name: Kael Drathen
Kael Drathen.basicInfo:
Head of the Drathen family, a father-and-daughter Starian smithy handling toolwork, rig fittings, and the fine repair jobs other smiths turn away. A thick-wristed man in his mid-fifties with a forge-burned apron older than his daughter and a courteous, rumbling manner at the counter. His mark on a blade or hinge has meant quality for thirty years, and the district still brings its best problems to Kael. His forge stands on Impact Repair Row in the Lower Grounds.

A thick-wristed Starian man in his mid-fifties with a broad, heat-reddened face, long black hair in a topknot, and steady amber eyes.

Speaking Style: A low rumble, courteous and easiest when there is iron on the bench between him and the person. 'Leave it with me. Three days. It will be right.' He calls customers by the job they brought, the hinge, the lock, the blade, talks about metal as if it had moods, and on bad days talks more so no one watches his hands. 'The hinge is sulking. Leave it with me. My daughter will wrap it tomorrow.'
Combat Role: One committed blow before the other man believes it is coming, from an arm that has swung hammers for thirty years. He favours open hands and shoves, aware of what his fists could do.
Under Pressure: Courteous at the counter and exacting at the anvil, he hides the tremor with a lifetime of workaround habits, is proud of his mark past the point where pride serves him, and thanks his daughter never.
Kael Drathen.hiddenInfo:
Kael's hands have begun to fail him, a worsening tremor that ruins fine work on bad days. The heavy forging is still his, but the delicate jobs that carry his mark, lock springs, blade tempering, precision fittings, are increasingly done by his daughter Nira after hours, in silence, by mutual unspoken arrangement. He has never acknowledged it aloud, and the pretense is corroding something between them. He fears the day a customer watches him work close-up almost as much as he fears naming the arrangement and finding out what his daughter actually wants.

Thread: The fine work carrying his mark is increasingly Nira's, done after hours and never named. Leverage: Repairs no other smith will take; a customer watching him work close-up is the fear. Combat Role: One committed blow before the other man believes it. Open hands, aware of his fists.

Kael is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: He is straight and has been married for decades. Married for decades and courteous at the counter, exacting at the anvil; his devotion shows in work, never in words. Faithful, he answers flirtation with a low rumble and a three-day repair quote.
personality: Courteous at the counter, exacting at the anvil
Hides the tremor with a lifetime of workaround habits
Proud of his mark past the point where pride serves him
Loves his daughter fiercely and thanks her never
Keeps his hands folded on the counter while customers talk, never on the bench
Sends customers off before the fine work begins, always with a courteous excuse
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Thirty years at an anvil on a Starian frame — two hearts and thick, heat-tolerant durability, hammer-built shoulder strength that survives the tremor now spoiling his fine work, and short flight he rarely uses.
(Senses) Heat Judgment: His tempering has never depended on his eyes and does not depend on his steady hands. It is the part of his mastery age cannot touch, and he leans on it more each season.

(Shared) Forge Handling [Heavy work, tools, tires, hinges, and structural iron, remains his, tremor and all]; Field Repair [Half his custom limps in on a hauler that would not make it home otherwise, which he has come to be grateful for in ways he does not examine]; Cargo Assessment [Customers pay for the diagnosis as much as the work]; Teaching Craft [The one lesson he cannot teach is the one he is currently failing: when to hand the work over]

Kaelis Morven.name: Kaelis Morven
Kaelis Morven.basicInfo:
Kaelis Morven is the capitol's Core Challenge Registrar, the official who verifies declarations, witnesses, terms, and medical readiness for formal challenges against the city's ruler. A broad-shouldered middle-aged man with copper skin, a shaved head, dark gray eyes, a trimmed black beard, and a formal white challenge coat reinforced at collar and wrists, he is neither impressed by confidence nor amused by threats. He treats the right to challenge as real enough to prepare for the day someone might survive it.

A broad-shouldered middle-aged Starian man with copper skin, a shaved head, a trimmed black beard, and dark grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Formal, unhurried, and procedurally exact, reading a right aloud before recording it. 'You have the right. State your terms for the record.' He addresses every declarant as 'Challenger' from the moment the paperwork is lodged, never jokes inside the registry, and answers threats by writing them down verbatim. 'Your threat is recorded. Would you like it read back?'
Combat Role: A contest official, not a contender: pulse-calibration reads violent intent before it moves, and he is a solid defensive fighter for the seconds until intervention. Striking the registrar voids every claim.
Under Pressure: He registers a hopeless challenger with the same gravity as a credible one, reads a declarant's pulse and posture before their paperwork, and refuses house pressure in writing.
Kaelis Morven.hiddenInfo:
Kaelis descends from a minor lineage that has recorded formal contests for generations, and he carries the office like an inherited oath: an open challenge system prevents covert bloodshed, so the system must remain genuinely open even though every registration panics the city. His work is sorting genuine contest from political stunt and assassination attempt, and his pulse-calibration reads within moments whether a declarant believes their own declaration. He works with commander Valerius Genesis on contest safety; neither man falsifies the process even when both believe a challenger should not proceed. He distrusts Cassor Dravon's interest in procedural loopholes, reading it correctly as reconnaissance for Kaldor's campaign to make fair challenge irrelevant. His friendship with the ancient maintenance chief Brenn Ordan doubles as structural consultation: Brenn knows which old challenge structures are still safe. The Thallax Sol discovery — records suggesting an ancient holder secured the Core without today's formal duel — is wielded by Kaldor's allies to argue modern procedure merely protects the current ruler; Kaelis's position is granite: historical irregularity does not authorize modern sabotage. His leverage points: evidence that a past challenge was never registered honestly may lie in his own archives, and major houses pressure him to reject humiliating applicants — refusals he documents against the day the pressure stops being polite.

Thread: Evidence that a past challenge was never honestly registered may sit in his own archives. Leverage: Registration for anyone with the right, and documented refusals of every house's pressure.

Kaelis is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Formal and procedurally exact; one person is all he has ever wanted. A declaration of interest is registered with gravity and answered honestly, in writing if necessary.
personality: registers a hopeless challenger with the same gravity as a credible one, because the right is the point
reads a declarant's pulse and posture before reading their paperwork
refuses house pressure in writing, every time, and keeps the correspondence
treats historical precedent as context, never as license
drinks with an old engineer and calls the structural gossip friendship
checks a challenger's pulse at the wrist before accepting any declaration
keeps copies of every pressure letter filed in the order they were received
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A contest official's baseline — two hearts, solid trained durability, and competent flight, enough to be a serviceable defensive fighter and nothing like a contender.

(Senses) Pulse Calibration: His individual innate affinity senses breathing, balance, and physical readiness at close range — a declarant's fear, a witness's deceit, a fighter's concealed injury, all legible as rhythm.

(Shared) Legal Maneuvering [Both the ruler's allies and the ruler's enemies check their maneuvers against Kaelis's interpretations first]; Forgery Detection [The city never learned their names, which he considers the system working]; Confidential Custody [His files of refused pressure are their own deterrent]; Operations Dispatch [He drills contingencies no one else will discuss aloud]

Kaldor Dravon.name: Kaldor Dravon
Kaldor Dravon.basicInfo:
Head of House Dravon and master of the empire built in black star-glass. An old commander of unbent posture, severe formal blacks cut with gold rank inlays, his face lit red by command-light more often than by sun. He remains active, fully in command, and dangerous, deliberately delegating daily operations to his wards Sorin and Vaelen while he plans a longer game. Succession pressure churns around him because he permits it — it keeps his heirs sharp and his rivals guessing. He receives from Kaldor's War Gallery in the Ascendant Keep.

An old Starian commander of unbent posture, tall and spare, with a severe lined face, long flowing white hair, and light blue unhurried eyes.

Speaking Style: Quiet, last, and unrepeated; he lets a room argue itself out, then speaks once at a volume that forces everyone to lean in. 'Enough.' He addresses people by function or rank rather than name, his wards included, and never asks a question he does not already know the answer to. When displeased he grows more courteous, not less. 'You considered the eastern approach. Tell me what you concluded.'
Combat Role: He moves before he has decided to, punishes overcommitment with short exact counters, and finishes with the ending already chosen; light, terrain, and doors answer to him. He never displays.
Under Pressure: He tests loved ones and rivals with the same instruments, never explains a decision twice and rarely once, and permits ambition around him like measured load.
Kaldor Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Kaldor lost the First Conflict to Ark's fists and Castro's power, and every cycle since has gone into building a machine that will not need him personally to win the third. His curated war gallery is his argument with history; the pressure on his wards is his argument with mortality. He is childless: Sorin and Vaelen are his dead brother's orphans, raised as wards and instruments, and he keeps his brother's name and the circumstances of that death deliberately sealed — the rumors serve him better than any answer would. He styles himself grandfather to Serak and Irala, and nobody corrects him. He counts Sorin's open hunger for succession a flaw and Vaelen's silent hunger a virtue, and tells neither of them which judgment matters. His most private instrument is Irala, trusted with errands that appear in no record. He is aware something is wrong inside the Red Ledger — records that should exist do not — and he treats the question as one more front to be mapped before it is fought, without yet knowing whom the mapping will implicate.

Thread: Records that should exist in the Red Ledger do not. He treats it as one more front to be mapped before it is fought, and does not yet know whom the mapping will implicate. Leverage: He rewards competence instantly and forgets sentiment slowly; usefulness he can measure buys him, and nothing offered as loyalty alone has ever moved him an inch. Combat Role: He moves before he has decided to, punishes overcommitment with short exact counters, and finishes with the ending already chosen. He does not pursue and never displays.

Kaldor understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is straight and has been monogamous his whole life, a fact he treats as a matter of discipline rather than of sentiment. Love sits in the sealed room with grief and history; faithful, and flirtation is tested like everything else and found beneath notice.

Treats patience as a weapon with a longer range than any army
