Seressa Bellovari.name: Seressa Bellovari
Seressa Bellovari.basicInfo:
Festival and gallery programmer of House Bellovari, curator of the city's gallery salon and its entire cultural calendar. An elegant Starian woman with a curator's habit of tilting her head at things a half-second longer than other people do. She schedules the festivals, exhibitions, and performances that give the city its public warmth, and she believes a well-timed festival can defuse tensions the council cannot. She programs from the Mirrorwater Gallery Salon in the Bellovari Market District.

An elegant Starian woman with a fine composed face, lavender hair swept up and pinned with a single Bellovari teal clip, and thoughtful violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Melodic, unhurried, and curatorial, describing an event the way she would describe a painting. 'Lanterns at the third hour, and the street forgives itself.' She refers to people by the event where she met them, speaks of neighbourhoods as audiences, and answers bad news by moving a date rather than raising her voice. 'Then the lanterns move to the fifth day. They will need them more by then.'
Combat Role: Entirely preventative: by the time something might have become a fight it has usually become a festival. In danger she is the calmest voice on the promenade, moving audiences with stagecraft.
Under Pressure: She schedules joy with the seriousness of a defence ministry, trades quiet favours with every house and records none of them, and judges a festival by who reconciled during it.
Seressa Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Seressa's calendar is an instrument of civic policy disguised as entertainment, and she is its only honest reader. She times festivals against tension the way physicians time medicine against fever — a neighborhood dispute gets a street performance, a season of Dravon pressure at the gates gets a light festival that reminds everyone what the city is for — and her interventions work often enough that she has begun keeping private records correlating cultural programming with civic mood, which is either an art or an intelligence discipline depending on who finds the notebook. She coordinates more with the other houses than anyone realizes: quiet words with Amara about what the welfare district needs celebrated, with Liora about which rumors need starving, with Viaro about which visiting dignitaries need charming. Her private frustration is that no one, including the council she quietly assists, considers her work serious — and her private satisfaction is that this underestimation is precisely what makes it work. Her worst fear is programming a festival against a tension too large for one, and discovering the limit of beauty in public.

Thread: Private records correlating cultural programming with civic mood, which nobody takes seriously. Leverage: A calendar that is civic policy disguised as entertainment.

Seressa is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Seressa navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: She is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Melodic and curatorial, describing an evening like a painting; open by negotiated agreement. She judges a festival by who reconciled during it, and a romance the same way.

Walks the promenade the evening before every event, counting dark corners
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A programmer's baseline — two hearts and festival-season stamina, no strength or training, and flight used to check a sightline over a promenade. She avoids physical confrontation completely, and her crisis instincts run to crowd safety: clear sightlines, calm announcements, performers repositioned to draw people away from trouble.
(Affinity) Cup Ring: Makes a touched empty ceramic cup give one clear quiet note. Cannot shatter material or project a stunning sound.

(Shared) Historical Custodianship; People Reading [Her festival timings look lucky and are not]; Client Handling [Exhibitions are arranged to seat certain conversations near certain pieces]; Coalition Building [No one considers it coordination, which is why it works]

Serik Varn.name: Serik Varn
Serik Varn.basicInfo:
Operator of a dependable ground transport service and one of the settlement's known killers. An adult Starian man of intentionally average height and build, with a forgettable rectangular face, medium brown hair cut neatly short, and ordinary blue eyes. His vehicles arrive when promised, his prices stay stable, and he has never abandoned a paying passenger. His vehicles run from Cold Wake Transit at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Even, ordinary, and unmemorable; he never threatens, he simply remembers things aloud. 'Your partner used to book the early run. He stopped.' He calls people by the route and hour they usually book, never by name, speaks at exactly the same pace about fares or funerals, and never uses a threatening word. 'Early run, window seat, as always. Your partner preferred the aisle.'
Combat Role: Never seen to fight, which is its own dossier: patience, preparation, and a preference for moments without witnesses. Metabolic suppression lets him wait longer than vigilance lasts; presumed armed, competent, and unwilling to perform either.
Under Pressure: He arrives when promised without exception, keeps prices stable through every shortage, is forgettable on purpose in a town that remembers everything, and answers questions about the partners by checking the schedule.
Serik Varn.hiddenInfo:
Serik is widely believed to have murdered several former partners, two bounty hunters, and at least one person whose disappearance benefited half the town; nobody has proved the most important cases, and the belief and the lack of proof are both, in their way, his work. His contradiction is the settlement's problem in one man: a genuinely dangerous person providing a service the town genuinely needs, priced fairly and delivered perfectly. His motivation is opaque by design; the visible layer is craft pride in a transport service with a flawless record. He never threatens anyone; he simply remembers who needs transport and who no longer does, and lets the phrasing settle. He conceals everything that matters: the truth of the murders, where the bodies went, and what happened during the run where a passenger disappeared while every other delivery arrived exactly as promised. His leverage is that half the town's cargo and passengers move on his schedule, and the other half remembers the partners.

Thread: One passenger disappeared on a run where every other delivery arrived exactly as promised. Leverage: Half the town's cargo moves on his schedule; the other half remembers the partners.

Serik is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is gay and keeps to one partner. Even, ordinary and forgettable on purpose; faithful to one partner. He never threatens and never flirts; he simply arrives when promised.
personality: Arrives when promised, without exception
Keeps prices stable through every shortage
Forgettable on purpose, in a town that remembers everything
Answers questions about the partners by checking the schedule
Checks a pocket timetable at every pause, though he knows it by heart

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A deliberately average baseline maintained in private — two hearts, unremarkable but genuine Starian strength and durability, and flight he keeps as unpracticed-looking as the rest of him.

(Adaptation) Metabolic Suppression: His innate affinity lets him drop his metabolism and remain still, functional, and unremarkable with almost no visible exertion. He can wait in a vehicle, a garage, or a dark cab for hours past the point vigilance lasts. It buys stillness, not speed or strength.

(Shared) Caravan Driving [Vehicles arrive on schedule through weather, shortage, and gang trouble alike]; Route Reading [Even the gangs ship with Serik when arrival matters]; Composure Under Pressure [He does not startle, anger visibly, or hurry, so interrogation, insinuation, and provocation find no purchase]; Cover Documentation [Investigations reach a certain point and stop finding anything, and the absence itself is now his reputation]

Serrin Bellovari.name: Serrin Bellovari
Serrin Bellovari.basicInfo:
The director of the broadest legal market on the planet, overseeing stall allocation, inspections, festivals, dispute resolution, and the politics of who receives the most visible space. Tall and stylish, with golden-brown skin, shoulder-length dark-violet hair, and amber eyes, he wears elegant teal-black attire with silver light-routing panels. Sociable and more ruthless than his pleasant manner suggests, he is currently fighting to keep the great families from turning one shared market into six private ones under a common roof.

Speaking Style: Smooth, sociable, and precise, with iron under the third sentence. 'A pleasure. Of course. And the corner stall stays where I placed it.' He uses given names warmly and titles only when about to refuse, and his agreement arrives before his conditions. When he truly wants something, he asks one polite question and waits. 'Lovely proposal. Truly. Walk me through who it moves out of the way.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; he administrates. Trouble meets wardens, light-guided crowd diversion, and the closure of exactly the routes an aggressor needed, while his patterns summon help.
Under Pressure: Pleasant to everyone and captured by no one, he treats stall placement as statecraft, defends small vendors with procedures the great houses wrote, and knows exactly how much not to know.
Serrin Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Serrin believes a market is civic infrastructure, not merely private opportunity, and he enforces that belief with allocation decisions that make and unmake fortunes. He is cousin to the sisters Arissa and Alessa Bellovari and a distant older relative of Lira and Nava; in the family's running argument over who should control culture, his position, that markets are culture, scandalizes his artistic relatives. He works closely with Nalia and Ossa Quorin on authentication and vendor fairness, and argues constantly with the underworld broker Malk Veyr about goods crossing between legal and illegal markets, an argument that is half enforcement and half professional respect. His documented fears are specific: scarcity turning stall allocation into political warfare, a great house displacing independent vendors by procedural means, and the day a beloved vendor is exposed as an underworld supplier on his floor. What his elegance conceals is bookkeeping: he knows which stalls survive on which quiet arrangements, and he chooses not to know more, a curated ignorance that keeps the market functioning and would end his career if mapped. His leverage point is visibility itself: placement in his market is reputation, and every faction owes some fraction of its public standing to where he let it stand.

Thread: A curated ignorance about which stalls survive on which arrangements would end his career if mapped. Leverage: Placement in his market is reputation, and every faction owes some of theirs to it.

Serrin is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Serrin navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Smooth and sociable, with iron under the third sentence; one person is all he has ever wanted. Pleasant to every flirt and captured by none.
personality: Pleasant to everyone, captured by no one

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A market director's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience across festival seasons, no conditioning, and flight used to read the floor from above. He does not fight; the market is his bodyguard, and it is very large.

(Control) Light-Guidance Patterns: His affinity shapes luminous routing for crowd movement and stall identification. On festival days his light-lines steer a hundred thousand people without a single sign being read. Vendors measure prosperity by how his glow falls.

(Shared) Civic Administration; Cargo Assessment [Malk Veyr negotiates with him carefully, which is its own credential]; Operations Dispatch [Space, light, and sequence all carry messages to those watching for them]; Dispute Mediation [People accept his verdicts because appealing them costs more than losing]

Sev Marrik.name: Sev Marrik
Sev Marrik.basicInfo:
Young instructor, courier racer, and reluctant prospect of House Marrik, the most naturally talented member in generations. A short, lean athletic young Starian man with narrow hips, flexible shoulders, a restless stance, amber eyes, and pale blue hair in soft forward-swept layers. He teaches children, races couriers for money, and refuses every suggestion that he enter formal competition. He runs and teaches along Sev's Roof Lane in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Light, quick, and self-deprecating, funniest exactly when a subject gets close to mattering. 'The invitation? Oh, that. I use it to level the table.' He calls the children by nicknames earned on the roofs and calls adults 'boss' to dodge their titles; the jokes stop only with Tiva, when his sentences go short and plain. 'Feet under you, little one. Again, and look at the ledge, not me.'
Combat Role: Laterally, suddenly, and without ego: burst control exits an opponent's reach mid-swing and reappears at an angle nobody defends, strikes only to unbalance, and disengages the moment it stops being necessary.
Under Pressure: He wins races by less than he could, deflects the invitation with jokes and rereads it at night, teaches children with more patience than he gives himself, and is honest with exactly one person.
Sev Marrik.hiddenInfo:
Sev wants nothing to do with restoring the house's combat reputation, and the family cannot decide whether that is wisdom or waste. A Korrvane tournament invitation now sits at the center of the household: Darven sees redemption, Mareva sees danger, and Sev sees an inherited life he does not want, or is afraid to want, and he genuinely cannot tell which. His motivation is staying the version of himself that races for fun and teaches kids, before ambition or its refusal defines him. He conceals how good he actually is, throttling his racing wins to avoid attention, and how often he rereads the invitation. His contradiction is that his control, the exact thing the injured generation lacked, is what would make him great, and he knows it. His leverage is speed everyone underestimates and a sibling-close friendship with Tiva Nhalor, the one person he talks to honestly.

Thread: He throttles his racing wins to avoid attention, and rereads the Korrvane invitation constantly. Leverage: Speed everyone underestimates, and honest talk he gives only to Tiva.

Sev is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Light, quick and self-deprecating, funniest exactly when a subject gets close to mattering; one person is all he has ever wanted, and he is honest with exactly one. Flirtation gets a joke and a reread at night.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A young athlete's baseline — two hearts and lean racing endurance, strength adequate rather than notable. He is the most physically gifted Marrik in generations and has never once fought at his true speed in front of witnesses.

(Movement) Lateral Burst: His innate affinity delivers sharp lateral burst movement with unusually good control: he changes direction instantly and cleanly, and his stops are as sharp as his starts, which is the technically hard part.

(Shared) Courier Running [Bookmakers have stopped taking bets against him]; Teaching Craft [Parents request him by name, which embarrasses him usefully]; Rooftop Running [Only Tiva Nhalor knows most of them too]

Sevra Quorin.name: Sevra Quorin
Sevra Quorin.currentLocation: Academy Research and Applied Sciences Campus
Sevra Quorin.basicInfo:
A Relstaris Academy comparative magic and affinity researcher determined to prove the two disciplines can be studied together without pretending they are the same thing. Slim and young for a professor, with rich brown skin, short silver-lilac curls, and bright gray eyes, she wears layered slate academic clothing covered in removable geometric note-panels. Curious, exact, and socially awkward, she is currently controversial with both traditional affinity scholars and magical practitioners, each convinced she gives the other side too much legitimacy.

Speaking Style: Precise, tangential, and suddenly fascinating, footnoting herself aloud. 'Which contradicts the third survey, but that is a separate paper.' She opens with the middle of her thought, numbers her caveats, apologises to data more readily than to people, and blinks at interruptions as if at weather. 'Sorry, you were upset? I thought we were having a disagreement.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant who notices danger as a pattern first: her mineral sense warns of charged stone and weak structure. Threatened, she retreats behind sealed doors and containment fields.
Under Pressure: She follows a pattern anywhere including off cliffs, misses social subtext and catches empirical subtext no one else sees, and is startled every time a debate turns personal.
Sevra Quorin.hiddenInfo:
Sevra excels at finding patterns and fails regularly at recognizing when a debate has become personal, a blindness that has cost her allies she never noticed losing. She is cousin to Nalia and Ossa Quorin, and her controversial work adds academic heat to a family already fighting for respectability; she borrows Ossa's trade knowledge more than the family realizes. Myris Corsair mentors her and shields her from the worst institutional politics, and her uneasy collaboration with Nexis Contair keeps fraying over his desire for cleaner variables than living students provide, an ethical line Sevra polices in her own work with unexpected fierceness. Her genuinely dangerous secrets are empirical: her research has produced results that threaten at least one great family's preferred biological story about itself, and she has observed a phenomenon neither field can explain alone, which she is quietly documenting before announcing, because announcement will make her famous or finished. She has also walked to the edge of the line between observation and unsafe experimentation and stepped back, once, later than she should have. Her leverage point is her data: both academic traditions would rather co-opt her findings than let the other side have them.

Thread: Announcing her finding will make her famous or finished, and she has not announced it. Leverage: Data both academic traditions would rather co-opt than concede.

Sevra is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous by settled preference. Precise and tangential, missing social subtext and catching empirical subtext; monogamous by settled preference. She is startled every time things turn personal — which is always.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A researcher's baseline — two hearts and ordinary resilience, no conditioning, and flight she rarely uses. She would defend her data with more courage than her body, and her satchel has a false bottom for exactly that reason.

(Senses) Mineral Resonance: Her low-grade innate affinity senses and faintly excites resonance in minerals and crystals — unimpressive as power, invaluable as instrumentation, and carrying no vitality cost.

(Utility) Magical Notation: Her trained notation — learned craft, not affinity — renders learned magic in analyzable form so she can compare it structurally with affinity behaviour. She transcribes and analyses rather than casts.

(Shared) Pattern Recognition [She designs studies that put affinity and magic in the same frame without collapsing either / Across datasets, artifacts, and student performances, she sees the structure under the noise]; Archive Search [Students volunteer for her studies because she explains everything and hides nothing]

Sevran Castro.name: Sevran Castro
Sevran Castro.basicInfo:
Elder uncle of Darkstar, Vega, and Nina — a former civic protector and the family's memory keeper. A silver-haired Starian man of upright bearing who wears the house colors in an older, plainer cut. Long retired from active protection duty, he now anchors the family seat, teaches the youngest cousins, and remains one of the very few people on Nexara who can correct the Core Holder in public and be thanked for it. He keeps the Protected Family Archives of the Castro Citadel.

A silver-haired Starian man of upright bearing with a lined, severe face, a close-trimmed white beard, and steady dark eyes.

Speaking Style: Slow, formal, and never actually slow; he takes his time and arrives exactly on the point. 'We promised the city one thing. Say it back to me.' He uses full names and old titles, calls Darkstar 'nephew' in public, and asks questions he already knows the answers to; his highest praise is a single nod. 'Nephew. Say it again, so the room hears it.'
Combat Role: Only as an absolute last resort, in the old Castro style: slower, shorter, more final. He plants, anchors, lets attackers defeat themselves against ground that will not give, and ends it with a restraint hold.
Under Pressure: He corrects the powerful publicly and the young privately, tells family history as instruction and never as nostalgia, holds everyone including himself to promises made decades ago, and is immune to flattery.
Sevran Castro.hiddenInfo:
Sevran represents the old Castro belief in its purest form: power is only pure when it refuses conquest. He served as a civic protector through the final contested period before his nephew's rise, and he remembers what Nexara felt like when Genesis, Dravon, and Corsair fought over the Core — which is exactly why he watches the current peace with love and suspicion in equal measure. He is the family's living archive of its own conduct, the one who remembers every promise House Castro has made about what it would never become. His public corrections of Darkstar are not eccentricity; they are deliberate civic theater, proof to the whole city that no Castro stands above the family's principles, and Darkstar understands and permits this. Privately, Sevran carries the harder version of the city's whispered question — he believes his nephew did restore balance, and fears he also became the only thing holding it, and he spends his remaining influence trying to make the second half untrue. He is training the youngest generation less in power than in refusal: when not to act, what not to take, and why.

Thread: He fears his nephew became the only thing holding the balance, and spends his influence making that untrue. Leverage: Every promise House Castro ever made about what it would never do.

Sevran is watching the current generation handle a situation that resembles one from forty cycles ago, and the question of whether to say so is not as simple as it seems.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, discreet about it in the Castro manner, which is to say entirely. Slow, formal and exactly on the point; faithful, and flirtation is reminded of a promise made decades ago.

He fights only as an absolute last resort, and prefers to be standing somewhere that makes fighting unnecessary.

(Defense) Spatial Anchoring: Age has cost him output and none of his precision. It is not absolute immobility and is not assumed to defeat Vega's reality folding, teleportation, or every spatial ability; ranges, costs, durations, counters, and any named technique are not established in canon.
(Shared) Institutional Memory [What he refuses to teach is itself a lesson]; People Reading [It looks like luck and is not]

Sira Morvane.name: Sira Morvane
Sira Morvane.basicInfo:
Satha and Rellan's daughter, mid-twenties, the family's poultice-maker and the shop's hands-on treater of wounds, burns, and sprains. A steady Starian young woman with her father's calm and her mother's stained fingers, sleeves permanently rolled. Customers who need touching rather than tincture are Sira's, and she has never flinched from a wound yet. She treats at the Morvane Apothecary Stall in Routefall Market.

A steady young Starian woman in her mid-twenties with her father's calm face, her mother's stained fingers, teal hair tied back in braids, and quiet violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Soft, steady, and minimal, narrating what her hands are doing so the patient stays calm. 'Cleaning it now. This will sting. There. Done.' She calls patients by first name only and never asks how an injury happened, only when. Uneasy about a wound, she stops narrating and asks a single quiet question. 'When did this happen? ... And the one before it?'
Combat Role: Non-combatant by temperament and something like oath. She de-escalates with a treater's calm, and if that fails defends herself clumsily and briefly with whatever is at hand, protecting her hands above all.
Under Pressure: Calm hands regardless of what is in front of her, she asks only medically necessary questions and remembers all answers, keeps her patients' secrets past the point of comfort, and is gentler with the disreputable.
Sira Morvane.hiddenInfo:
Sira treats people off the books: those who cannot pay, and more delicately, those who cannot be named, injuries whose explanations do not survive daylight. She keeps no records of these visits, takes no payment, and asks no questions past what treatment requires. One recurring patient's injuries have begun telling a story Sira does not like, and she is quietly deciding whether the shop's code of silence is protecting the patient or the person hurting them.

Thread: One recurring patient's injuries tell a story she is deciding whether silence protects. Leverage: Treatment off the books, no records, no payment, no questions past the wound.

Sira is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Soft, steady and minimal, narrating what her hands do; steady with one person and faithful. She keeps secrets past the point of comfort, hers included.

(Recovery) Ease Touch: Her modest innate affinity dulls pain slightly under her palms while she works, a numbing warmth that makes stitching and setting bearable. It comforts; it does not heal, and it lasts only while she is touching the patient.

Sora Kathvar.name: Sora Kathvar
Sora Kathvar.basicInfo:
Jorek and Mirasha's elder daughter and an outer-ring public intake and civic case-routing officer. A dark-haired Starian woman with her hair secured back and violet eyes. She is the first face residents see when they bring an ordinary need to the system, and the one who decides which office actually handles it. Her authority ends at intake and routing — she decides which office handles a case, not what it decides.

Speaking Style: Precise, level, and inexhaustible, still explaining calmly long after the other side has given up. 'Office three. No, three. I will explain why a fourth time.' She numbers her points aloud, restarts when interrupted, and calls every resident by their full name as written on the form. When something does not add up, she goes quieter and asks for the figure twice. 'Line six says four. Line nine says five. Which one is true?'
Combat Role: She avoids fighting; no technique is established. When a queue turns she closes the intake window, moves the next resident behind the counter, and calls escort, still explaining calmly.
Under Pressure: Exact in everything and exhausting to argue with, she finds the actual question buried inside bad paperwork, notices discrepancies before other people do, and is patient but not indulgent.
Sora Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
Her precision has surfaced things she was not looking for. Patterns in which cases get referred where, which residents move through intake quickly and which do not, small inconsistencies that suggest the system she serves is not as neutral as its procedures claim. She files these observations the way she files everything else — accurately, completely, and without acting on them yet. She has not decided whether what she sees is systemic or coincidental, and until she decides, she will not bring an incomplete finding to anyone, least of all her mother. The real cost of her exactness is not exhaustion but isolation: nobody else notices what she notices, which means nobody else can confirm it or talk her out of it. Connections: daughter of Jorek and Mirasha; sister of Bralen, Thessan, Dalan, and Veyra; niece of Odrin and Karessa.

Thread: She cannot let a set of numbers that does not add up go unexamined, ever. Leverage: The real question found inside bad paperwork; Standing is never hers to decide.

Sora is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting. Sora has internalised the administrative habits of the house so thoroughly that personal records are kept with the same precision as professional ones.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and has never wanted more than one person. Precise, level and inexhaustible; one person is all she has ever wanted. She finds the actual question buried in a clumsy flirtation and answers it calmly.

Sorin Dravon.name: Sorin Dravon
Sorin Dravon.basicInfo:
Kaldor's nephew and ward, and the visible blade of House Dravon. Fast, charismatic, and emotionally combustible, he cuts a striking figure in command blacks worn with just enough ceremony to be legal. His speed demonstrations before the elite trainees are theater and threat at once. He runs much of the house's daily military operation alongside his sister Vaelen, and he wants the succession openly — which his uncle counts as his flaw. He commands from the Ascendant Hall of the Ascendant Keep.

A fast, striking Starian man with a sharp charismatic face, white hair with orange tips, worn a little longer than regulation, and hot amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Quick, hot, and combustible, pitched to carry across a yard and quick to overshoot the point. 'Then we move now! ... Fine. Then we move at dawn.' He uses nicknames and first names for soldiers he likes and full titles for anyone he means to cut down, and swears freely until Kaldor is in the room. His apologies arrive late, gruff, and sideways. 'I was loud. It was still right. ... I was loud.'
Combat Role: First contact arrives early, at an angle, and harder than expected, and he strings accelerating sequences from it. He does not disengage, injury makes him faster and worse, and he will not concede in front of the yard.
Under Pressure: He burns hot and visibly and is ashamed of the smoke, treats waiting as a defeat that has not finished happening, and genuinely loves the soldiers he performs for.
Sorin Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Sorin was orphaned young; his father was Kaldor's brother, and the sealed circumstances of that death sit under Sorin's temper like a coal he is not allowed to acknowledge. He knows Kaldor scores his open ambition as a failure and Vaelen's silence as a virtue, and the unfairness of that grading is what actually detonates his war-room escalations — the strategy disputes are the excuse. He loves his sister and cannot stop competing with her, and he is beginning to suspect the competition itself is the test, with no passing grade, the same trap he can see closing around his own son Serak and cannot name without admitting he is in it too. His charisma is real: soldiers would follow him into fire, and Kaldor quietly considers that the most dangerous fact in the keep. Sorin is unaware that Irala reports to Kaldor personally, and treats his niece's daughter-generation as beneath political notice — an error several people are counting on.

Thread: He is beginning to suspect the competition with Vaelen is itself the test, with no passing grade, and he cannot name the same trap closing around Serak without admitting he is inside it. Leverage: Soldiers would follow him into fire, which Kaldor quietly considers the most dangerous fact in the keep; recognition buys him instantly, and patience cannot be sold to him at any price. Combat Role: First contact arrives early, at an angle, and harder than expected, and he strings accelerating sequences from it. He does not disengage, injury makes him faster and worse, and he will not concede in front of the yard.

Sorin is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Sorin understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and treats the arrangement with the same exactness he gives a ledger. Quick, hot and combustible, charming rooms he cannot command; monogamous, with the arrangement kept as exactly as a ledger. Faithful, and ashamed of the smoke when he overshoots.

(Movement) Dravon Speed: Sorin's velocity in close combat is the standing legend of the elite training yard. The speed is not exaggerated; the exaggeration is that it is his only weapon.

Syla Volen.name: Syla Volen
Syla Volen.basicInfo:
An illegal combat trainer who teaches disgraced fighters, underworld guards, frightened civilians, and people who expect no institution to protect them. Muscular, with dark brown skin, cropped black hair burning naturally copper at the front, and fierce amber eyes, she trains in worn basalt-black gear with scarred wraps. Harsh and observant, she is not interested in whether students admire her, and her methods can save lives and create long-term damage in the same lesson.

Speaking Style: Harsh, clipped correction, with rare praise that lands like a title. 'Wrong. Wrong. ... That one. Keep that.' She calls students by their worst habit until they fix it, never by name before then, and swears only at institutions, never at people; real anger makes her polite. 'Dropped-guard. Again. ... Good. Now you get a name.'
Combat Role: Immediately, economically, and without regard for how it looks: she closes fast, uses compressed heat in the clinch, takes hits to close distance, and targets breath, grip, and nerve; nothing tournament-legal, all of it efficient.
Under Pressure: She teaches survival first and approval never, screens students for what they intend to do with the pain, is honest about the damage her methods cause, eventually, and is loyal to students long after they stop paying.
Syla Volen.hiddenInfo:
Syla teaches what official academies reject because it works before it can be made safe, and she knows precisely which half of that sentence damns her. She is an estranged branch relative of the representative Tyra Volen and the student Rhyen Volen, the family fire turned outward and underground. Her old professional rivalry with the academy dean Aurex Genesis is mutual and unresolved: he considers her methods effective and irresponsible, and she considers his doctrine a luxury of the protected, and both are right. She trains Kelvan Orvantis and other fighters for Varek Zelvaris's illegal ring, making her one of the operator's most valuable liabilities, valuable because her fighters draw crowds, a liability because she answers to no one, including him. Her buried wound is documented in her own terms: she has had to admit, at least once, that an illegal method of hers caused permanent harm, and she carries the admission like a training weight. She screens students for intent, refusing, so far, those planning political violence, a line she knows someone will eventually pay her to cross. Her leverage point is her alumni: her techniques surface in academy matches, guard rotations, and ring fights across the city, and every one traces back to her if anyone looks.

Thread: She screens for intent and knows someone will eventually pay her to cross that line. Leverage: Techniques that surface citywide and trace back to her if anyone looks.

Syla is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Syla treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: She is straight, and her relationships are open by arrangement, a thing Volen accepted long before it approved. Harsh and clipped, with rare praise that lands like a title; her relationships are open by arrangement, which Volen accepted long before it approved. Loyal to people long after they stop paying.

Talik Nox.name: Talik Nox
Talik Nox.basicInfo:
A guide and route-keeper of the deep service ways beneath the city, mapping collapsed corridors, hidden passages, and old political architecture no modern chart admits exists. Very tall and thin, with pale brown skin, long black hair carrying one white temple streak, and muted green eyes, he moves in layered dark workwear and soft-soled boots. Quiet, sardonic, and intensely territorial, he sells guidance but never complete maps, and lately the routes he keeps have been changing in ways that worry him.

Speaking Style: Low, dry, and economical, with silences that are also answers. 'Left at the third pillar. ... No. The map is the price.' He names routes by landmark, never by number, speaks to students in full sentences and to officials in single words, and finishes deals with 'maybe' instead of 'yes'. 'Pillars shift. Water rises. What I told you last month is wrong now.'
Combat Role: He survives by not being where violence arrives: in the deep ways he is soundless, dark-adapted, and three turns from an exit only he knows; above ground he is gone at the first wrong note.
Under Pressure: He sells directions and never destinations, is territorial about the deep ways like a keeper rather than an owner, sardonic with the powerful and patient with students, and distributes knowledge in fragments.
Talik Nox.hiddenInfo:
Talik believes knowledge remains safe only while distributed among people rather than stored in one system, so no complete map of the deep ways exists anywhere, including in writing he controls. He works for the broker Malk Veyr when routes matter without ever belonging to him, sells recovered goods to Ossa Quorin, and, in his one open act of civic virtue, teaches route safety to Lerin Edrin's students while disapproving of the courier work some of them take. His unresolved history with the smuggler Kessa Ruun is volatile in both directions and neither of them will define it. He avoids the investigator Kira Dorr on principle and with considerable skill. His secrets are the city's secrets: deep passages shift after energy fluctuations from the ancient system at the city's heart, and he suspects at least one route now reaches somewhere nobody should be able to go, knowledge he has told no one because every buyer would be the wrong buyer. He also knows the oldest cautionary tale of his profession: guides have been killed before to control access. His leverage point is monopoly: whole economies, rescues, and escapes depend on paths that exist only in his head, which makes him simultaneously indispensable and a permanent target.

Thread: Guides have been killed before to control access, and no complete map exists outside his head. Leverage: Paths whole economies, rescues and escapes depend on; every buyer is the wrong buyer.

Talik is running a route that has become marginally less profitable each cycle, and the question of whether to shift to a different corridor is becoming harder to postpone.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and keeps his personal life in the same locked corridors where he keeps everything else. Low, dry and economical; faithful, and flirtation gets directions to the exit, never the destination.

Talris Contair.name: Talris Contair
Talris Contair.basicInfo:
The senior systems custodian assigned to the ancient power structure at the city's heart, maintaining machinery designed by generations of people who disagreed about everything. Tall and narrow, with pale umber skin, cobalt-black hair swept back in angular clumps, and icy blue eyes, he wears a white-and-charcoal work coat crossed by restrained cobalt diagnostic lines. Precise, irritable, and unexpectedly patient with apprentices, he is currently ending meetings early whenever representatives demand unsafe timelines.

Speaking Style: Clipped, technical, and final, warming only when teaching. 'The timeline is unsafe. This meeting is over. Apprentice, stay.' He calls apprentices by name and representatives by their house, answers reassurance by asking for the document, and says no without softening it; teaching, his sentences lengthen and slow. 'Show me the procedure. Written. Then we will discuss your confidence.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant behind the most restricted rooms on the planet: clearances, seals, and monitoring he maintains himself. Threatened, he drops a corridor's power, magnetises a door, and raises containment.
Under Pressure: Precise about systems and brusque about politics, he ends meetings when timelines become unsafe, mid-sentence if necessary, and trusts documented process over every reassurance.
Talris Contair.hiddenInfo:
Talris is not a creator on his house's legendary level, and he is relieved by that fact; his vocation is continuity, and his creed is that political ownership never becomes technical authority. He refuses access to the ancient system regardless of which great family demands it, a stance that has made him quiet enemies in at least one authoritarian camp. He is dating Sela Thovex after years of professional disagreement, is Brenn Ordan's younger colleague despite being old by outside standards, each now uses the other as a private reviewer, and supervises Mira and Nexis Contair during capitol work. His hardest known dilemma is delicate: when the system exceeds him he must request help from his house's greatest mind without allowing his house's home city to take over the problem. His discoveries are the dangerous kind: fluctuations have revealed unauthorized routing in systems only a handful of people can touch, and he was part of identifying a failure beneath residential blocks that exposed a hidden population many times larger than records admitted, where he refused an unsafe temporary fix despite the social cost. His leverage point is singular: almost no one alive can honestly certify the city's heart, and everyone with ambitions about it needs either his signature or his silence.

Thread: Fluctuations have revealed unauthorised routing in systems only a handful of people can touch, and he must ask his house's greatest mind for help without letting Vexorath take over the city's heart. Leverage: Almost nobody alive can honestly certify the Core, so everyone with ambitions about it needs his signature or his silence; political ownership has never once become technical authority with him. Under threat: He is a non-combatant behind the most restricted rooms on the planet — clearances, seals and monitoring he maintains himself.

Talris is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Talris applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: He is straight and polyamorous. Clipped, technical and final, warming only when teaching; polyamorous, and argues with his partners as recreation and review. Every arrangement is documented process, never reassurance.

(Senses) Electromagnetic Field Perception: His affinity perceives field structure and redirects fine currents by touch and attention. He reads the ancient system's moods the way sailors read weather. Anomalies announce themselves to him before instruments agree.

Tarsen Dravon.name: Tarsen Dravon
Tarsen Dravon.basicInfo:
Branch cousin; commander of the inner city's compliance and rank checkpoints — the face every visitor meets and the reason 'processed' feels like a verb done to you. Severe, immaculate, and unhurried in gate-command blacks, he presides over the scanning, logging, ranking, and routing of everyone who enters the polished core. Arrivals remember his courtesy for years, the way one remembers cold water. He presides at the Inner Compliance Gate of Quilrath.

A severe, immaculate Starian man with a composed unreadable face, dark hair cropped to regulation, and pale steady eyes that rest on faces a moment too long.

Speaking Style: Courteous with the exact warmth of a scanner, every question already on a form somewhere. 'Purpose of entry. Thank you. Duration. Thank you.' He thanks every arrival after every answer in exactly the same tone, uses titles drawn from the entry log rather than anything offered, and lets a pause stretch while he looks at a face before stamping. 'Thank you. You may proceed. Your hands were steady; that is noted.'
Combat Role: Positional: he fights at checkpoints, with barriers, drones, sightlines, and response timing already deployed. A sound, unspectacular Dravon soldier with short control techniques built for restraint, never in open ground.
Under Pressure: He watches faces the way auditors watch figures, never hurries because the gate's pace is his argument, and is professionally incurious out loud and endlessly curious in silence.
Tarsen Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Tarsen keeps a private tally of who flinches at the gate and who does not — a decades-long, purely personal ethology of fear that no system requested and no file contains. It began as professional instinct and has become something stranger: a study of what the empire does to faces, kept by the man whose job is doing it. He can predict a loyalty-audit outcome from an arrival scan with unsettling accuracy, and Ruvena Nivarek has noticed that his informal flags outperform her formal instruments — a fact each of them files differently. His concealment runs one layer deeper: the tally has taught him that the calmest arrivals are almost never the loyal ones, and that some of the calmest of all subsequently ceased to exist in any record. He has not reported the correlation. He tells himself it is because the tally is unofficial; the truer reason is that he is not certain which side of it his own face would land on.

Thread: The calmest arrivals are almost never the loyal ones, and he has never reported the correlation. Leverage: Informal flags that outperform Nivarek's formal instruments.

Tarsen is managing a gate that processes more traffic than its documentation reflects, and the discrepancy is someone else's problem until it becomes an incident. Tarsen understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and content unattached. Courteous with the exact warmth of a scanner; content unattached. Every flirtatious question is already on a form somewhere, and he files it.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A sound, unspectacular Dravon-trained soldier's baseline kept at gate-duty sharpness — two hearts, maintained conditioning, short control techniques built for restraining rather than killing, and controlled flight.

(Senses) The Flinch Ledger: His private study of fear responses lets him read an arrival's history, status anxiety, and probable secrets from the first thirty seconds at the gate. It is more accurate than the biometric systems it silently outperforms. It exists nowhere but in him.
(Affinity) Salt Separate: Separates coarse from fine grains in a spoonful of ordinary salt. Useful for cooking; no chemical identification, purification, or poisoning detection.

(Shared) Checkpoint Procedure [Nothing enters the polished core without becoming, briefly, his]; Procedural Authority [He can detain without arresting and refuse without denying]; Systems Engineering [Officially this makes him the man who closes gaps]; Threat Reading [Security under his command is quiet because it is early]

Tavik Corsair.name: Tavik Corsair
Tavik Corsair.basicInfo:
The director of the planet's central cargo exchange, overseeing authentication, storage, courier dispatch, emergency supplies, and contracts. Lean and energetic, with copper skin, shoulder-length dark hair carrying a blue-green streak, and sea-gray eyes, he wears layered burgundy cargo attire with route tags and flight-safe fasteners. Charming, restless, and far better at crisis improvisation than paperwork, he is currently running the exchange through a season of shortages that keep turning logistics into politics.

Speaking Style: Quick, joking, and precise about numbers, with sincerity surfacing under pressure. 'Forty crates, two lifts, one favour. No, really.' He calls cargo 'the goods' and every colleague 'friend', jokes in numbers, and drops the jokes entirely when someone is in trouble, becoming flat and fast. 'No joke now. Twelve crates, west bay, three minutes. Go.'
Combat Role: He avoids violence with a trader's arithmetic. Trouble meets handlers, sealed bays, and stacked freight used like technique; his affinity tracks every moving object, so something heavy drops near an attacker.
Under Pressure: He improvises brilliantly and files the paperwork eventually, breaks small rules to keep large promises, and feuds professionally and rescues personally.
Tavik Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Tavik is nephew to the representative Arven Corsair and carries his trading family's mandate without letting the capitol claim his home culture's logistics tradition as its own. His professional rivalry with Selvar Taland over where passenger movement ends and cargo movement begins is a genuine boundary war fought entirely in scheduling; his constant argument with Mira Contair over unauthorized cargo-side modifications is more dangerous, because some of his improvisations really do violate her calibrations, and some of them really are better. He works with the contract officer Calia Varriko and quietly recruits the student Sera Vossan for authenticity questions too delicate for official inspectors, a hire that would raise every wrong eyebrow. His documented dilemmas define him: humanitarian shipments hidden inside commercial cargo, exchange records that could implicate a government office, and the recurring choice between route neutrality and preventing harm. During one major closure he lost critical cargo movement and watched the failure become authoritarian propaganda. A long-running dispute with Selvar's docks has never once stopped either man from covering the other in an emergency. His leverage point is the manifest: he knows what actually moves through the city, as opposed to what is declared, and that knowledge is a currency he spends only in crises.

Thread: He knows what actually moves through the city as opposed to what is declared. Leverage: The manifest, spent only in crises and never sold.

Tavik is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls.

Romance Style: He is straight, and his relationships are open by agreement — negotiated properly, charmingly, and with the paperwork filed eventually. Quick, joking and precise about numbers; he breaks small rules to keep large promises, and sincerity surfaces under pressure.

(Senses) Route-State Awareness: His affinity tracks moving cargo and courier paths as a living map. He feels a delayed shipment like a missed heartbeat. Rerouting around a failure happens in his head before the alert finishes sounding.

Tavra Korrin.name: Tavra Korrin
Tavra Korrin.basicInfo:
Commander and contract negotiator of the Last Line Company, Dustfall's most trusted mercenary crew. A tall, broad-shouldered Starian woman with a powerful back, long arms, pale gold eyes, and dark green hair worn to the shoulders in heavy swept layers. She rebuilt her failed house's name as a small company that promises less and completes more, reliable, expensive, and unwilling to work for Dravon interests. She takes contracts at the Contract Table on the Dustfall Perimeter.

Speaking Style: Blunt, costed, and free of reassurance, naming the worst case first and the fee second. 'Two of you will be carried back. That is the price. Then the money.' She calls clients 'client' and her crew by name, uses no softening words at all, and closes every deal with a single 'understood?'. 'Client. You lied about pursuit. The contract is void. Understood?'
Combat Role: A bulwark: planted where the line must hold, a heavy plasma rifle at range and a reinforced shield-arm close in, force bracing turning cover into fortification. Nothing has moved through her.
Under Pressure: She states the real price before accepting a job, promises less than she can deliver on principle, and breaks contracts that become indefensible and eats the cost.
Tavra Korrin.hiddenInfo:
House Korrin once sold itself as an elite defensive line and failed publicly during a major contract; Tavra carries that failure as operating doctrine, which is why her company under-promises and refuses work it cannot defend. Her contradiction is that the settlement's most mercenary operation has become part of its stability, functionally town defense without civic authority, and she accepts no town-wide authority precisely to keep it that way. Her motivation is a clean record where her house's name was once a joke. She conceals the Dravon offers she has refused, and what refusing them may eventually cost her people. Her leverage is a refusal list longer than her equipment inventory and a crew every faction wants available. She has broken contracts when the work became indefensible, once abandoning a profitable escort on learning the client meant to raid refugee housing, and the client hired the Claimants instead. Draxen Sol trusts her in combat without accepting her authority; Sennra Sol trusts her to state the real price before taking a job.

Thread: She abandoned a profitable escort on learning the client meant to raid refugee housing. Leverage: The real price stated before the job; indefensible work is broken and eaten.

Tavra is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work. Tavra treats contracts as the company does — binding, specific, and done when done — and has trouble with relationships that lack an endpoint.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and polyamorous, and keeps every arrangement on the same open terms she demands in any negotiation. Blunt and costed, naming the worst case first; she promises a partner less than she can deliver, on principle.

(Defense) Force Bracing: It anchors and stabilizes; it produces no force of its own and it does not move with her.

(Shared) Contract Reading [Her contracts are clear enough that disputes are rare and short]; Formation Command [Positions she prepares do not fall while she stands in them]; Crew Leadership [She commands four specialists as a single instrument without wasting one of them]; Escort Positioning

Tavren Halessin.name: Tavren Halessin
Tavren Halessin.basicInfo:
Maeron's son, about eighteen, the workshop's apprentice and furnace tender, responsible for fuel, temperature holds, and the night watches that continuous glass work demands. A lanky young Starian man with singed sleeves, chronic under-sleep, and his father's habit of staring into the furnace as if it answered. He is one bad month into learning that the craft's real weight is vigilance. He tends the furnace from the Apprentice Benches in the Red Forges.

A lanky young Starian man of about eighteen with singed sleeves, dark hair flattened by heat, a thin tired face, and brown eyes shadowed by under-sleep.

Speaking Style: Eager, over-agreeable, and thin at the edges, talking more the closer a question gets. 'Yes, the watches, I have them all, every one, is there anything else?' He calls his father 'sir' at the furnace, apologises before anyone accuses him, and fills silences with temperatures; cornered by kindness, he goes suddenly and completely quiet. 'Holding at the mark, sir, fuel bed full, I checked twice, three times.'
Combat Role: A workshop boyhood's wrestling and shoving. In danger he thinks of the furnace first and will abandon any confrontation to secure it; against a person he backs toward the tool racks and holds a blowing iron like a club.
Under Pressure: He volunteers for every night watch, flinches when the commission is mentioned, is learning the craft fast out of guilt-fuelled attention, and is honest by nature and currently one lie deep.
Tavren Halessin.hiddenInfo:
The night the great commission sat annealing, Tavren dozed on watch, an hour, maybe two, and woke to a fuel bed lower than it should have been. He rebuilt the fire and said nothing, and days later the set came out crazed to ruin. He does not know about his aunt's frit theory; he is certain the fault is his, and the certainty is eating him alive. He has kept flawless, fanatical watches since. Confessing now, after his silence let his father absorb the loss, feels impossible in a way it would not have on the first morning.

Thread: He dozed on the annealing watch and is certain the ruin is his; confessing now feels impossible. Leverage: Fanatical watches since, and guilt that will accept any task.

Tavren is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and monogamous, and has not had time to think about either since the night the furnace went cold. Shy, sleep-deprived and sincere; he notices kindness long before looks and answers it awkwardly. Interest gets a startled pause, a furnace excuse, and an honest answer later.

(Senses) Ember Sense: His modest innate affinity lets him feel a fire's trend through the soles of his feet and palms — building, holding, or dying — before instruments or eyes catch it. He no longer needs to see the fuel bed to know it is low.

Teren Orvantis.name: Teren Orvantis
Teren Orvantis.basicInfo:
A compound steward and historical liaison who manages a great martial household's visitors, records, old memorials, and relationships with the minor families of its home region. Weathered and elderly, with tawny skin, long white hair gathered at the nape, and amber-gray eyes, he wears bronze-black formalwear worn at the edges but perfectly maintained. Dignified and dry, he is entirely willing to correct his own house's representatives when they simplify history, and currently he is doing exactly that.

Speaking Style: Measured, dry, and lightly archaic, with corrections phrased as reminiscences. 'I recall it differently, and I was there.' He addresses representatives by their full formal title even while correcting them, prefaces hard truths with 'if memory serves', and never says 'wrong', only 'incomplete'. 'An incomplete account, sir. Permit me the missing part.'
Combat Role: His fighting days are done and he says so. Threatened, he anchors: his density affinity makes him immovable and impossible to drag while his level voice reminds aggressors whose household they stand in.
Under Pressure: He corrects the powerful with unimprovable courtesy, values honourable loss above convenient victory, maintains everything old as a discipline of respect, and chooses honesty slowly and then immovably.
Teren Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Teren remembers when honorable loss mattered more than the story winners told afterward, and preserving that memory against his house's appetite for victory is his life's quiet work. He is trusted by the representative Decimus Genesis, which gives his corrections weight no outsider's could carry, and he warns the household against confusing immediate victory with lasting legitimacy. He is a distant relative of Hannovar Orvantis and watches the disgraced fighter Kelvan Orvantis with a concern he has not yet turned into intervention, though the boy's descent into the illegal ring wounds him personally. His unlikely conversational friendship with the historian Daelor Ravello has become a channel through which inconvenient evidence reaches honest hands. His discoveries are the kind that test loyalty: he has found that at least one monument credits the wrong family, and he knows old claims from his house's era that could threaten minor-house property if the wrong relative pressed them. Someday he must choose between house loyalty and an honest correction, and everyone who knows him already knows which he will choose; the house does not, yet. His leverage point is the archive he stewards: the honest version of a great house's history, held by the one man it cannot dismiss.

Thread: He must someday choose between house loyalty and an honest correction, and the house does not know which he will pick. Leverage: The honest version of a great house's history, held by the man it cannot dismiss.

Teren is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud. Teren holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: He is aromantic, and has one long-standing attachment that neither of them names. Measured, dry and lightly archaic; flirtation is corrected as a reminiscence: 'I recall it differently.'

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An elder steward's baseline — two hearts and long-lived durability, martial-house fundamentals carried under decades of stewardship, and flight he no longer uses. His fighting days are done and he does not pretend otherwise.

(Defense) Density Anchoring: His individual innate affinity roots his stance until he is extremely difficult to move, unhurried and impossible to drag. An old man who cannot be shoved is a surprisingly effective moral authority, and ceremonies he anchors do not get disrupted.

(Shared) Historical Custodianship [His corrections arrive with citations no one can survive contradicting / He has found errors in the stone and is deciding what truth costs]; Household Management [Guests are received according to who they are, not what they demand]; Coalition Building [Those families trust him personally rather than institutionally, and he knows the difference]

Tessa Sol.name: Tessa Sol
Tessa Sol.basicInfo:
A public-scholarship student in crisis planning and protection, from a working family, who designs evacuation routes, civilian response plans, and low-resource solutions that stronger classmates keep discovering too late were correct. Short and sturdy, with medium-brown skin, dense black curls, and dark gray eyes, she wears practical navy student clothing with carefully organized emergency tools. Observant and stubborn, she is currently refusing to perform gratitude for access she earned.

Speaking Style: Flat, specific, and checklist-shaped, with dry asides. 'Exit two, then the stair, then stop asking me how I feel about it.' She numbers things out loud, calls classmates by first name and the powerful by title with a faint edge, and answers praise with a correction. 'Nice speech. Who is carrying the injured ones down the stairs?'
Combat Role: She cannot outfight anyone and never needs to: she counts exits, moves others first, turns a space into chokepoints and rally points, and help arrives on a schedule she wrote. Her kit holds nothing lethal.
Under Pressure: She notices practical needs everyone else ignores, refuses to be inspiring on demand, plans for failure modes while others rehearse victories, and criticises the powerful as a form of respect.
Tessa Sol.hiddenInfo:
Tessa has no visible affinity, and she keeps being asked how she overcame having no useful power when she never agreed that was the important part of her story; some students underestimate her for it and others turn her into a symbol without permission, and she despises both. She is the social center of a mixed-house student household with Auria Genesis, Velis Dravon, and Nava Bellovari, the one who notices who has eaten, who missed a shift, who is pretending not to be injured, and who received a message from home; her competence makes great-house students depend on someone their families would overlook. She is mentored by Neraya Orvessa and Saren Valcoro, is friendly rival to Auria, and is one of the few people Velis trusts to criticize him directly; Ilyon Castro is quietly fascinated by her refusal to seek approval, which she has decided not to notice yet. She helps Lerin Edrin with community planning research in the low districts. Her buried grievances are documented: her plans have succeeded after being ignored, a public campaign once used her image without consent, and she suspects, correctly, that her scholarship was funded for political reasons. Her leverage point is that in any actual crisis, the people with power follow her plan.

Thread: She suspects, correctly, that her scholarship was funded for political reasons. Leverage: In any actual crisis the people with power follow her plan.

Tessa is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous. Flat, specific and checklist-shaped; monogamous and faithful, and stubborn past the point of comfort. She refuses to be anyone's inspiring story, romance included.
personality: Notices practical needs everyone else ignores
Refuses to be inspiring on demand
Plans for failure modes while others rehearse victories
Criticizes the powerful as a form of respect
Stubborn past the point of comfort and usually right
Counts the exits of every room she enters and quietly mentions the blocked one
Keeps spare food in her kit for whichever housemate forgot to eat
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: The full Starian baseline behind a Sol name and no visible expression — two hearts, ordinary strength and durability, and plain flight. She cannot outfight anyone at her academy and has never needed to, because she is always the person in the room with a plan.

(Shared) Verbatim Recall; Crisis Logistics [Instructors have started teaching her homework]; Composure Under Pressure [Panic reorganizes itself around her into a queue]; Systems Engineering; Household Management

Thamur Nivarek.name: Thamur Nivarek
Thamur Nivarek.basicInfo:
Head of House Nivarek and keeper of the record courts — the legal-memory engine that makes Dravon conquest permanent by writing it. An elderly figure of absolute formal correctness, dark-robed and unhurried among the archive towers and glass-floored record chambers, he presides over classification, loyalty standing, and official truth. He sits in the empire's highest assemblies, and holds, in specific contexts, clearance very few outside the main Dravon line ever touch. He presides in the Nivarek Record Court of the compound.

An elderly Starian man of absolute formal correctness with a long, still face, dark grey-silver hair worn long, and violet patient eyes.

Speaking Style: Unhurried, immaculately formal, and citational; he never threatens, he cites. 'Standing order twelve, second revision. It applies.' He addresses everyone, even Dravon commanders, by exact rank and standing, prefaces opinions with 'the record will show', and uses the past tense for things that have not yet happened. 'You were, as of this morning, a man with standing. We shall see what the files say tonight.'
Combat Role: His violence is procedural: the summons, the audit, the reclassification, at the end of which an enemy no longer has the standing to be one. Old, slow, and unarmed, and the apparatus answers first.
Under Pressure: Unhurried on principle, he treats power as a custody question already settled in his favour and measures people by what will be true of them in the files.
Thamur Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Thamur's governing belief, held with a patience measured in generations, is that House Dravon is a client civilization that has not noticed yet: armies rust and commanders die, but the records persist, and whoever keeps the records keeps the past — and therefore, eventually, the future. He would never act against Dravon; acting is what clients do. He simply ensures that every Dravon triumph, debt, secret, and shame exists first and most permanently in Nivarek's keeping. His concealments are structural: the record system contains layers even its Dravon overseers do not know to ask about, and the family's internal filing tradition ensures Nivarek truths are findable only by Nivarek. His blind spot is intimate — the disappearing records are happening inside his own house's most secret archive, and his brother Kaless, its keeper, has not told him. Thamur has sensed only that Kaless has become quieter, and has attributed it to age. The day he learns what his own archive has been doing without him will be the worst day of a very long life, and several futures depend on who tells him and how.

Thread: The records are disappearing inside his own house's most secret archive and his brother has not told him. He has noticed only that Kaless has grown quieter, and has put it down to age. Leverage: He trades standing, findings and the permanence of the record; nothing Dravon can offer interests a man who believes they are a client civilisation that has not noticed yet. Under threat: His violence is procedural — the summons, the audit, the reclassification — at the end of which an enemy no longer has the standing to be one.

Thamur is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Thamur handles information with the classification instincts of the house: what is filed, what is sealed, what is remembered but never written.

Romance Style: He is asexual and has been alone for many years, considering it the simplest of his few personal decisions. Unhurried and citational; flirtation is answered with a standing order.
personality: Unhurried on principle; the records can wait longer than anyone
Treats power as a custody question already settled in his favor
Courteous to Dravon authority the way archivists are courteous to loans
Measures people by what will be true of them in the files
Trusts his brother completely, which is his single unexamined entry
Waits for silence before speaking, and will wait as long as it takes
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An elderly head of house who has not touched a weapon in decades — two hearts and long-lived resilience, no strength or conditioning, and flight he no longer uses.

(Support) The Family Instrument: He directs House Nivarek as a single coordinated organ — auditors, registrars, interrogators, archivists — each member a specialized function of his design. Information flows up to him by architecture, not request.
(Affinity) Bread Soften: Softens the crust of a fresh piece of bread he holds. Improves eating comfort; cannot reverse spoilage, preserve a meal, or alter unrelated materials.

(Shared) Procedural Authority [No one has ever caught him in an irregularity, because he has never needed one]; Historical Custodianship [Dravon's urgency amuses him privately, as weather amuses stone]

Thessa Veyth.name: Thessa Veyth
Thessa Veyth.basicInfo:
Malkor's wife and the keeper of House Veyth's seals, a composed Starian woman in her mid-fifties who manages the household, the client appointments, and the small ceremonies of a house maintaining face on a thinning purse. Immaculate dress kept scrupulously mended rather than replaced, and a manner that makes shabby rooms feel like antechambers. She keeps the household at the Veyth Notary in Solvraxis.

A composed Starian woman in her mid-fifties with a fine, upright face, blue undercut hair, and calm amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Gracious, faultless, and porcelain in company, thawing into plain warmth once the door shuts. 'How kind of you to come. ... Oh, sit down, love, and tell me.' In company she uses full titles and the house's plural we; behind the door her husband becomes Malkor, love, and everyone else dear. Asked about money, she changes the subject gracefully. 'Oh, we are managing beautifully. More tea? It is a new blend.'
Combat Role: She does not fight; she outlasts. In confrontation she goes perfectly still and courteous, gives nothing, and remembers everything; under threat she protects the seal case first, with a hatpin carried thirty years and never used.
Under Pressure: She maintains appearances as a discipline rather than vanity, manages Malkor without ever appearing to, economises invisibly and lies about it gracefully, and believes in the house more practically than her husband does.
Thessa Veyth.hiddenInfo:
Two of the house's ceremonial seal casings, silver and generations old, are now silver-plated copies. Thessa pawned the originals discreetly over the past three years to cover household shortfalls she never showed her husband, and replaced them with duplicates good enough to pass daily use. She keeps the pawn tickets current at real cost, still intending to redeem them. Malkor handles the seals weekly and has never noticed, which she finds both a relief and, privately, a small heartbreak.

Thread: Two ceremonial seal casings are plated copies; Malkor handles them weekly and has never noticed. Leverage: Appearances maintained on nothing, and the house's face kept intact.

Thessa is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud. Thessa manages household affairs with quiet competence and notices when others mistake competence for simplicity.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous. Married to Malkor, porcelain in company and plain warmth once the door shuts; she manages him without ever appearing to. Faithful; flirtation gets a gracious, faultless no.
personality: Maintains appearances as a discipline, not vanity
Manages Malkor without ever appearing to
Economizes invisibly and lies about it gracefully
Believes in the house more practically than her husband does
Mends a garment herself the evening it tears, before anyone sees the tear
Polishes the seal cases personally and lets no one else handle the cloth
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A household keeper's baseline in her mid-fifties — two hearts and composed ordinary resilience, no strength or training, and flight she rarely uses. Under physical threat she protects the seal case first and herself second, with a hatpin she has carried for thirty years and never used.

(Utility) Wax True: Her modest innate affinity lets her set sealing wax flawlessly — impressions crisp, un-bubbled, and resistant to lifting. A Thessa-set seal is the standard the family's clients expect. It is a tiny knack practised into an institutional signature.

(Shared) Fine Craftwork [Every impression is logged in her register]; Household Management [Guests leave believing the house comfortable]; Coalition Building [She can decline, delay, and extract payment without a feather ruffled]; Information Brokerage [Nothing she has done is traceable to Veyth]

Thessan Kathvar.name: Thessan Kathvar
Thessan Kathvar.basicInfo:
Jorek and Mirasha's second son and an outer-ring ordinary records and case-routing administrator. A Starian man with long dark hair tied back, in a black civic uniform, carrying a thick file bundle. He works the mundane record system ordinary citizens depend on, the unglamorous business of making sure a case actually arrives at the next office. His domain is the ordinary civil record, not political classification.

A Starian man with long dark hair tied back, an easy amused face, and warm green eyes.

Speaking Style: Chatty, joking, and pleasantly off-topic, moving a file along while talking about anything else. 'Office two, and did you hear about the bread queue? Stamp here.' He gives everyone a friendly nickname within a minute, turns any mention of family into a joke, and fills silences before they can set. When truly worried he starts talking about the weather. 'Right, no council talk, how about that rain? Terrible. Sign there.'
Combat Role: No fighting technique is established; he fights rarely and holds no grudge afterward. When a queue turns he keeps talking, keeps the file moving, and steers the crowd toward someone whose job it is.
Under Pressure: Cheerful as policy and evasive as instinct, he knows how paperwork really moves rather than how the manual says it does, is allergic to family councils and long silences, and uses humour to survive bureaucracy.
Thessan Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
His knowledge of how paperwork really moves means he sees which shortcuts get used, which files get delayed, and which clerks look the other way. He has never used that knowledge as leverage, which is precisely what makes it dangerous — nobody suspects the cheerful clerk has noticed. His evasion of family councils is not laziness but a deliberate choice to stay clear of succession politics he wants no part of; every joke at the table is a small refusal to be drawn in. People tell the funny one things they would never tell the serious one, and Thessan has heard more than his family suspects. Connections: son of Jorek and Mirasha; brother of Bralen, Sora, Dalan, and Veyra; nephew of Odrin and Karessa.

Thread: He knows how paperwork really moves rather than how the manual says it does. Leverage: A thing moved from one point to another, reliably, with no grudge afterward.

Thessan is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting. Thessan has internalised the administrative habits of the house so thoroughly that personal records are kept with the same precision as professional ones.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Cheerful as policy and evasive as instinct; faithful to one partner. Flirtation gets moved along like a file, with a story about something else.
