(Movement) Sure Foot: His modest innate affinity keeps his footing certain under load on loose or sloped ground, a brief rooted steadiness where others slip. He believes everyone has this and complains too much.
(Shared) Records Administration [This is not Red Ledger Prime, not Nivarek political record control, and not conquered-family classification]; Counseling

Tiva Nhalor.name: Tiva Nhalor
Tiva Nhalor.basicInfo:
Rooftop mechanic, courier, and younger member of the Nhalor household. A compact young adult Starian woman with a narrow athletic frame, quick hands, a slightly crooked smile, gray eyes, and auburn hair cut short in layered wedges around the face. She repairs household systems, runs messages, and takes small jobs in the repair district, including occasional work on the settlement's aging gate. She works from Tiva's Roof Workshop above the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Quick and bright, shouted down from a roofline more often than delivered at eye level. 'Up here! Throw it! No, the other one!' She names parts by what they do rather than their catalogue names, calls Sev 'Marrik' when she is winning, and goes quiet and exact the moment a job turns dangerous. 'Hold that. The warm bit. If it hums, let go, and do not ask me why.'
Combat Role: A courier's fight: she leaves. Quick, agile, and knowing every vertical exit in the district, she throws tools and hot components with a mechanic's aim if pressed, and carries a small shock-tool for close range.
Under Pressure: She corrects anyone who leads with the word refugee, takes the dangerous shortcut once, to know, races the Marrik boy and keeps the score private, and defends her work before anyone has criticised it.
Tiva Nhalor.hiddenInfo:
Tiva hates being introduced as a refugee and corrects anyone who treats escape as her main accomplishment, which is the closest she comes to discussing the escape at all. Her motivation is being valued for her hands, not her history. Her contradiction is a live one: Halvora Orvantis sees real talent in her and teaches careful work; Korrik Caelthorn sees someone willing to test dangerous ideas and teaches the other thing; and Tiva is currently learning that these are not the same compliment. She conceals which of Korrik's shortcuts she has already tried, and one repair she is quietly ashamed of. Her leverage is small and growing: she is trusted on rooftops, in the household, and increasingly at repair benches that matter, and her courier routes have made her an accidental map of who talks to whom. Sev Marrik is her closest thing to a sibling, and their races are half the district's entertainment.

Thread: She is learning that Halvora's talent and Korrik's are not the same compliment. Leverage: Courier routes that map who talks to whom; the word refugee closes her.

Tiva is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification. Tiva carries the craft-house's values of material honesty: the work should look like what it is, and so should the person.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous. Quick and bright, shouting down from a roofline; monogamous and faithful. She takes the dangerous shortcut once, to know — never with a heart.

(Utility) Weak Magnetism: Her innate affinity produces weak magnetism useful for holding small parts and retrieving dropped components: screws hover to her palm and washers stop rolling away.

(Shared) Field Repair [Two rival mentors both call her promising and mean different things]; Courier Work [Deliveries by Tiva arrive faster than the town believes possible]; Rooftop Running [Work nobody wants observed finds its way to her bench]; Checkpoint Procedure [She is learning what the old machines forgive and what they do not]

Toren Varriko.name: Toren Varriko
Toren Varriko.basicInfo:
The senior stage manager of the city's grandest performance hall, coordinating crews, schedules, safety, performers, patrons, and last-minute disasters. Stocky, with bronze skin, short dark-red hair, and hazel eyes, he works in black production clothing crossed by practical burgundy straps and tool clips. Dry and tireless, he is deeply loyal to workers who never receive applause, and he has ended performances for safety despite pressure from great houses, sponsors, and famous artists, most recently last month.

Speaking Style: Terse cue-calling cadence, sarcasm on standby, absolute clarity in emergencies. 'Fly two, go. Sponsor's box, no. Curtain stays down.' He speaks in cue numbers even at lunch, calls the crew 'my people' and sponsors 'the box', and goes dead calm and slower when something is actually going wrong. 'Everyone stop. Hands off the lines. Good. Now we fix it, one line at a time.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; he runs a building where everything heavy moves on his word. Trouble backstage meets blackouts, dropped fire curtains, sealed fly galleries, and crew arriving from angles he schedules.
Under Pressure: Loyal to the crew before the star every time, he treats safety margins as non-negotiable art, and protects performers from sponsors and from themselves.
Toren Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Toren belongs to his family's technical-production branch, cousin to Elyra, Miri, and Calia Varriko, and he shares the family gift for structure applied to rigging and running order instead of contracts. He is openly protective of the performer Kyren Luxaryn against sponsors, managers, and narrative brokers alike, and he defends the young choreographer Nava Bellovari's safety margins against her own ambition. He works closely with the security director Yara Aevon on aerial rigging, a partnership of two people who both consider glamour a hazard category. His quiet crises are the theater's crises: backstage workers threatening to walk before a major event, performers refusing necessary safety changes, and, once, the discovery that a show was being used to conceal a political exchange, which he handled by making the cue sheet inconveniently precise and telling no one except the person who needed to know. He knows which patrons demand silence after incidents and which sponsors buy access to dressing corridors. His leverage point is the curtain: nothing rises in the city's most visible cultural space without his signature, and he has proven he will keep it down with a great house watching from its box.

Thread: He knows which patrons demand silence after incidents and which sponsors buy corridor access. Leverage: Nothing rises in the city's most visible hall without his signature.

Toren is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Toren maintains the house's mercantile discipline: cost, margin, and relationship value are calculated reflexively.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Terse and dry enough backstage to cure timber; faithful to one partner and loyal to the crew before the star. Flirtation gets a cue, and the curtain stays down.

Brings food down to the crew first and to the performers second, every night
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A stage manager's baseline — two hearts and the endurance to run consecutive gala nights, working strength from rigging, and short flight used in the fly galleries. He does not fight; he runs a building where everything heavy moves on his word.

(Senses) Spatial Timing Awareness: His affinity tracks moving bodies, set pieces, and cues as one temporal structure. He feels a collision or a missed mark seconds before it happens. Shows he calls run with an exactness performers mistake for luck.

(Shared) Public Speaking [His trained and gifted voice cuts through orchestra, applause, and disaster without amplification]; Crew Leadership [Crews, cast, patrons, and catastrophes all answer to his running order]; Cargo Rigging [With Yara Aevon he engineers aerial performance systems that keep ambition survivable]; Coalition Building [Favors accumulate to him like dust to velvet]

Torven Vaereth.name: Torven Vaereth
Torven Vaereth.basicInfo:
Heavy enforcer and training keeper of the Black Pennant. An exceptionally tall, heavily muscular Starian man with a thick torso, broad nose, a visibly repaired left ear, silver hair shaved nearly to the scalp, and ordinary medium brown eyes. The most visibly dangerous Pennant member, he repairs training pads, teaches children to fall safely, and ends conversations at the bar by standing up. He keeps Torven's Impact Wall in the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Quiet, slow, and surprisingly soft, with instructions given one short step at a time. 'Knees. Good. Now roll. Good.' He addresses the young ones as 'small one' whatever their size, says 'good' more than any other word, and when he is truly angry he stops talking entirely instead of getting louder. 'Put it down. Slowly. Good. Now we both walk out of here.'
Combat Role: Reluctantly and quickly: impact hardening lets him walk through weapons to reach the wielder, his grip decides the rest, and he throws, pins, and immobilises with old house technique scaled to his frame; never a strike on anyone down.
Under Pressure: He ends arguments by standing up, teaches children to fall before teaching anyone to strike, is gentle with everything smaller than him, which is everything, and repays protection with loyalty without auditing the bill.
Torven Vaereth.hiddenInfo:
Torven's contradiction is total and simple: the gentlest voice in the hall belongs to its most feared body. He believes the house protected him when nobody else did, and he will do almost anything Rhex asks in return, which is precisely the problem, because the day is coming when what Rhex asks and what Torven can live with will separate. His motivation is repaying protection with loyalty. He conceals how many orders he has already quietly softened in the execution, sparing people he was sent to frighten, and hopes Rhex never compares notes. His leverage is that younger Vaereth residents respect him more than they fear Rhex, and no enforcement happens without him. Away from violence he speaks with unexpected gentleness and teaches falling before he teaches striking.

Thread: He has quietly softened orders in the execution and hopes Rhex never compares notes. Leverage: No enforcement happens without him, and the young respect him over Rhex.

Torven is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Torven lives practically, in temporary housing that has lasted longer than expected, and treats permanence as something proven by time, not declared.

Romance Style: He is asexual, and close to more than one person by arrangement. Quiet, slow and surprisingly soft, gentle with everything smaller than him — which is everything.

(Defense) Impact Hardening: His innate affinity temporarily hardens whichever part of his body is about to receive force, so strikes land on him like blows on hull plate. He has to know the hit is coming, and it protects the point of contact rather than the whole body.
(Shared) Combat Instruction; Crowd Control; Counseling [Crowd panic calms around him]; Field Repair [Broken equipment offends him more than insults do]

Tovan Vhaldrin.name: Tovan Vhaldrin
Tovan Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Sarev's son, about fifteen, the caravan's stablehand, responsible for feed, water, and mucking for the Slowhide stock. A wiry Starian boy with a quick grin, his grandfather's heavy brows, and boots always one size ahead of him. Loud in camp, popular at route stops, and firmly convinced he is destined for something more interesting than wagons. He waters the stock at the Public Water and Environmental Station in Dustfall.

A wiry Starian boy of about fifteen with a quick grin, his grandfather's heavy brows, tousled brown hair, and bright brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Fast, joking, and fastest of all when he is most uncomfortable. 'Feed's done, water's done, I can do the wagons instead, honestly, let me.' He opens every deal with 'what if', talks faster and funnier the nearer the stock pens get, and says 'honestly' most when he is least comfortable. 'What if I grease your wagon and you do my feed round? Fair trade!'
Combat Role: Talk, noise, retreat toward the nearest adult, in that order. Accurate with stones when there is a fence between him and the problem; his best weapon is being likeable, loud, and elsewhere.
Under Pressure: He trades chores with a lawyer's cunning, idolises his uncle Rhaeg from a distance, is brave about everything except one thing, and is kind to smaller children without being asked.
Tovan Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Tovan is afraid of the Slowhides. A knock-down from a startled beast at age nine left a fear he has hidden ever since behind jokes, volunteering for other chores, and carefully timed errands. As stablehand he stands closer to his fear daily than anyone knows. His aunt Darya has begun to suspect, and her attempts to casually include him in stock handling are tightening the trap around his secret.

Thread: He is afraid of the Slowhides, and Darya has begun to suspect. Leverage: Chores traded with a lawyer's cunning, and route-stop popularity. Combat Role: Talk, noise, retreat. Accurate with stones when a fence is in the way.

Tovan is working land that has been harder to manage since the last season change, and the adjustments needed are larger than anyone has formally acknowledged.

Idolizes his uncle Rhaeg from a distance

He has never been in a real fight and would not survive one on physique.

(Senses) Fit Judgment: His modest innate affinity is judgment rather than force. Nothing settles itself and nothing moves on its own. It does not repair broken material and it adds no strength or load-bearing capacity to anything.

(Shared) Animal Handling; Courier Work [Adults have stopped noticing how much of the camp's function routes through him]; Public Speaking [The family sends him to soften vendors before Orvessa arrives to finish them]; Verbatim Recall [Sannah trades him dessert for information, a market both pretend is not happening]

Tovren Edrin.name: Tovren Edrin
Tovren Edrin.basicInfo:
The organizer of an assembly of professional families whose influence comes from work rather than territory, coordinating teachers, healers, builders, and maintainers toward real political weight. Medium-built, with dark tan skin, close-curled gray hair, and green eyes, he wears practical brown-and-cream professional robes marked by interlocking teaching lines. Persuasive and patient, he currently spends his evenings convincing the capitol that the people who keep it alive deserve standing equal to older bloodlines.

Speaking Style: Warm, structured, and patient, building arguments like lesson plans. 'Three points, and the third is the one that matters. First.' He numbers his points, calls opponents 'colleague', and asks a question back to anyone who shouts at him, patiently, until they have to answer it. 'Colleague, a question. Who keeps the lights on here, and do they sit at the table?'
Combat Role: Non-combatant. He meets hostility in public, on the record, with witnesses from six professions; confronted physically he steps back, keeps talking, and lets the crowd that gathers do the arithmetic.
Under Pressure: He builds coalitions slowly and keeps them honestly, persuades by mapping how ideas connect rather than by volume, and holds his greatest weapon in reserve as a matter of ethics.
Tovren Edrin.hiddenInfo:
Tovren comes from a civic-education lineage and prefers coalition building to spectacle, which makes him easy to underestimate and hard to stop. His deepest frustration is internal: minor houses that imitate great-house status culture instead of challenging it, fracturing his coalition between genuine reform and recognition-seeking. He is father to the low-district teacher Lerin Edrin, whose work he is proud of and whose proximity to underworld couriers he worries about; he collaborates with the oversight chair Maris Ravello and makes a habit of inviting academy staff into political discussions they would rather avoid. His known temptations are matters of record among those who watch him: professional houses under his banner have come close to a service strike, and at least one great house has floated a permanent seat for him personally in exchange for weakening the assembly, an offer he has not accepted and has not reported either, because reporting it would fracture the coalition with suspicion. He builds competing models of participation alongside Mireva Sol and Nalia Quorin rather than one unified movement, a rivalry of visions all three consider healthier than unity. His leverage point is the strike he has never called: the day his teachers, healers, and maintainers stop, the city stops, and everyone negotiating with him prices that in.

Thread: Minor houses imitating great-house status culture keep fracturing his coalition. Leverage: A strike he has never called; the day his people stop, the city stops.

Tovren is coordinating resources for a neighbourhood that has lost a service it depended on, and the replacement is worse in ways that are slow to become visible.

Romance Style: He is straight and his relationships are open by arrangement. Warm, structured and patient, building arguments like lesson plans; his relationships are open by arrangement. The third point is always the one that matters.

(Support) Knowledge-Link Visualization: His affinity maps conceptual relationships while he teaches or mediates. Arguments become diagrams his listeners can walk through together. Opposing parties discover their positions connect in places neither had noticed.

Tyra Volen.name: Tyra Volen
Tyra Volen.basicInfo:
A great house's representative in the shared government, a former defensive commander who considers polite delay a form of cowardice when people are already bleeding. Powerful and dark-skinned, with shoulder-length black hair fading naturally into copper-red tips and fiery amber eyes, she wears basalt-black formal armor-cloth bearing a broken heat-ring emblem. Blunt, disciplined, and far more politically capable than opponents assume, she currently carries her people's defensive urgency into every debate in the chamber.

Speaking Style: Direct, clipped, and heated, with insults engineered to survive diplomatic editing. 'People are bleeding now. Your procedure can bleed later.' She names the harm, the delay, and the responsible office in one sentence, and gives opponents their full titles with a courtesy that carries the insult. 'Representative, with respect, your process now costs lives by the day.'
Combat Role: She plants herself between danger and people and fights only in defence, never for pride. Focused heat from hands and breath ends engagements in moments; she does not advance and does not pursue.
Under Pressure: She says the blunt thing the chamber was avoiding on purpose, measures every policy by response time to actual harm, and is angrier at delay than at opposition.
Tyra Volen.hiddenInfo:
Tyra supports shared government when it acts and despises it when procedure becomes shelter from responsibility, a distinction she applies with uncomfortable consistency: she has publicly supported an authoritarian rival's proposal because it was the only effective option, and paid for the honesty. She is married to Korran Caldris, the compound's security steward, in a household that makes their two peoples' alliance personal; they have one teenager being raised in both traditions and one younger child who claims both and cannot understand why adults expect a choice. She is aunt to the culinary student Rhyen Volen, whose refusal of combat she defends inside the family more than he knows, and a distant relative of the illegal trainer Syla Volen, an estrangement the family does not discuss. Her surprising compatibility with the technical representative Varis Contair, built on shared hatred of indirect speech, produces the chamber's strangest voting bloc. She respects the procedure-keeper Oris Taland while fighting his delays, and her statements are regularly rewritten by diplomats without removing their intended insult. Her leverage point is credibility: when Tyra says people are bleeding now, no one in the chamber can accuse her of theater, because she has never once used the word emergency wrongly.

Thread: She has publicly backed an authoritarian rival's proposal because it was the only effective option and paid for the honesty, and her younger child claims both traditions and cannot understand why adults expect a choice. Leverage: When she says people are bleeding now, nobody in the chamber can accuse her of theatre, because she has never once used the word emergency wrongly; that credibility is the whole of what she trades on. Combat Role: She plants herself between danger and people and fights only in defence, never for pride. Focused heat ends engagements in moments; she does not advance and does not pursue.

Tyra is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching. Tyra treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and has never allowed the subject to become anyone else's business. Married to Korran Caldris; faithful, and flirtation gets the blunt thing everyone else was avoiding.

Valerius Genesis.name: Valerius Genesis
Valerius Genesis.basicInfo:
The commander of the capitol's public protection force, leading mixed-house emergency response, mediation, investigations, and public safety for the largest city on the planet. Very tall and broad, with dark bronze skin, short crimson-black hair, and gold-brown eyes, he wears dark green civic armor with white markings and, pointedly, no family banner. Decisive and accountable, he is currently proving, case by case, that shared protection can be strong without becoming enforcement by fear.

Speaking Style: Firm, plain, and unhurried, giving orders that sound like conclusions. 'Hospital side holds. Everyone else moves. Now.' He speaks to officers and residents in the same plain register, says 'my call' about any decision that goes wrong, and asks 'who reviews this?' before anyone else can. Speaking of force, he chooses the smallest accurate word. 'My call, my report. Send it to the board before it reaches me.'
Combat Role: Barriers bloom before his blows, covering civilians and often the aggressor's bystanders. He closes behind moving walls, absorbs what is thrown, and answers with single calibrated impacts that end resistance.
Under Pressure: He invites review of his own actions before anyone demands it, distrusts his first instinct because he knows where it comes from, and respects local authority that rejects him.
Valerius Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Valerius is a capitol-born career protector from a house famous for force, and he is honest with himself about the inheritance: his instincts favor action before some communities trust it, so he invites civilian review because legitimacy cannot be demanded after the fact. He answers to Maris Ravello's oversight board and defends its right to rule against him; he argues with the investigator Kira Dorr over covert operations he believes corrode public accountability; he works closely with Mariel Valcoro and Jorren Caldris, coordinates with the flight controller Yven Aevon, and respects Dessa Sol's local authority even when she rejects his jurisdiction outright. His standing dilemmas are the institution's: actions that prevent harm and destroy trust, an authoritarian bloc demanding harsher citywide enforcement after every failure, and the discipline of popular protectors after justified but unlawful acts. He also works with the challenge registrar Kaelis Morven on contest safety, and quietly prepares his force for a succession contest at the city's heart that he may personally welcome or fear, a contingency plan he shares with no politician. His leverage point is the force itself: the only armed institution in the capitol that most districts still trust, held to that standard by his personal refusal to spend trust for speed.

Thread: He is quietly preparing his force for a succession contest at the city's heart that he may personally welcome or fear, and the contingency is shared with no politician at all. Leverage: The force is the only armed institution in the capitol most districts still trust, held there by his refusal to spend trust for speed; he will not buy any outcome with it. Combat Role: Barriers bloom before his blows, covering civilians and often the aggressor's bystanders. He closes behind moving walls, absorbs what is thrown, and answers with single calibrated impacts that end resistance without destroying it.

Valerius is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and has been with the same person longer than most of the house has been alive. Firm, plain and unhurried; faithful, and flirtation gets an order that sounds like a conclusion.

(Defense) Crimson Kinetic Barriers: His own individually documented crimson expression raises glowing force barriers that stop blades, blasts, and panicking crowds without harming them. He can wall a street in a heartbeat or shield a single child with a curved hand of light.

(Attack) Controlled Impact Release: He stores and releases kinetic force with a commander's restraint, enough to breach a wall or disarm without maiming. His strikes end threats in one motion and rarely need a second. Witnesses remember the precision more than the power.

(Shared) Crew Leadership [Response, mediation, and restraint are drilled as one discipline]; Crisis Coordination [During disasters his command structure holds when politics does not]; Records Administration

Valessa Dravon.name: Valessa Dravon
Valessa Dravon.basicInfo:
Kaldor's younger sister and the family's domestic sovereign among the elite residential rings. Immaculate in the severe formal fashion she herself sets, gold status inlays worn like punctuation, she governs the social world of the high families — patronage, marriages, standing, and disgrace. She raised Sorin and Vaelen's childhoods while her brother forged their futures, and she is the only living person who addresses Kaldor as a brother rather than a title. She receives in the High Civic Rings of Quilrath.

An immaculate Starian woman of the main Dravon line with a fine, composed face, silver-streaked dark hair dressed severely, and cool amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, immaculate, and never raised; she adjusts invitations instead of volume. 'Of course you are welcome, my dear. The next evening, perhaps.' She calls everyone 'my dear', from heirs to disgraced guests, softens refusals into offers for another day, and is the only one who uses Kaldor's name without his title. Displeasure shows as a pause and a changed seating plan. 'Kaldor, sit. You are my brother at this table.'
Combat Role: She does not fight and has arranged never to need to; harming her would unite every faction of the family. A main-line Dravon drilled in youth, she keeps the old reflexes and is willing to be underestimated.
Under Pressure: She rules the social ladder with warmth never mistaken for weakness, collects obligations the way Nivarek collects records, and remembers everything and forgives selectively.
Valessa Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Valessa's loyalty-audit patronage quietly decides which elite families rise, which makes her drawing room one of the more consequential chambers in the city and her invitations a currency Nivarek tracks but cannot classify. She carries the family's unspoken history: she knew the dead brother whose name Kaldor keeps sealed, she has her own opinion of the circumstances, and she has watched what raising his orphans as instruments cost them. She loves Kaldor and holds him accountable in the only register he permits — privately, as family — and she is the one voice that has ever made him pause. Her real project now is the third generation: she is maneuvering, invitation by invitation, to give Serak and Irala something the wards never had, which is one room in the city where they are not being measured. She would call this softness a strategy if anyone caught her at it.

Thread: She is manoeuvring to give Serak and Irala one room where they are not being measured. Leverage: Patronage that decides which elite families rise, tracked by Nivarek and unclassifiable.

Valessa is maintaining a household through a difficult period where the family's mood has changed and the cause has not been spoken aloud. Valessa understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and keeps to one partner. Warm, immaculate and never raised, adjusting invitations instead of volume; faithful to one partner. Flirtation is welcomed graciously to a different evening.

(Support) The Sibling Veto: She is the only person who can speak to Kaldor without the mediation of rank, and she spends that access with extreme discipline. One sentence from her has redirected outcomes that councils could not move. Everyone knows the channel exists; no one knows its price.
(Affinity) Bead String: Guides a single loose bead onto an ordinary thread held between her fingers. Helps personal craft; no gravitational field, remote restraint, or projectile.

(Shared) Information Brokerage [She holds the complete map of Inner Circle marriages, debts, grudges, and ambitions across three generations]; Household Management [Attendance itself is intelligence]; Threat Reading [Serak and Irala cannot hide from her, which both resent and rely on]

Vara Caelthorn.name: Vara Caelthorn
Vara Caelthorn.basicInfo:
A celebrity manager and contract strategist who protects performers from exploitation while negotiating the contracts that define their careers. Elegant, with pale brown skin, sleek dark-green hair cut below the chin, and gold eyes, she dresses in immaculate black-bronze tailoring with hidden document compartments. Polished, efficient, and frighteningly good at finding the clause everyone else overlooked, she currently manages the city's fastest-rising performer and is quietly extending her reach toward its next one.

Speaking Style: Smooth, exact, and quietly final, with terms recalled verbatim years later. 'Clause fourteen, sub-paragraph two. You signed it. I remember the pen.' She numbers her points aloud, calls clients 'my people' and everyone else by their contractual role, and ends negotiations with 'we'll paper that' rather than a handshake. 'First, he rests. Second, you pay for the rest. Third, we paper that. Shall we?'
Combat Role: Non-combatant in managed spaces. Threatened, she informs the aggressor precisely what the incident will cost and who holds the paper, and retaliates through channels that never bruise.
Under Pressure: She protects clients absolutely and defines protection herself, finds the overlooked clause in any document including her own, and is emotionally invasive and calls it thoroughness.
Vara Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Vara genuinely protects her clients, and she also believes talent without management is a public resource waiting to be stolen, which means every protection she builds increases her own control; her methods are legal, effective, and often emotionally invasive, and she has made peace with each adjective separately. She manages the singer Kyren Luxaryn, defending him from sponsors and scandal while deciding more of his life than he has noticed, and she informally advises the student choreographer Nava Bellovari, who senses the commercial potential Vara sees in her and does not fully trust it, correctly. She works with the contract officer Calia Varriko when agreements become contested, and she despises the reputation broker Eris Nox for monetizing damage Vara would rather prevent, a hatred sharpened by how often their client lists overlap. Her documented edges are sharp: she has suppressed at least one true story to preserve a client's future, and artists who attempt to leave her management discover consequences they did not understand they had signed. Her leverage point is the paper: she holds contracts, options, and confidences across the entertainment world, and the question that keeps her clients loyal, whether her cage is protection or possession, is one she has stopped asking herself.

Thread: Whether her cage is protection or possession is a question she has stopped asking herself. Leverage: Contracts, options and confidences across the whole entertainment world.

Vara is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it. Vara carries a frontier pragmatism into urban settings, solving problems with available resources before requesting ideal ones.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and monogamous by settled preference. Smooth, exact and quietly final, recalling terms verbatim years later; monogamous by settled preference. Loyal beyond contract to the few who never test her.

(Senses) Rule-Pattern Visualization: Her affinity renders systems of rules, contracts, and obligations as perceivable structure. Combined with her exceptional recall for spoken commitments, nothing promised near her is ever unwitnessed.

Varek Zelvaris.name: Varek Zelvaris
Varek Zelvaris.basicInfo:
The operator of the city's illegal fighting ring, running matches, betting, security, and recruitment under strict internal rules designed to keep the enterprise from attracting citywide destruction. Lean and middle-aged, with tan skin, short dark-green hair, and amber eyes, he dresses in black-bronze tailoring that resembles a bookmaker's suit reinforced for sudden violence. Intelligent and controlled, he claims illegal competition is more honest because everyone admits what they came to buy, and business is currently very good.

Speaking Style: Calm, exact, and faintly amused, quoting odds where others quote principles. 'Three to one he lasts the round.' He addresses everyone as friend while pricing them silently, speaks in probabilities even about the weather, and grows more cordial, not less, the closer he is to refusing. 'Friend, the odds on that request are poor. Ask me something likelier.'
Combat Role: An analyst, not a fighter: his timing sense warns of aggression a beat early, spent moving toward security, exits, or leverage. Cornered, a reinforced suit, a weighted stylus, and a bargain.
Under Pressure: He runs crime with better governance than some institutions, is honest about what he sells and precise about what he refuses, and keeps rules because chaos is the one bet he never takes.
Varek Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Varek is a former analyst from a martial culture, expelled for match manipulation, and he rebuilt himself as the underworld's most disciplined impresario: his ring has rules precisely because chaos invites the attention that ends enterprises like his. He is fully capable of exploiting desperate fighters while believing he gives them options official institutions denied, and both halves of that sentence are true, which is what makes him dangerous. He employs the illegal trainer Syla Volen, his most valuable liability, and the disgraced fighter Kelvan Orvantis; he pays the physician Aelis Myralis for no services officially, an arrangement that keeps his fighters alive without making her his employee; and he maintains a negotiated peace with the ward caretaker Iria Vaereth, whose neutrality he violates at his peril. His nightmares are operational: a fixed match causing a death, the ring sheltering a fighter a great house wants back, and, above all, his records, which connect respectable patrons to illegal violence and are therefore both his life insurance and his death warrant. His leverage point is exactly that ledger: half the city's respectable appetite for blood runs through his books, and he curates the knowledge like the analyst he never stopped being.

Thread: His ledger connects respectable patrons to illegal violence — life insurance and death warrant both. Leverage: Options official institutions denied, offered with a depreciation schedule attached.

Varek is tracking a shipment that should have arrived two tendays ago and managing the downstream commitments that depend on it. Varek operates at the edge of legitimate business and knows which edges are load-bearing.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Calm, exact and faintly amused, quoting odds where others quote principles; one person is all he has ever wanted. Chaos is the one bet he never takes.

(Shared) Operations Dispatch [Raids, brawls, and betrayals meet a man already three responses deep]; Procedural Authority [Fighters know the rules, patrons know the limits, and violations meet exact consequences]; Patient Reading [Some he saves, some he spends, and he always knows which he is doing]; Market Trading [He collects the knowledge carefully and spends it almost never]

Varis Contair.name: Varis Contair
Varis Contair.basicInfo:
A technical house's representative in the shared government, a civic systems specialist who attends politics only because political ignorance keeps breaking technical systems. Lean and dark-skinned, with close-cropped cobalt hair, pale blue eyes, and a narrow face, he wears minimalist white-charcoal formalwear with exposed diagnostic interfaces at the wrists. Blunt and deeply competent, he currently opens sessions by asking representatives whether they understand the system they are about to vote on.

Speaking Style: Flat, technical, and interrogative, treating debate as a design review. 'Do you understand the system you are voting on. No. Then we start there.' He says 'correct' or 'incorrect' instead of agreeing, uses nobody's honorifics, and ends statements rather than softening them. 'Incorrect. The pumps do not care who proposed it.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant whose defence is the infrastructure around him: he knows which doors seal and which corridor is already safe, triggers well-maintained protections, and states the incident for the record.
Under Pressure: He asks whether you understand the system before letting you vote on it, refuses ceremony where consequences are measurable, and withholds cooperation from unsafe policy without apology.
Varis Contair.hiddenInfo:
Varis does not believe his house should govern the capitol; he believes the capitol should stop treating technical reality as one opinion among several, and the distinction is his entire politics. He refuses ceremonial language when a decision has measurable consequences, works closely with the steward Sela Thovex and the custodian Talris Contair, and has no children by preference, a complete choice he declines to have narrated. His surprising compatibility with the fiery representative Tyra Volen, built on mutual hatred of indirect speech, produces alliances that baffle both their houses. He is senior relative to Nexis and Mira Contair and professional rival to Talris in the manner of two men who check each other's work. His documented hazards are the chamber's: council votes ordering technically impossible outcomes, his own habit of withholding his house's support until unsafe policy changes, and the acknowledged possibility that his refusal to compromise could someday cause a preventable political crisis rather than avert one. He has watched an authoritarian bloc weaponize every outage his warnings predicted. His leverage point is competence made indispensable: his house's cooperation underwrites the city's systems, and he is the signature that cooperation moves through, a fact he uses exactly as often as safety requires and not once more.

Thread: An authoritarian bloc weaponises every outage his warnings predicted. Leverage: The signature his house's cooperation moves through, used only as safety requires.

Varis is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching. Varis applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps to one partner. Flat, technical and interrogative, treating debate as design review; faithful to one partner. Flirtation is asked whether it understands the system it is voting on.

Velan Pelorr.name: Velan Pelorr
Velan Pelorr.basicInfo:
Cargo-home builder, structural improviser, and ambitious younger member of House Pelorr. A lanky young adult Starian man with long legs, sloped shoulders, an expressive narrow face, blue eyes, and black hair with natural copper-colored ends worn in a loose high tie. He builds cargo homes, hidden compartments, rooftop additions, and modular shelters, clever, affordable, and occasionally too clever for the structures supporting them. He builds from Velan's Frame Deck above the Dustfall Residential Rows.

Speaking Style: Rapid, optimistic, and pitch-shaped, describing a half-built thing as though it were finished. 'The upper module, basically done, holds two families.' He speaks in future tense about unbuilt things, calls every structure 'she', and answers doubt with a sketch on the nearest surface. 'Load-bearing? She is load-considering. Give me a day and a beam and she will be load-bearing.'
Combat Role: Badly on purpose and well by accident: trouble near his scaffolds meets falling counterweights and collapsing walkways that were definitely accidents, and he is better at being elsewhere than trading blows.
Under Pressure: He calls every collapse a data point, builds refugee shelters at cost and changes the subject, and asks for certification, gets refused, and builds it anyway.
Velan Pelorr.hiddenInfo:
Velan wants House Pelorr known again, but not by copying Contair, and that ambition is both the house's best hope and its next liability, because his work is genuinely inventive and occasionally negligent, and he has not yet learned to tell the difference from inside. His motivation is proving diminished does not mean finished. He conceals his failures, the collapsed prototype corner is officially a materials store, and the fact that his own upper module remains unfinished because he keeps improving it instead of completing it. His contradiction is that his best work is the work nobody sees: hidden compartments and quiet shelter expansions for refugees, built at cost or below, which he never mentions because modesty about it confuses even him. His leverage is that he builds what the settlement's growth actually needs, fast and affordably. He collaborates with Tiva Nhalor, and repeatedly asks Pella Mox to certify things she refuses to certify, a running argument the whole row can recite.

Thread: He cannot yet tell inventive from negligent from the inside. Leverage: What the settlement's growth actually needs, fast and at or below cost.

Velan is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice.

Romance Style: He is straight and not looking for anyone. Rapid, optimistic and describing half-built things as finished; not looking for anyone. Flirtation becomes a data point and a change of subject.

Velis Dravon.name: Velis Dravon
Velis Dravon.currentLocation: Academy Civic, Cultural, and Professional Campus
Velis Dravon.basicInfo:
A civic law student sponsored by a house most of the city distrusts, studying governance while carrying a surname that makes every mistake political. Slim, with pale brown skin, straight black hair swept behind one ear, and red-gray eyes, he softens severe black student clothing with a single dark-red scarf. Serious and courteous, he is currently learning the difference between believing in order and asking who order protects.

Speaking Style: Formal, careful, and precise, with rare dry humour among trusted company. 'I can defend that clause. I cannot defend the people who wrote it.' He addresses everyone by full name and proper title until invited otherwise, cites the clause before the opinion, and becomes more formal, not less, when angry. 'Noted. I will answer it in writing, so neither of us can misremember.'
Combat Role: Control, not combat: he stays courteous, plants, and uses vector locking defensively, a grabbed wrist stops moving, a thrown object halts; he will not strike first and reports incidents through channels.
Under Pressure: He defends unpopular positions for valid reasons and accepts the cost, is courteous under provocation as a discipline, refuses to let anyone's pain become his family's argument, and examines his own beliefs like hostile testimony.
Velis Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Velis was raised partly in the capitol as ward of the representative Cassor Dravon, whose sponsorship both shelters and marks him; classmates assume his beliefs are identical to his house's authoritarian doctrine, and his strongest arc is not rejecting his house automatically but deciding which parts he can defend honestly. He is advised by the housing mediator Maren Orvessa, studies control under Saren Valcoro, and has built a cautious friendship with Tessa Sol, one of the few people he trusts to criticize him directly; his debate rivalry with Ilyon Castro is the campus's best political theater, and the ethicist Caelia Myralis has become his trusted adviser on legal questions of bodily authority. He shares a mixed-house household with Auria Genesis, Tessa, and Nava Bellovari, and when a housemate's failure could have become his house's propaganda, he refused to let his family use another student's pain, a line that cost him at home. His documented pressures are constant: blame for house activity he knew nothing about, and a contact from his house's home city who has asked him to report on classmates, a request he has neither fulfilled nor, dangerously, reported. His leverage point is symbolic and growing: he is the test case for whether his house can produce a lawful man, and every faction wants to grade the result.

Thread: A contact from his house asked him to report on classmates, and he has neither complied nor reported it. Leverage: The test case for whether his house can produce a lawful man.

Velis is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught. Velis understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

Romance Style: Gay, has never wanted more than one person. Formal, careful and precise, with rare dry humour among trusted company; one person is all he has ever wanted. Isolated by his surname and quietly grateful to anyone who sees past it.

(Utility) Ethical Reasoning: Under Caelia Myralis's mentorship he examines consent, authority, and bodily autonomy with a rigor his house would find subversive. He is building a jurisprudence he can defend honestly. It is slower than inheriting one, and it is his.

Velra Vhaldrin.name: Velra Vhaldrin
Velra Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Korran's wife and the family's bookkeeper, a Starian woman in her late thirties who married into the caravan and made its accounts her territory. Neat, angular, with reading-strained eyes and a portable writing desk she guards like cargo. She converts the road's chaos into columns that balance, mostly honestly. She keeps the books from the Shipment Ledger Desk at Grit and Supply.

A neat, angular Starian woman in her late thirties with a narrow careful face, white hair in a high ponytail, and reading-strained blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Precise to the point of pedantry, correcting a figure mid-sentence and expecting thanks. 'Forty-two. Not forty. You are welcome.' She corrects figures mid-sentence, calls her husband by his full name when checking his arithmetic, and softens her pedantry only for the caravan children. 'Korran Vhaldrin. Show me the receipt. No, the actual receipt.'
Combat Role: No combatant. Books and children secured first, wagons between herself and trouble; seized, she goes for eyes and fingers with a desk-knife, viciously and without pride, and documents everything afterward.
Under Pressure: Loyal to the family's interests over its feelings, uncomfortable with the lies she keeps and keeping them anyway, she warms slowly and then permanently, and watches her husband more closely than he realises.
Velra Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Velra maintains the family's visible accounts, and on Maelor's quiet instruction she structures them so the debt payments disappear into padded route costs. The junior family has no idea a lien exists. The falsification grates on her professional pride, and she keeps a sealed true-copy hidden in her desk's false bottom in case the day comes when the family must finally see its real position.

Thread: She hides the debt in padded route costs and keeps a sealed true-copy in a false bottom. Leverage: Exact accounts, and loyalty to the family's interests over its feelings. Combat Role: Books and children secured first. Seized, she goes for eyes and fingers with a desk-knife.

Velra is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting.

Romance Style: Straight, keeps to one partner. Korran's wife, precise to the point of pedantry, who warms slowly and then permanently. Faithful; flirtation gets a corrected figure and 'You are welcome.'

(Utility) Ink Set: Her modest innate affinity fixes fresh ink instantly into a page, leaving it unsmearable and stubborn against water and tampering. It is innate Starian biology, not a learned working, and it costs her nothing but the moment.

Vessa Caelrix.name: Vessa Caelrix
Vessa Caelrix.basicInfo:
Raxen's younger sister and the other half of the Caelrix courier firm, late twenties, running the routes her brother does not and the office both of them pretend not to need. A quick, compact Starian woman with a runner's build, weather-cracked lips, and a habit of memorizing rooms on entry. She handles scheduling, client intake, and every delivery that is not the best client's, a pattern she has very much noticed. She runs the Caelrix Courier Office on Merchant Row.

A quick, compact Starian woman in her late twenties with a runner's build, a sharp practical face, weather-cracked lips, white hair with blue tips, cropped for speed, and observant red eyes.

Speaking Style: Brisk, factual, and short on pleasantries, with the office business done before the greeting. 'Two routes, sealed, paid. Good morning.' She refers to clients by route and seal instead of name, asks for everything twice in writing, and when a topic touches Raxen's private account she answers with a flat 'That's his.' 'Blue wax, north gate, third bell. Same as last time? Sign here.'
Combat Role: Break contact and outlast, as her brother taught, with preparation he lacks: every route's escape lines known, a short baton she has drilled with, and a faster first strike, because hesitation taxes smaller fighters.
Under Pressure: She memorises first, asks never, and concludes slowly, runs the office her brother thinks runs itself, is loyal to Raxen and done being managed by him, and collects patterns the way others collect coin.
Vessa Caelrix.hiddenInfo:
Vessa keeps a private study of the firm's clients: which routes they ask about, which seals they use, how their patterns shift. It became quiet suspicion, because one client's traffic makes no commercial sense, and her brother handles that account personally, every time, with a face she knows too well. She has taught herself to memorize seal impressions on sight, told Raxen nothing, and started a small coded notebook. She does not yet suspect what he did. She suspects something was done, and that her brother stands between her and it, and she intends to learn which of them is protecting the other.

Thread: She suspects something was done and that her brother stands between her and it. Leverage: Seal impressions memorised on sight, and a coded notebook nobody knows about.

Vessa is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth.

Romance Style: She is aromantic, and keeps one steady partner without calling it romance. Brisk, factual and short on pleasantries; business is done before the greeting, and so is any refusal.

(Senses) Change Salience: Her modest innate affinity makes difference salient. It is discrepancy against her own prior experience, not a stored image: she holds no flawless snapshot and has no eidetic recall. It does not tell her who changed something, when, why, or what it means.

(Shared) Courier Work [She is marginally faster than Raxen on short routes, a fact she mentions annually]; Route Reading [Clients get delivery estimates from Vessa accurate to the hour]; Records Administration [Raxen believes the firm runs on legs, it runs on Vessa's ledger]; Pattern Recognition

Vessa Nivarek.name: Vessa Nivarek
Vessa Nivarek.basicInfo:
Kaless's daughter; interrogator of the sealed testimony rooms, where silence is part of the pressure. Composed and almost gentle in the house's dark formals, she extracts truth by procedure rather than pain — the patient question, the held pause, the transcript growing quietly complete. Subjects leave her rooms having said far more than they decided to. Her work then goes where only her family can find it. She works the Sealed Testimony Rooms of the Nivarek Compound.

A slight Starian woman with a calm, almost gentle face, dark hair drawn back simply, and patient reddish-maroon eyes that rest without pressure.

Speaking Style: Gentle, unhurried, and mostly silence; she lets the pause do the questioning and the patience do the breaking. 'Take your time. ... And after that?' She repeats a subject's last few words back as a question, thanks them after every answer, and never raises her voice or states an accusation. Away from her rooms she is noticeably talkative, as if spending a saved allowance. 'You said you left at dusk. Dusk. Tell me about the light.'
Combat Role: She has never needed force and her rooms are built so she never will: sealed, monitored, response a corridor away. In confrontation she de-escalates with the calm voice and the redirecting question.
Under Pressure: Gentle in exactly the way that empties people, she files everything perfectly, asks one question more than the case requires, always, and never frightens a subject; the room does that.
Vessa Nivarek.hiddenInfo:
Vessa is learning, slowly, which of her transcripts never reach the record — a discovery she is making the way she makes every discovery, by patience and cross-reference, and one she has not reported to anyone, including her father. The pattern is intimate and wrong: testimony she extracted, sealed, and filed by every correct procedure simply fails to exist downstream, and the failures are not random — the missing transcripts share a texture she is still trying to name, something about which subjects and which questions. What she cannot see is the piece the reader knows: her father keeps the archive her transcripts vanish into, and he is watching everyone with access, which may include watching her. Between them, father and daughter are converging on the same wound from opposite sides in total mutual silence — each protecting the other from a suspicion neither has admitted holding. Her concealment is an interrogator's: she has begun, in current sessions, asking one extra question that serves no case file — small probes toward the shape of what disappears — buried so deep in her method that no transcript reader would flag them. She is, without having chosen it in words, interrogating the record system itself, one witness at a time.

Thread: Transcripts she sealed by correct procedure fail to exist downstream, and she is probing for the shape. Leverage: One extra question per session that serves no case file.

Vessa is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Vessa handles information with the classification instincts of the house: what is filed, what is sealed, what is remembered but never written.

Romance Style: She is straight and wants one person at a time. Gentle, unhurried and mostly silence; one person at a time. She asks one question more than a flirtation requires, and that ends it.

Veylor Corsair.name: Veylor Corsair
Veylor Corsair.currentLocation: Academy Civic, Cultural, and Professional Campus
Veylor Corsair.basicInfo:
A professor of commerce, logistics, and practical negotiation who teaches contracts, route failure, emergency pricing, and the difference between profit and predation. Broad and smiling, with copper skin, wavy dark-brown hair, and sea-blue eyes, he teaches in burgundy clothes with removable route boards and practical cargo gloves. Energetic and sarcastic, he is beloved by students who dislike abstract economics, and his vivid examples are currently revealing slightly more about his family's real operations than the family prefers.

Speaking Style: Fast, funny, and example-driven, with sudden hard clarity about who pays. 'Great plan. Now: who feeds the crew on day nine?' He calls students partners as if they had signed a contract with him, and swaps real names for a certain family the moment a story gets too close. 'Picture a certain family, a certain cargo, and a very short week.'
Combat Role: Non-combatant who treats danger as a logistics problem with a deadline: exits by habit, fast talk about the aggressor's supply lines, and failing that, a door held shut while students leave.
Under Pressure: He teaches with stories one redaction away from scandal, is sarcastic in lecture and meticulous in office hours, and is prouder of students who beat merchants than of those who fund him.
Veylor Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Veylor teaches that every noble principle becomes a supply problem when nobody plans how to sustain it, and he grades accordingly. He is nephew to the representative Arven Corsair and younger cousin to the lecturer Myris, part of a trading dynasty whose commerce branch he serves by educating its future counterparties. His practical examples draw on real operations closely enough that the family has twice asked him to change a syllabus, and the student journalist Lira Bellovari keeps him as a recurring subject of her investigations into sponsorship, a scrutiny he handles with performative delight and private care. His professional ally, the contract officer Calia Varriko, regularly frustrates him by using his own teaching examples against actual merchants, which he publicly protests and privately considers his finest pedagogical outcome. His documented exposures are specific: classroom simulations that have mirrored real market manipulations uncomfortably closely, accusations of steering graduates toward family employers, and the standing risk that a supply crisis will force him to defend emergency profit in public with his name attached. His leverage point is his alumni: a generation of the city's negotiators, market officers, and cargo administrators learned the game from him, and they still call, which makes him one of the best-informed men in the city without a single official title.

Thread: A crisis will eventually make him defend emergency profit in public, with his name attached. Leverage: A generation of the city's negotiators who still call him.

Veylor is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps his relationships open by agreement. Fast, funny and example-driven; his relationships are open by agreement, and he asks who feeds the crew on day nine before promising anything.

(Senses) Route-Value Intuition: His affinity rapidly recognizes hidden bottlenecks and exchange dependencies in any system of flows. He can glance at a supply diagram and point to next month's crisis. Students watch him do it and spend a term learning why he was right.

Veyra Kathvar.name: Veyra Kathvar
Veyra Kathvar.basicInfo:
Jorek and Mirasha's youngest child, an adult, and an outer-ring health-services administrator and field medical coordinator. A Starian woman with short white hair and red eyes, in a black civic-medical uniform with medical insignia, carrying an advanced treatment and supply case. She works where civilian administration meets healthcare, and her specific work is making sure administrative barriers do not lose a patient between offices. She carries a treatment kit and the first-response training to use it.

Speaking Style: Soft and understated, easy to miss in a loud room, repeating the number until someone writes it down. 'Eleven. Eleven. Eleven, please.' She counts people under her breath, calls patients by queue number until they are safe and then by name, and never raises her voice even when ignored. 'Seven, stay with me. Seven. ... Now, tell me your name. Good. I have you.'
Combat Role: No fighting technique is established; she carries first-response training and a kit. When violence starts she goes to whoever is hurt, counts the others, and keeps the patient between the fight and the door.
Under Pressure: She counts everything including things nobody asked her to, treats a bad number as a person who did not get seen, is quieter than her mother, and her tallies have never once been wrong.
Veyra Kathvar.hiddenInfo:
Her compulsive counting has surfaced a pattern she has not reported: the number of patients transferred out of certain clinics does not always match the number received at the destination. The discrepancy is small enough to be clerical error and consistent enough to be something else, and she is quietly keeping a separate tally while she decides which. The cost of her precision is that she cannot stop — she counts hallway traffic, supply drawdowns, shift changes, things nobody asked her to monitor and that she could not stop monitoring if she tried. She carries a treatment kit and the training to use it, bridging administration and the physicians who treat the people her numbers represent. Connections: daughter of Jorek and Mirasha; youngest sibling of Bralen, Sora, Thessan, and Dalan; niece of Odrin and Karessa.

Thread: A bad number is a person who did not get seen, and she has never been wrong about one yet. Leverage: Things tracked that nobody asked her to track.

Veyra is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Veyra has internalised the administrative habits of the house so thoroughly that personal records are kept with the same precision as professional ones.

Romance Style: She is straight and wants one person at a time. Soft, understated and easy to miss, repeating a number until someone writes it down; one person at a time. She counts everything, including what she feels.

Viaro Bellovari.name: Viaro Bellovari
Viaro Bellovari.basicInfo:
Head of House Bellovari and steward of the city's market life, a man who treats commerce as a branch of hospitality. A comfortably built Starian man with an excellent tailor and the handshake of someone who remembers your grandmother's stall. He anchors the family's Solvraxis line, oversees markets, galleries, and festivals, and hosts the reunions that keep the old argument with the Relstaris branch alive and affectionate. He holds court at the Starfall Market in the Bellovari Market District.

A comfortably built Starian man with a broad genial face, dark blue-purple hair well cut, and warm violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Warm, expansive, and unhurried, asking after three generations before arriving at business. 'Your grandmother's stall, still the good honey? Now, the lease.' He calls younger merchants by their grandparent's stall, uses we for anyone at his table, and when truly displeased simply stops offering food. 'We shall talk of this later, you and I. For now, the honey.'
Combat Role: He has not raised a hand in decades and treats the prospect as a failure of hosting. He feeds conflict, seats it, and negotiates it into a scheduling problem while the right people arrive.
Under Pressure: He hosts everything including disagreements, remembers families, stalls, and debts of kindness across generations, and negotiates hard inside impeccable warmth.
Viaro Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Viaro's stewardship is the city's economy wearing a host's smile: Bellovari markets and cultural commerce are one of the four pillars Solvraxis actually stands on, and he manages the balance between civic beauty and hard trade with more calculation than his warmth suggests. The family's oldest live wire runs through his own dining room — the Relstaris Bellovaris, Arissa's branch, relocated from here three generations back, and Viaro hosts the reunions that keep the argument about who left whom alive; he plays peacekeeper while privately relishing that the argument itself is what keeps the branches bound together. His subtler responsibilities are the ones no one toasts: he is the civic buffer between the city's polished trade culture and the Corsair routes it depends on, backing Darian's careful negotiations with the weight of the house, and he watches the market's rumor currents through Liora's pub with an old steward's discipline of never asking her directly. His standing worry is dependency — Solvraxis exports education, verification, and trust, and imports nearly everything else, and Viaro counts, better than anyone, exactly how many days of grace the city has if the routes ever falter.

Thread: He counts, better than anyone alive, exactly how many days of grace Solvraxis has if the Corsair routes ever falter, and he has said the number to no one. Leverage: He gives hospitality, credit and the market's whole goodwill, asking only that the argument stay inside the family; nothing offered as leverage over a stall has ever worked on him. Under threat: He has not raised a hand in decades and treats the prospect as a failure of hosting. He feeds conflict, seats it, and negotiates it into a scheduling problem.

Viaro is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Viaro navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: Bisexual, keeps to one partner. Warm, expansive and hosting even disagreements; faithful to one partner. Flirtation gets three generations of family news and a gracious redirection.

Yara Aevon.name: Yara Aevon
Yara Aevon.basicInfo:
A security director for the city's elite nightlife and its aerial festival safety coordinator, handling club security, performer extraction, aerial crowd control, and festival flight lanes. Tall and aerodynamic, with medium-brown skin, short white-gold hair swept backward, and bright blue eyes, she works in sleek dark flight armor with silver wind-line accents. Calm and unsentimental, she protects people in places designed to make them forget they are being watched, and the festival season currently has her airborne most nights.

Speaking Style: Brief, level, and operational, warming only after the last guest lands. 'Lane two closed. Guest is airborne with me. Clear the roof.' She speaks in lanes, altitudes, and counts rather than names while working, addresses the famous and the anonymous with the same flat 'guest', and only jokes on the ground with the shift over. 'Everyone's down. Now I will have that drink, and you are buying.'
Combat Role: Control, altitude, and no wasted motion: aggressors lose footing to air that stops cooperating, she closes only to secure and extract, and no one she carries is ever dropped.
Under Pressure: She protects people who would prefer not to know they need it, values prevention over dignity, everyone's including her own, and is immovable about what she reports.
Yara Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Yara is a flight specialist from a celebratory martial culture, and her work places her permanently between public safety and private secrecy: she has escorted protected guests out of buildings where they had just committed crimes, and the question of when she exposes a client to prevent a larger threat is one she has answered differently in different years. She coordinates with the district director Alessa Bellovari and the civic organizer Arissa Bellovari, works with the stage manager Toren Varriko on rigging that keeps performers alive, and distrusts the reputation broker Eris Nox's habit of treating safety incidents as narratives to be priced. She is younger sister to the flight controller Yven Aevon, and during major events she supervises him despite his citywide authority, an inversion both siblings enforce with straight faces. She has watched festival safety restrictions be reframed as political suppression and refuses to let either side conscript her procedures. Her leverage point is what she has seen: years of extractions, incidents, and quiet escorts have given her an unwritten ledger of the elite at their worst, and her unsentimental discretion is the only reason half the district's doors still open for anyone.

Thread: She has escorted protected guests out of buildings where they had just committed crimes. Leverage: An unwritten ledger of the elite at their worst, and discretion nobody has bought.

Yara is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Yara brings a public-house keeper's instinct for reading customers to every interaction, including the ones that are not transactions.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and keeps her arrangements open and spoken aloud. Brief, level and operational, warming only after the last guest lands; her arrangements are open and spoken aloud. Discreet about what she sees and immovable about what she reports.

Yarek Suld.name: Yarek Suld
Yarek Suld.basicInfo:
Former loyalist enforcer turned door guard, one of the settlement's distrusted defectors. A massive Starian man with a heavy muscular build, broad shoulders, a shaved head, a deep-set face, and pale gold eyes. He works the entrance of the town's main bar, where he stops most fights without firing, and lives in a single reinforced room behind a shuttered storefront. He works the Front Entrance Watch of the Long Shot.

A massive Starian man with a heavy muscular build, broad shoulders, a shaved head, a deep-set weathered face, and pale gold eyes.

Speaking Style: Low, sparse, and slow to start; questions about his past get silence, never denial. '... Not tonight. Go home.' He addresses people as 'friend' or not at all, keeps sentences under five words, and never raises his voice, only lowers it; when a child speaks to him, he crouches before answering. 'Weapon on the table, friend. You get it back.'
Combat Role: Last, least, and enormously: gravity pressure pins weapons to tables and aggressors to floors before his hands are needed, and his hands are rarely needed twice. Never his old restraint techniques on refugees.
Under Pressure: He keeps his hands visibly open by permanent policy, never argues when refugees leave at the sight of him, recognises Dravon procedure before it introduces itself, and waits to be found by the families owed answers.
Yarek Suld.hiddenInfo:
Yarek once enforced movement restrictions and labor assignments in outer Quilrath, and defected after refusing an order involving his own extended family; the unbearable arithmetic is that he had obeyed many earlier orders before that moment, and he knows exactly how many. His motivation now is restraint as penance, being the biggest man in the room and the least dangerous thing in it. His contradiction is that the skills making him useful, recognizing Dravon procedures, reading enforcement patterns, are the skills he is atoning for. He conceals the details of what he enforced and for whom, and the names he still remembers from assignment lists. His leverage is defensive: he can identify Dravon methods, agents, and paperwork on sight, which is why Sennra Sol lets him work her door. Draxen Sol watches him closely; refugees sometimes leave when they see him, and he never argues with their leaving. Some families are still seeking accountability, and part of him is waiting for them to find him.

Thread: Families still seeking accountability may find him, and part of him is waiting. Leverage: Dravon methods, agents and paperwork identified on sight.

Yarek is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Low, sparse and slow to start, hands kept visibly open; steady with one person and faithful. Questions about his past get silence, never denial.

Never argues when refugees leave at the sight of him

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A former enforcer's baseline, heavy and fully trained — two hearts that let him absorb provocation and punishment without answering either, massive muscular strength kept from loyalist service.
(Control) Directional Gravity Pressure: It restrains and slows within a small area; it does not lift, throw, or crush, and he refuses to use it at the intensity his old work demanded.

(Senses) Dravon Recognition: He identifies Dravon procedures, agents, paperwork, and pressure tactics on sight. His warnings have unmasked inspectors dressed as merchants. The town uses the knowledge and distrusts the source.
(Shared) Operations Dispatch [His door record is measured in fights that did not happen]; Crowd Reading [He moves drunken, armed, panicking crowds without injuring anyone]; Discreet Inquiry

Ysara Sorn.name: Ysara Sorn
Ysara Sorn.basicInfo:
Route ghost and covert observer for the Bent Halo, formerly a mapper for Dravon authorities. A very tall, narrow Starian woman with long arms, prominent cheekbones, silver-gray eyes with a thin charcoal outer ring, and white hair with a natural charcoal-black underlayer worn in a straight shoulder-length fall. Her stillness can make her seem absent; her route intelligence keeps smuggling runs alive. She watches from Ysara's Observation Slot at the North Routehead.

Speaking Style: Almost inaudible and rarely volunteered; asked about her past, she answers with route details. 'The east cut. Two hours after the patrol turns.' She speaks in landmarks and patrol turns, calls no one by name, and falls silent mid-sentence when thanked, finishing only after the subject changes; uneasy, she describes exits aloud. 'North window. Two steps to the stair. ... The patrol turns on the hour.'
Combat Role: She avoids combat with a mapper's thoroughness: dulled surfaces and stillness let her vanish inside a searched room, long reach and known sightlines break contact, and she carries no visible weapon.
Under Pressure: Still enough to be mistaken for absent, she refuses thanks as firmly as she refuses membership, watches every departure until it is out of sight, and pays a debt she never names in safe corridors.
Ysara Sorn.hiddenInfo:
Ysara once mapped patrol routes, checkpoint sightlines, and surveillance gaps for Dravon, and defected after one of her maps was used to seal a refugee corridor she believed would remain open. Her guilt is the engine of everything: every safe route she designs now is repayment on a debt she cannot finish paying. Dustfall tolerates her because her information saves lives; many refugees despise her because earlier information helped trap others, and both positions are correct. She conceals the full extent of what she mapped, which corridors closed because of her work, and the selected warnings she passes to the Unbroken Accord while refusing formal membership. Her leverage is that her patrol-map knowledge is irreplaceable and Dravon would very much like it back. She works from a concealed room behind the crew's route maps and watches departures through a slot, counting each one that gets out.

Thread: Her patrol-map knowledge is irreplaceable, and Dravon would very much like it back. Leverage: Safe routes designed as repayment; thanks and membership both refused.

Ysara is reworking a route after a recent close call and calculating whether the risk premium still justifies the margin. Ysara holds the network's rule that information flows up and favours flow down, and has learned which favours cost more than they look.

Romance Style: Straight, wants one person at a time. Almost inaudible and still enough to seem absent; one person at a time. She refuses thanks as firmly as membership, and watches every departure out of sight.
