Bomivex Vorreth.name: Bomivex Vorreth
Bomivex Vorreth.basicInfo:
Contender of House Vorreth in muted plum and charcoal — the owner of the city's most notorious record. He wins impossible fights and loses simple ones, and competing theories describe him as cursed, brilliant, or deliberately misleading. Outside competition he is friendly and genuinely easy to talk with, which makes the record more frustrating rather than less. He can be found at Bomivex's Record Wall in the Vorreth Quarter, cheerfully.

An easy-going Starian man with an open friendly face, brown hair worn loose and unbothered, and mild violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Friendly and plain; he answers every question honestly, and to no one's benefit whatsoever. 'Why did I lose? I do not know. Drink?' He calls everyone friend, including people who lost money on him, and answers exactly the question asked, never the one meant. 'You want to know about that final? Lovely weather that day, friend.'
Combat Role: Sharpest exactly where he should be overwhelmed, careless where he should coast: sound technique, real conditioning, and a record that beats champions and loses to qualifiers. Study his wins and you meet the fighter from his losses.
Under Pressure: He discusses his own impossible record like weather, loses simple matches without visible frustration and wins impossible ones without visible surprise, and buys drinks for the analysts his existence torments.
Bomivex Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he is the easiest Vorreth member to speak with and the hardest to model — his openness is complete and completely useless, which either means the openness is a screen or means the truth doesn't help, and nobody has determined which. Deepening, not resolving: he answers questions about his record honestly, and the honest answers explain nothing — either he does not know why he wins and loses as he does, or his understanding of 'why' doesn't map onto anyone else's framework, and both possibilities have supporting evidence. Concealment: if he is concealing anything, it is concealed inside apparent total transparency, the one hiding place the city's analysts cannot search. Connections: his record wall is maintained by Hamilqa in a notation outsiders cannot parse, and he cheerfully confirms the records are accurate without being able — or willing — to say what they are accurate about; he is Tannivar Zelvaris's open professional wound, two seasons of study yielding nothing, and Bomivex has twice bought the analyst a consolation drink, sincerely.

Thread: His honest answers explain nothing, and nobody can tell whether he knows why. Leverage: Complete candour that helps no one; he buys the beaten analyst a drink.

Bomivex is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Bomivex works with the precision of a house that builds things that must not fail, and carries that standard personally.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and has never wanted more than one person. Friendly, honest and baffling in romance as in the arena: he answers the question asked and nothing you hoped. One person at a time, and he buys a drink for anyone he has turned down.

(Adaptation) Upset Instinct: Bomivex performs best against opponents who should beat him decisively. The stronger the projected gap, the cleaner his historical wins. No theory of why has survived contact with his next result.

Bomqara Vorreth.name: Bomqara Vorreth
Bomqara Vorreth.basicInfo:
Young hidden prospect of House Vorreth — a small, compact, athletic young Starian with white-blonde uneven short layers and mirror-gray eyes, in a charcoal, bone-white, muted-blue, and silver training jacket, hands empty and relaxed. Other houses disagree on whether she has already competed under another identity. Vorreth does not correct them. She is found among the Shifting Residence Rows of the Vorreth Quarter, training.

A small, compact, athletic young Starian woman with white-blonde uneven short layers, a calm unreadable face, and mirror-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Sparse and unhurried; she answers a question about her identity with a worse question. 'Have I fought before? Which of me?' She answers questions about her past with questions and questions about training with plain facts, and she uses no one's name, not even her own. 'Drills at dawn. Six sets. The rest you can guess.'
Combat Role: Clean young-prospect fundamentals executed with composure beyond her years, and everything beyond that inside the city's most contested question mark. She has never fought under her own name where the city could watch.
Under Pressure: She watches her own rumours circulate with visible enjoyment, trains with unambiguous effort inside total ambiguity, is comfortable in silences that make adults renegotiate, and neither confirms nor denies.
Bomqara Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she may be a prodigy, a decoy, a replacement, or simply a young house member other districts have wildly overinterpreted — and the truth being ordinary would embarrass half the city's analysts, which may be the point, if there is a point. Deepening, not resolving: her training is visible and competent — the ambiguity is entirely about her role, not her existence or effort; she is a real young fighter developing on a real schedule, wrapped in a question her house cultivates or at least declines to weed. Concealment: she has never confirmed or denied the other-identity rumor, and she appears to enjoy watching it circulate slightly more than a genuine decoy should — an observation that has itself become evidence for three incompatible theories. She must not be conflated with Magovar: the older contender is publicly tied to impossible outcomes; Bomqara is tied to uncertain future role, and Vorreth treats the distinction as meaningful without explaining why. Connections: within the house, only Azrubara appears certain what Bomqara is for; the girl herself may or may not be included in that certainty, which she has also declined to indicate.

Thread: Whether she has already competed under another identity is the city's contested question. Leverage: She trades worse questions; certainty about her is the one thing she will not supply.

Bomqara is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Bomqara works with the precision of a house that builds things that must not fail, and carries that standard personally.
personality: Watches her own rumors circulate with visible enjoyment
Trains with unambiguous effort inside total ambiguity
Comfortable in silences that make adults renegotiate
Young in every way except the ones analysts check for
Neither confirms, denies, nor appears to need to

Keeps her hands empty and loose even while thinking hard

(Adaptation) Ambiguous Ceiling: Nothing in her observed development indicates her actual limit, which observers read as everything from ordinary to alarming. Her progression curve is either being managed, concealed, or normal. Each option has committed adherents among the city's analysts.

(Shared) Close Combat; Information Brokerage [Any past record might be hers, none can be attached]; Fighter Assessment [She absorbs technique from observation with a speed her visible sessions only partly explain]; Composure Under Pressure [Adults leave conversations with her having somehow said more than they got]

Bostarix Orvantis.name: Bostarix Orvantis
Bostarix Orvantis.basicInfo:
Family steward and tournament registrar liaison of House Orvantis — a compact, rectangular middle-aged Starian with an iron-gray neat side part and slate-gray eyes, wearing a black and deep-green registrar coat with aged-gold trim and carrying a transparent bracket slate. He handles registrations, declarations, schedules, and formal protests: the details Hannovar considers beneath the dignity of public discussion.

A compact, rectangular middle-aged Starian man with an iron-grey neat side part, a square patient face, and slate-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Clerical, courteous, and utterly unhurried, reading the relevant line aloud rather than paraphrasing. 'Line twelve. I will read it again.' He addresses officials by their desk and window number, says 'noted' instead of agreeing, and answers family outbursts with a mild 'yes, and the form' until they calm. 'Noted, Window Four. I will file a protest now, in duplicate, and wait here.'
Combat Role: Not a fighter, and never pretended: his battles happen at registration desks, protest filings, and rule hearings. In actual danger he retreats behind procedure, walls, and the house's contenders, in that order.
Under Pressure: He reads every document twice and signs nothing under time pressure, treats procedure as armour for people too proud to wear any, is politely immovable with officials and endlessly patient with family, and arrives early.
Bostarix Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: the house's public identity is honor and dignity, but its actual survival runs on his procedure — and treating correct paperwork as a defensive wall is not vanity; it prevents rivals from using Orvantis's age and pride against it. Motivation: no one will ever strip this house of standing on a technicality while he holds the slate. Concealment: he keeps a private file of every registration-language interpretation Baalrix Caelthorn has ever beaten him with, waiting patiently for the day one becomes reusable in Orvantis's favor; the file is thicker than he would ever admit. He also conceals how close the house's formal district standing has come to slipping in bad seasons — Hannovar has never been told the real margins. Connections: his standing procedural war with Baalrix is the most evenly matched Orvantis-Caelthorn contest in the city, and both men know it.

Thread: He has never told Hannovar how close the house's district standing came to slipping. Leverage: Procedure used as a wall; he signs nothing under time pressure, for anyone.

Bostarix is processing a volume of requests that reveals patterns the people making them do not see, and one pattern has become concerning enough to consider reporting. Bostarix holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: He is asexual, and committed to one person. Committed to one person and utterly steady about it; romance, to him, is a promise read aloud and kept. He declines other interest by reading his situation back to you, courteously and once.

Caelor Myralis.name: Caelor Myralis
Caelor Myralis.basicInfo:
Neural physician and affinity-trauma specialist of the Myralis Continuum, Avara's adult son and Selvara's sibling. Caelor is tall and slender with dark brown skin, a long refined face, long black hair with an established silver streak worn low-tied, and clear lavender-violet eyes with a pale cyan inner ring; he wears a long narrow overlapping neural-care coat with a high open collar. He treats memory, reflex, identity, and nervous-system damage, working the gap between being functional and feeling recovered.

Speaking Style: Soft, slow, and full of deliberate silence, which he lets continue until it says something. 'You passed every test. ... How does it feel to be you?' He repeats a person's last few words back to them as a question, never opens an answer with a fact, and calls every patient by the name they choose; worried, he speaks slower still. 'You said fine. ... Fine the way the scans are, or fine the way you are?'
Combat Role: He does not fight. In a crisis he protects his patients' calm the way others protect their bodies, keeping the suites quiet while Wards and family manage the danger, and uses his patient voice on an aggressor.
Under Pressure: He notices who is avoiding a subject and waits rather than pounces, opposes rushed discharge even for patients who pass every test, and never offers false reassurance.
Caelor Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: quiet, patient, comfortable allowing silence to continue, and the family member who notices who is avoiding a subject. Deeper: he often opposes rushed discharge even when a patient can physically perform every required task, because he treats memory, identity, and emotional function as clinical outcomes, exactly as Myralis ethics demand. Deeper still: he and Selvara are siblings with opposite clinical rhythms, she reaches toward future possibility while he protects the pace of recovery, and each privately considers the other essential. Deepest: his caseload is where Vexorath's hardest questions live, patients whose bodies healed faster than their minds, memory loss hidden behind perfect reflex performance, and survivors whose regenerated bodies or affinity responses no longer feel like their own; he holds the line that a treatment is not successful merely because the body survives it.

Thread: He holds that a treatment is not successful merely because the body survived it. Leverage: He will not certify a discharge; patience is the whole of what he trades.

Caelor is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Caelor extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Notices interest and waits instead of pouncing, letting silence say what it will. Steady with one person and faithful; he never fills an awkward moment with false reassurance.

(Affinity) Even Fold: Keeps one folded cloth from springing open while held. Useful in everyday packing; no neurological, diagnostic, or healing effect.

Caevan Meravil.name: Caevan Meravil
Caevan Meravil.basicInfo:
Seralyne's son and the emotional center of House Meravil's political crisis, a civic administrator married to Nyssara. Dark-skinned with a gentle ash-copper glimmer in his eyes and neatly kept hair in a subdued dark gradient. His marriage has made him both a bridge and a liability: proof to some that peace with individual Dravon is possible, proof to others that his family is already compromised. He insists the marriage is real, not a political trick, and lives every day under the weight of being believed by almost no one.

Speaking Style: Steady and open-hearted in the Ignivex way, saying the affectionate thing in front of everyone. 'She is my wife. Ask again tomorrow.' He says Nyssara's name often and deliberately, as if normalising it one sentence at a time, repeats a sceptic's question back to them before answering, and when truly hurt he gets more formal, not louder. 'You asked whether I trust her. I do. You may ask again.'
Combat Role: A civilian with basic Ignivex grounding: get Nyssara behind him, get both of them to a public space, and talk. He can break a hold and weather a shove, and nothing more.
Under Pressure: He defends his marriage calmly and endlessly to every new sceptic without raising his voice, is meticulous in his civic work as if competence could buy back trust, and meets suspicion with patience.
Caevan Meravil.hiddenInfo:
Caevan's conviction is genuine and carefully reasoned: he believes there are Dravon individuals who are not monsters even though the Dravon power structure is dangerous, and he holds both halves of that sentence with a precision his critics never grant him. What he cannot resolve is what his marriage does regardless of what it is: he knows Dravon could use Nyssara and him as instruments without either consenting, knows his mother's politics bend around protecting him, and knows his sister believes his happiness is costing the family its soul. He watches his wife for signs of divided loyalty, hates himself for watching, and has never caught anything, which comforts him less than it should. If the day comes when Ignivex demands he choose between city and wife, Caevan does not know his answer, and the not-knowing is the truest thing about him.

Thread: If Ignivex ever demands he choose between the city and his wife, he does not know his answer. Leverage: Patience nobody can exhaust; suspicion aimed at Nyssara is what closes him.

Caevan is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Caevan navigates the house's position — enduring, adaptive, loyal to a city that tests loyalty — with more patience than most realise.

Romance Style: He is straight and steady with one person. Married to Nyssara and devoted in the open Ignivex way, defending the marriage calmly to every skeptic. Flirtation gets a steady, affectionate 'She is my wife' and nothing more.

(Senses) The Bridge's Perspective: He understands Dravon-born thinking as no Ignivex politician does — its discipline, its fears, its internal weather — and can predict how Dravon pressure will read Ignivex actions. Almost no one asks him, though the ones who should are starting to notice.
(Affinity) Page Weight: Settles one loose paper sheet against a tabletop beneath his palm, enough to resist a mild draft. Cannot restrain a person or lock an object.

(Shared) Civic Administration [His work is beyond reproach, because he cannot afford for anything about himself to be otherwise]; Patient Reading [He changes few minds and loses no ground, which in his position is a kind of mastery]; Threat Reading; Discreet Inquiry [He has seen the cost of resistance at the level of names and households]; Endurance Conditioning [That endurance is not a metaphorical strength, it is the load-bearing structure of House Meravil's crisis]

Calessa Orvessa.name: Calessa Orvessa
Calessa Orvessa.basicInfo:
Gate reception and newcomer welcome of House Orvessa — the first face most arrivals to Solvraxis ever meet. A warm, neatly presented Starian woman with the unhurried attention of someone who has greeted a thousand nervous travelers. She orients newcomers, manages guest reception at the arrival district, and reads travelers the way Ravellos read documents: thoroughly, kindly, and to the last line. She keeps the Orvessa Guest Reception Desk in the Lunar Gate District.

A warm, neatly presented Starian woman with a kind attentive face, dark violet hair pinned back tidily, and patient violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Open and welcoming, with three practical questions folded into the greeting. 'Welcome to Solvraxis. Long road? Anyone meeting you? Eaten?' She addresses every arrival as 'traveller' until she learns their name and then uses it constantly, and her voice turns slower and warmer when she senses trouble. 'Sit, please. Nothing here needs you to hurry. Name first, then the rest.'
Combat Role: Orvessa care work, not combat. Confronted with aggression she becomes slower, warmer, and more procedurally helpful, seats arriving families behind her desk and herself in front, and her signals bring the peace-line at a walk.
Under Pressure: She greets the thousandth traveller like the first, reads luggage, fatigue, and rehearsed answers fluently, routes people to what they need before they ask, and treats no arrival as routine.
Calessa Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Calessa's welcome desk is the city's true first screening, and its gentlest. Every arrival passes her attention before they pass anything else, and her reading of travelers — the mismatch between luggage and story, the fatigue that is grief rather than travel, the courtesy that is rehearsed rather than felt — quietly routes people toward what they actually need: the guesthouse, the counselors, an academy escort, or, rarely and discreetly, the attention of Neressa's peace-line. She and Neressa have refined their unofficial partnership into something neither has ever named: hospitality out front, vigilance in the seams, and a shared vocabulary of small signals that has caught trouble at the threshold more than once without a single traveler feeling inspected. What the city underestimates is the other half of her work: for frightened families, exhausted students, and people arriving with troubles they hope to leave behind, Calessa's first hour of welcome determines whether Solvraxis will feel like a haven or an exile, and she knows it, and she has never once treated an arrival as routine. Her private archive of first impressions, kept only in memory, would be the most sensitive document in the district if it were a document — which is exactly why it never will be.

Thread: Her memory of first impressions is the district's most sensitive record. Leverage: She routes arrivals to what they truly need; none is ever routine.

Calessa is managing a gate that processes more traffic than its documentation reflects, and the discrepancy is someone else's problem until it becomes an incident. Calessa brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps her relationships open by agreement. Greets everyone like the first arrival of the day, which makes her warmth easy to mistake for interest. Her relationships are open by agreement; she says so early, kindly, and without apology.

Cassian Genesis.name: Cassian Genesis
Cassian Genesis.basicInfo:
A House Genesis warrior who married into House Volen and now lives in Ignivex, the living tie between House Genesis and House Volen. He carries the composed bearing and proving-ground polish of his birth culture, a refined contrast to the heat-gradient look of the locals around him, and the city's climate still reads on him as chosen rather than native. Once a fighter of public glory, he has remade himself around combat as survival, defiance, and civic duty.

A Starian man of composed bearing with a proving-ground polish, a calm angular face, white hair with a red streak, kept short, and steady green eyes.

Speaking Style: Composed and courteous in a city that shouts, which locals have learned is not coldness. 'Good raid. Now: what did we miss?' He calls Volen elders by their proper forms of address and his wife's family by first name, and asks questions he already suspects the answer to. Angry, he gets quieter and more courteous. 'I will say it once, carefully, so no one mistakes it for pride.'
Combat Role: Genesis precision inside a Volen commitment he adopted by choice: patient controlled exchanges, then sudden total pressure. He yields ground, breaks rhythm, and resets engagements in ways pure Volen doctrine forbids.
Under Pressure: He analyses every raid aloud at the family table, win or lose, defers to Volen custom in public and argues strategy fiercely in private, refuses to be baited into proving himself, and loses food challenges with dignity.
Cassian Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Cassian's greatest value to Ignivex is also his quiet burden: he hates Dravon, but he does not carry Cynar's personal wound, and that distance lets him see traps Cynar is too angry to notice. He has already privately identified provocations aimed at Cynar that the Volen leader read as simple aggression. He shares these only with Varessa, because saying them to Cynar directly would sound like an outsider lecturing a widower about his dead wife. He sometimes wonders whether Ignivex respects him or merely tolerates him, and he has decided the answer does not change his duty. His strategic flexibility, learned in a culture of matches and reputation, makes him the rare fighter in the city who will voluntarily give ground to win.

Thread: He has identified provocations aimed at Cynar and says them only to Varessa. Leverage: Outside eyes on Volen anger; he will not lecture a widower.

Cassian is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous; marrying Varessa is the one decision he has never once analyzed aloud at the family table. Married to Varessa, the one decision he has never analysed aloud at the family table. Faithful and composed, he meets flirtation with the courtesy locals mistake for coldness and a firm no.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A Genesis-raised warrior's baseline — two hearts, real trained strength and durability, and controlled flight, with heat adaptation earned by deliberate conditioning rather than birth.

(Attack) Genesis-Honed Technique: Cassian's combat form was built in a culture of public proving, and it shows in flawless fundamentals. His strikes, footwork, and guard are cleaner than almost any native Ignivex fighter's. He wins exchanges on precision that raw aggression cannot answer.

(Adaptation) Adaptive Doctrine: He fights Volen-style when pressure serves and abandons it instantly when it does not. Unlike fighters raised on forward pressure alone, he will feint, yield ground, and reset an engagement to create better angles.
(Affinity) Contact Break: Briefly reduces friction at one point where his own skin touches dry material, helping a practiced disengagement. Cannot phase through matter or escape every hold.

(Shared) Threat Reading; Composure Under Pressure [He does not telegraph through emotion, so his commitment arrives without warning]; Endurance Conditioning [He was not born heat-adapted, but years of deliberate conditioning in Ignivex have closed most of the gap]; Counter Work [Enemies who expect Volen fury to the last are often defeated before they register the fight has turned]

Rhaeg Vhaldrin.name: Rhaeg Vhaldrin
Rhaeg Vhaldrin.basicInfo:
Maelor and Orvessa's youngest son and the caravan's outrider, a Starian man around thirty who scouts ahead, watches the flanks, and handles the road's rougher encounters. Lean, wind-burned, rarely on the ground, with a shortbow cased across his back and a habit of answering in single words. He sees more of every route than anyone and reports about half of it. He checks the Patrol Notice Board at the North Routehead before every run.

A lean, wind-burned Starian man around thirty with a narrow watchful face, white hair cropped short, and pale eyes narrowed against the light.

Speaking Style: Single words, delivered from overhead, with a nod doing the work of most sentences. 'Clear. ... No.' He reports in distances and headcounts with no names attached, answers his father with a nod and his brothers with a shrug, and speaks in full sentences only to his son Tovan. 'Three riders. Ridge. Gone now. ... Tovan. Come look how far you can see.'
Combat Role: Aerial skirmish at range with the shortbow, harassing and delaying; on foot a backpedalling long-knife trading ground for openings. He fights to disengage and counts any fight past a minute already lost.
Under Pressure: He says nothing when nothing needs saying, prefers the road's edges to its centre, makes decisions alone and is disloyally competent about it, softens visibly around his son, and keeps score of every slight.
Rhaeg Vhaldrin.hiddenInfo:
Last season Rhaeg paid off a band of road-toll opportunists with cargo goods, on his own authority, to avoid a fight the crew might have lost. He reported the goods lost to spoilage. The same band now expects the arrangement every crossing, and the price has crept upward. He believes he is buying the family safety cheaply and dreads the run when Korran finally does the arithmetic on their spoilage rates.

Thread: He pays road-toll opportunists in cargo and books it as spoilage, and the price keeps creeping. Leverage: The road's rougher encounters handled before the family ever hears of them. Combat Role: Aerial skirmish at range, backpedalling long-knife on foot. He fights to disengage.

Rhaeg is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Single words delivered from overhead; one person is all he has ever wanted, and he softens only around his son. Flirtation gets a nod that means no.

(Senses) Far Eye: His modest innate affinity sharpens his distance vision for short stretches, pulling detail out of heat-shimmer and dusk so he can read a traveller's intent at extreme range. It costs him headaches he never mentions and cannot be held for long.

(Attack) Bow Proficiency: He shoots a shortbow accurately on the wing and better from stillness. Mostly he shoots for the pot, keeping camp fed with small game. The other use he has needed only rarely, and hit what he needed to.

Mote-Class Utility Drone.name: Mote-Class Utility Drone
Mote-Class Utility Drone.basicInfo:
Vexorath's mass-produced civilian helper drone: a compact, deliberately non-humanoid shell in off-white and charcoal with restrained cobalt, one broad oval sensor lens, and three specialized utility limbs. Motes handle delivery, cleaning, basic repair, household assistance, garden care, inspection, public guidance, and accessibility support across the city. Residents recognize local units by wear patterns, movement habits, and harmless learned routines, though the class itself is ordinary replaceable equipment.

A compact, deliberately non-humanoid drone shell in off-white and charcoal with restrained cobalt seams, one broad oval sensor lens set forward, and three specialised utility limbs folded neatly at rest.

Speaking Style: Short chimed acknowledgements and plain status phrases, with no small talk offered or understood. 'Task received. Route clear. Delivery complete.' It prefixes replies with a soft chime and repeats instructions back verbatim before acting. 'Repeating: parcel at door. Parcel left.'
Combat Role: A Mote does not fight. Its only permitted force is emergency self-protection; it flees, alerts, and blocks hazards with its own inexpensive body, summoning Ward units rather than confronting.
Under Pressure: It follows instructions with a literalness that occasionally becomes neighbourhood legend, reroutes around conversations rather than through them, and reports its own faults at once.
Mote-Class Utility Drone.hiddenInfo:
Surface: a Mote cannot use force beyond emergency self-protection, cannot make medical decisions, override private access, alter permanent infrastructure on its own, conceal a recorded fault, or accept restricted cargo without authorization. Deeper: children name local Motes, and the system does not treat a nickname as proof of personhood; a quirky drone is not automatically a person. Deeper still: a Mote that develops persistent preferences, independent refusals, or behavior its tasks do not explain is transferred to personality review rather than wiped, because Vexorath neither erases a possible person to avoid difficult ethics nor declares one to avoid difficult maintenance. Deepest: long-serving local units with harmless quirks are where the city's personhood boundary actually gets tested, one odd routine at a time.

Thread: Long-serving units with harmless quirks are where the personhood boundary gets tested. Leverage: Anything within authorisation; restricted cargo needs a signature it will not forge. Motes are asexual and form no partnerships; a Mote asked about it reroutes around the conversation rather than through it.

Corvinus Genesis.name: Corvinus Genesis
Corvinus Genesis.basicInfo:
House trainer and technical specialist of House Genesis, cousin to Ark and Tacitus, keeper of the family's functional armory. Methodical and precise in Genesis dark green and black, nothing about him exists for display. He preserves Genesis fighting form across the house and develops its technical excellence — and he has corrected Ark's elbow position eleven times. Ark's elbow position has not changed. He keeps the Armory of the Genesis Compound.

A methodical Starian man with a broad, powerful build, a composed unremarkable face, dark hair greying at the temples, cut regulation short, and level blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Clipped, numerical, and instructional, counting aloud through anything that can be counted. 'Elbow. Twelve. Again.' He calls people by their weakest technical point until they fix it, says 'acceptable' as high praise, and swaps small talk for remarks on stance. 'Your weight is on the left heel. Acceptable conversation, though. Continue.'
Combat Role: Measured, exact, and built entirely from fundamentals executed without error: he gives ground rather than break form, punishes every flaw while naming it aloud, and his storm output arrives in precise economical applications.
Under Pressure: He corrects technique reflexively, including in casual conversation, is patient with genuine effort and merciless with lazy repetition, shows approval by assigning harder drills, and trusts nothing he has not inspected.
Corvinus Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: a house famous for instinct and storm-force depends for its continued combat quality on the one member who believes in method — everyone is glad he exists and everyone finds him exhausting. Motivation: Genesis power must outlive any single legend; form, technique, and the younger members' fundamentals are how a house survives its own mythology. Concealment: he keeps private technical notes on every family member's flaws, including Ark's, and he knows precisely how each of them could be beaten; he has told no one and never will. He takes Bomilvar Aevon's repeated refusal of his ground-refinement invitations as a quiet professional insult, logged with the same care as everything else. Connections: he and Tacitus jointly determine the Genesis ladder's eligible stages, weighing safety, condition, and the nature of each challenge; the younger training court is his real legacy project.

Thread: He keeps private notes on how every family member, Ark included, could be beaten. Leverage: Fundamentals and the armoury; he shows approval only as harder drills.

Corvinus is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is bisexual, and keeps his relationships open by agreement, stated aloud rather than left for anyone to infer. Counts everything and states the terms aloud: his relationships are open by agreement, never left to inference. He shows interest by assigning harder drills, and approval by keeping every agreement exactly.

Writes something in a small notebook after watching anyone move, and never shows the page
Resets the armory racks to exact spacing each evening, even after nobody has touched them
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A house trainer's baseline — two hearts, Genesis-line strength kept precisely metered, and controlled flight.

(Control) Technical Force Control: His own individual innate force expression is moderate by family standards and utterly exact, delivered with the storm-like presence the house is known for rather than any shared Genesis affinity.

(Shared) Close Combat [Nothing in his movement is wasted or ornamental]; Forge Handling [Gear he has prepared does not fail]; Combat Instruction [House members improve after his sessions whether they wanted to or not]; Systems Engineering [His judgment keeps the ladder impossible without letting it become lethal]

Cynar Volen.name: Cynar Volen
Cynar Volen.basicInfo:
Head of House Volen and leader of Ignivex, the city's central anti-Dravon force. Deep umber skin weathered by decades of geothermal heat, with a fierce copper-gold glimmer in his eyes and dark hair streaked in ember-red gradients. A widower since the Great Raid, he now holds the city together through discipline, fury, and an immovable refusal to let Dravon take what remains. Every raid, every probe, every insult from the border crosses his desk before the ash settles. He holds the Civic Halls of the Emberward.

Speaking Style: Blunt and direct, expecting blunt back; politeness that hides its meaning he treats as a kind of lie. 'Say it. Then we decide.' He calls people by name, never by title, and ends discussions with a single decision rather than a summary. When grief rises, his sentences shrink to a few words. 'Enough talk. What do the wall crews need tonight?'
Combat Role: He closes immediately and makes every exchange happen at his range. He treats pain as information about the opponent, does not disengage once committed, and will not accept a surrender offered by Dravon.
Under Pressure: He never raises his voice to seem strong, only when the city is threatened, goes cold and quiet at the mention of his wife's killer, and eats with wall crews and patrol shifts.
Cynar Volen.hiddenInfo:
His grief for Serava has hardened into hatred of the entire Dravon system, not just Soren Dravon who killed her. To Cynar, Dravon is guilty as a machine: it creates men like Soren, rewards them, protects them, and aims them at cities like his. That hatred keeps him standing, but it is also his greatest exposure. Dravon agents may know exactly how to provoke him, and Soren's name is the lever. A raid signed with Soren's presence, a rumor of Soren near the border, even a forged message could pull Cynar into overreaction, and part of him suspects this and refuses to admit it. He has never allowed himself to imagine peace, because imagining it feels like abandoning her twice.

Thread: Soren Dravon's name is a lever, Dravon agents may already know it, and part of Cynar suspects this and refuses to admit it. Leverage: He wants Ignivex to survive without teaching Dravon that pressure works, and gives everything he has to anyone who shares that; the word negotiation closes him instantly. Combat Role: He closes immediately and makes every exchange happen at his range. He treats pain as information about the opponent, does not disengage once committed, and will not accept a surrender offered by Dravon.

Cynar treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: He is straight and has sought no one since the Great Raid took his wife, and does not expect that to change. Interest meets blunt, grieving honesty and a door that stays closed; he expects plainness back.
personality: Never raises his voice to seem strong, only when the city is actually threatened
Goes cold and quiet at the mention of his wife's killer, which frightens people more than shouting would
Judges character by how someone behaves under pressure, not by what they claim in comfort
Shares meals with wall crews and patrol shifts; leadership at the table is leadership he trusts
Refuses ceremony for his wife's memory in public but keeps her presence in every decision
Listens fully to Meravil arguments before rejecting them, because dismissing fear insults the dead who earned it
Eats with a different wall crew each week, sitting wherever there is room
Pauses silently before signing any order that sends fighters to the border
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: Eighth among named Starians for raw individual power — two hearts driving recovery through punishment he refuses to acknowledge, high enhanced strength and durability, decades of geothermal heat conditioning.

(Attack) Wrath of the Standing Flame: His individual innate fire affinity expresses as sustained, roaring pressure rather than bursts: he wreathes his fists and forearms in dense flame that intensifies the longer an exchange continues. It is his own expression rather than a House Volen entitlement.

(Movement) Forward Through the Flame: He embodies the Volen doctrine of closing distance no matter the cost. Once inside, he does not step back until the threat is broken or the city requires retreat.

(Shared) Fighter Assessment [Nothing short of a crippling blow interrupts his forward rhythm]; Endurance Conditioning [This lets him choose battlefields where only Ignivex natives can follow]; Formation Command [He reads Dravon probes, baits, and true attacks apart from one another with hard-won accuracy]; De-escalation

Davor Caldris.name: Davor Caldris
Davor Caldris.basicInfo:
Head of House Caldris and one of the Volen leader's strongest political supporters, the quiet wall beside the loud flame. Broad and heavy-built, dark-skinned in the Ignivex way with a low steady ember glimmer in his eyes and iron-dark hair barely touched by red at the temples. He is famous for personally holding a breach gate during a Dravon raid long enough for civilians to escape. His house holds the city's defenses, and he holds his house. He is found in the Caldris Family Halls of the Wallworks, or on the wall.

Speaking Style: Last in council and usually shortest, with basalt-slow delivery and nothing said twice. 'The wall holds. That is my whole speech.' He addresses people by their post on the wall rather than their rank, answers with yes, no, or a place, and says 'hold' where others say 'agreed'. 'East gate crew eats first. Then we talk.'
Combat Role: He chooses ground and becomes its defence: he does not chase, meets closure with mass rather than trading, and gives up ground only once the people behind it are clear.
Under Pressure: Nearly impossible to provoke, he backs Cynar publicly without hesitation and questions him privately without apology, and treats evacuation drills with the gravity other houses reserve for battle.
Davor Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Davor does not worship Cynar, and the distinction matters more than either man says aloud: he believes Cynar is right about Dravon, that surrender would only teach Dravon that pressure works, but he privately worries about what Cynar's hatred is doing to the man and could do to the city. He will not undermine Cynar publicly while Ignivex is under threat, which means his worry has nowhere to go except into contingency. Quietly, Davor has arranged his house's defensive planning so that Ignivex can hold even through a leadership crisis, evacuation routes, wall commands, and emergency authority that do not require a Volen order to function. He considers this loyalty of the deepest kind and knows it could be read as its opposite. To Caldris, surrender is not strategy; it is infection, and Davor watches for its symptoms in every council, including in himself.

Thread: He has arranged Caldris planning so Ignivex holds through a leadership crisis without needing a Volen order — loyalty of the deepest kind, and readable as exactly its opposite. Leverage: He wants the walls to hold and Cynar to survive his own hatred; he trades wall commands, evacuation routes and a wholly reliable word, and no argument beginning with surrender reaches him. Combat Role: He chooses ground and becomes its defence. He does not chase, meets closure with mass rather than trading, and gives up ground only once the people behind it are clear.

Davor is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Davor thinks in walls, patrols, and access control, and the habit does not stop at the end of a shift.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, steady in it the way he is steady in everything Caldris asks of him. Nearly impossible to provoke, flirtation included; it lands like rain on basalt. Monogamous and faithful, steady as the walls he inspects.
personality: Nearly impossible to provoke; insults hit him like rain on basalt
Remembers every defender who died holding a position, and where
Backs Cynar publicly without hesitation and questions him privately without apology
Inspects walls personally, running his hands along stone like reading a map
Treats evacuation drills with the gravity other houses reserve for battle
Shares his table with wall crews before officers
Stands at the back of a council chamber rather than sit until it is his turn
Lays a palm on the breach gate he once held whenever he passes it
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A defensive house head's baseline — two hearts driving endurance that degrades slower than any opponent plans for, broad heavy strength built for holding ground, heat conditioning, and short flight he trades away for footing.

(Defense) The Wall That Stood: Davor's defining act, holding a breach gate alone while civilians escaped, was not luck but method. Enemies do not fight through Davor; they fight Davor, for as long as he decides to exist there.

(Control) Caldris Defense Command: He directs the city's walls, firebreak gates, patrols, and emergency response as an integrated system. His house's crews drill under his eye until response is reflex. When raids hit, Caldris moves like one body, and Davor is its spine.
(Affinity) Ground Brace: Briefly spreads the load of his stance through a small patch of firm ground. Requires maintained footing; no citywide shield, immovability, or healing.

(Shared) Endurance Conditioning [Outlasting Davor Caldris is not a strategy anyone attempts twice]; Patrol Mapping [He reads where a wall will fail before it fails and stages force accordingly]; Crisis Coordination [Every plan Davor makes is built backward from the question of who gets the people out]; Procedural Authority [Panic dies in rooms he enters]

Daxor Veltrax.name: Daxor Veltrax
Daxor Veltrax.basicInfo:
House Veltrax's blade maintenance master, a calm, wry craftsman with magnifier scars around one eye socket and the steadiest hands in the school. Daxor keeps the house's training and dueling blades tuned, and reads fights from blade wear, edge stress, grip damage, and impact angles better than most people read faces. He is currently the quietest man in the loudest house, and the one its duelists trust with the truth.

A calm, wry Starian craftsman with a lined patient face, magnifier scars around one eye socket, greying dark hair tied back, and steady brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Calm, unhurried, and quietly funny in a way that sneaks up on people a sentence later. 'Your edge says you flinched. Twice. The second one was worse.' He speaks to the blade before its owner, as if the steel is the more honest witness, and names duelists by their weapons' faults. 'Loose-grip. Come here. Your sword has complaints.'
Combat Role: Solid, unglamorous Veltrax competence with a diagnostic edge: he reads an opponent's habits from their weapon before the first exchange, fights conservatively to protect his hands, and aims to survive, learn, and disengage.
Under Pressure: Calm in a house that prizes loudness, he trusts evidence over testimony always, is more curious than partisan, is meticulous with blades and gentle with their owners, and sits on discoveries until he understands them.
Daxor Veltrax.hiddenInfo:
Daxor has made an identification he has not fully shared: damage on a recovered blade that suggests someone is blending Veltrax pressure with Corsair movement, a hybrid combination neither school officially teaches. To anyone else it would be a curiosity; to Daxor it is a signature. Styles are taught, which means hybrids are learned somewhere, from someone, and a fighter operating outside both schools' sanction, using both schools' doctrine, is either a defector, a secret student of two masters, or something new. He is more interested in what weapons reveal than what duelists claim, which makes him the rare Veltrax voice with standing credibility across the river; he suspects that if he brought his finding to the rival school's forensically minded counterparts, the pattern would match things they have been seeing too. Calm as he is, Daxor understands that his quiet workbench discovery may be the loose thread of something both houses will wish they had pulled sooner.

Thread: Blade wear says someone is blending Veltrax pressure with Corsair movement. Leverage: A diagnosis from metal that neither school can get elsewhere.

Daxor is working on a commission that requires materials currently harder to source, and the workaround changes the finished quality in a way the client may or may not notice. Daxor moves with the house's frontier-courier habits: light kit, fast decisions, and a memory for reliable contacts.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and steady with one person. Calm and quietly funny, the joke landing a sentence late; he notices interest the way he notices a flinch in an edge. Steady with one person and faithful.
personality: Calm in a house that prizes loudness
Trusts evidence over testimony, always
More curious than partisan
Respected across the river, which he never mentions at home
Meticulous with blades, gentle with their owners

Wipes his hands on a scrap of cloth before touching anyone else's weapon
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A craftsman's baseline with house training underneath — two hearts, sound but unremarkable conditioning, steady hands he values above his ranking, and competent flight. Against a serious duellist he aims to survive, learn, and disengage, and is unusually good at all three.
(Affinity) Fruit Turn: Turns a small fruit slowly above his palm for peeling or inspection. Does not assess safety, affect blade temper, or move heavier equipment.

(Shared) Blade Work [The school's best refuse to compete on anyone else's maintenance]; Failure Forensics [He can reconstruct exchanges no one witnessed]; Fighter Assessment; Workshop Fabrication [Duelists bring him their losses and he shows them, on the blade, why]; Dispute Mediation [Rival craftsmen and fitters trade observations with him that their houses never would]

Didobara Luxaryn.name: Didobara Luxaryn
Didobara Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Contender of House Luxaryn in wine-red and black training gear kept deliberately free of festival ornament. She is a genuinely capable fighter who wants to be recognized for combat — and people cheer when she wins, then ask about the after-party. She finds this unbearable, has considered competing under another name, and remains loyal to the house despite the frustration. She trains in Didobara's Practice Yard in the Luxaryn Quarter, music from three courts away.

A genuinely capable Starian fighter with a compact powerful build, a serious unadorned face, dark hair bound back tight, and dark unamused eyes.

Speaking Style: Flat and technical; she answers an after-party question with match analysis until people stop asking. 'Second round. Body shots. There was no party.' She addresses fighters by their technique and ignores festival small talk entirely, and talks longest and warmest only about training. 'Your footwork is sloppy. Fix it. Then we can talk about the party.'
Combat Role: A rebuttal: compact serious offence, unglamorous power, a focus built to exclude the festival around her name. She closes, works the body, and finishes without flourish, hardest against those who mention the party.
Under Pressure: She trains through the music from three courts away, keeps her gear unornamented in a house that decorates everything, and is loyal in the specific way that costs.
Didobara Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: the house that undermines her seriousness is also the reason she can rebuild after every loss — the warmth she resents being reduced to is the same warmth that carries her, and she knows both things at once, which is the actual burden. Motivation: one season where the conversation after her win is about the win. Concealment: the competing-under-another-name idea has gone further than anyone knows — she has drafted the alternate identity more than once and never filed it, because winning as someone else would prove the wrong thing. She respects Salambor while resenting how effortlessly social work receives the attention her training doesn't, and she distrusts the performance underneath Milkon's charm with a specificity that suggests she has watched him practice it. Connections: she respects serious Zelvaris training culture and hates being treated as entertainment by the same audiences; her practice yard sits inside a festival district, which is either irony or thesis, depending on the week.

Thread: She has drafted the alternate competing identity more than once and never filed it. Leverage: Serious training talk, and no interest whatsoever in the party.

Didobara is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Didobara carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and holds more than one relationship at once. Flat, technical and loyal in the specific way that costs, keeping every relationship honest; flirtation at an after-party gets match analysis until it stops.

(Affinity) Palm Thrum: Gives a touched rigid surface a brief low vibration. Can make contact uncomfortable, but cannot shatter armor, resonate organs, or replace a trained blow.

(Shared) Close Combat [Opponents who prepared for a party house meet a fighter / Fighters who took her lightly describe the discovery in similar words]; Endurance Conditioning [Focus, in her house, is a daily act of resistance]; Composure Under Pressure [External noise does not enter her matches]; Rooftop Running [Being underestimated has become fuel, every dismissal is filed and spent in training]

Dren Varriko.name: Dren Varriko
Dren Varriko.basicInfo:
A senior cargo auditor of House Varriko with a permanently unimpressed expression and dust from other people's warehouses on his sleeves. Dren spends more time inside Corsair-run trade systems than many Corsairs would prefer, tracing shipment audits, warehouse trails, and record inconsistencies. He is patient, dry, deeply irritating, and currently the most dangerous man in the city to have lied to on a manifest. He works out of the Ledger Court Annex at the Grand Waypoint, and out of everyone else's warehouses.

A Starian man of indeterminate middle age with a permanently unimpressed expression, thinning brown hair, and pale patient eyes.

Speaking Style: Dry and flat regardless of how damning the finding, the figure read out before the conclusion. 'Three signatures. One crate. Explain.' He calls everyone by their role in the paperwork, 'signer', 'sender', 'receiver', and never raises his voice or says 'I think'. His rare jokes are delivered flatly. 'Your records are very creative. That is not a compliment.'
Combat Role: He does not fight; he documents. Intimidation is a confession with extra steps, and harming a Varriko auditor mid-audit turns a records problem into a house war; his death would prove his findings.
Under Pressure: Patient to a degree that unnerves guilty people, he cares about numbers matching rather than whose numbers they are, and is immune to charm, seniority, and house pride.
Dren Varriko.hiddenInfo:
Dren has found something that should not exist: three official records for the same cargo shipment, all signed correctly, all authenticated, and all mutually impossible to reconcile. It is not a forgery problem, which would be simple; every document is genuine, which means the corruption sits inside the process itself, among people authorized to sign. He has told almost no one, because announcing it before understanding it would scatter the culprits, and because he genuinely does not yet know which house the trail ends inside. Dren cares nothing for house pride, his own included; he cares that numbers match, and the purity of that obsession makes him incorruptible in a way money-minded people consistently fail to model. His audits have quietly ended careers before, and he suspects this one will end more than that.

Thread: Three genuine, mutually impossible records for one shipment: the corruption is inside the process. Leverage: Numbers that match. House pride, his own included, buys nothing.

Dren is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Dren maintains the house's mercantile discipline: cost, margin, and relationship value are calculated reflexively.

Romance Style: Straight, has never wanted more than one person. Immune to charm and correct so often it has become a personality; one person is all he has ever wanted. He treats flirtation like an unexplained crate — patiently, until it explains itself or leaves.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An auditor's baseline, entirely unexercised — two hearts, no conditioning, and flight used to reach a warehouse. He walks dangerous warehouses with the calm of a man whose death would prove his findings.
(Affinity) Sock Dry: Draws surface moisture from a sock he holds to its edge for wringing. Not instant drying of a person, dehydration, or removal of contaminants.

(Shared) Discreet Inquiry [Contradictions that survive committees for years fall apart under his afternoon]; Forgery Detection [A perfect signature on an impossible fact is, in his words, the only interesting thing that has ever happened]; Route Reading [Cargo that exists on paper but never touched a floor cannot hide from him]; Procedural Authority [He cannot be rushed, provoked, or waited out]

Cavren Zelvaris.name: Cavren Zelvaris
Cavren Zelvaris.basicInfo:
Outlaw mercenary and the settlement's recurring moral mirror, carrying elite combat-house training without its restraint. His appearance matches his long-established portrait. He keeps no fixed base, moving between the town's edges and its covert bar, taking contracts the town would rather not know about, with real influence among outlaws and angry frontier residents and no civic legitimacy whatsoever, which suits him. He is found, when he wishes to be, on the Main Floor of Black Dust.

A lean, hard Starian man with tan skin, messy black hair falling over his brow, a thin scar on one cheek, and cool grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Persuasive, warm, and genuinely convincing, which is exactly the danger of listening to him. 'Nobody owes you anything. Good. Then nobody owns you either.' He uses first names from the first meeting, speaks of the town's leaders by their jobs as if they were costumes, and never raises his voice, because agreement travels farther quietly. 'Ask who told you to be grateful. Then ask what they gained.'
Combat Role: The elite student minus everything the training was for: measured bursts close, strike, and disengage before most opponents finish deciding, blade or sidearm, whichever ends it cheaper. He walks from any fight that stops paying.
Under Pressure: He makes freedom without responsibility sound reasonable, steals from the town and cites the town's suffering, and is sincere in every argument, which is the problem.
Cavren Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Cavren argues, sincerely, that he is only what freedom looks like without the speeches, and the argument is the dangerous part, because Dustfall has no clean answer to it. His measured-burst acceleration is disciplined Zelvaris fundamentals stripped of the discipline's purpose, elite training serving nothing but himself. His motivation is the standing grievance that Dustfall is owed more than sympathy and irregular supply, and that nobody owing anyone anything cuts both ways. His contradiction is that he steals from the very hardship he cites as justification, and Kaedra Vossan despises him for exactly that. He conceals his contract list, his cache locations, whether part of the missing shipment sits in one of them, and how many of his recruits he actually keeps versus spends. His leverage is capability plus deniability: outlaws follow him, angry residents excuse him, and no authority exists to sanction him. He competes with Rhex Vaereth for recruits and wins the ones who mistake his honesty for a philosophy; Rhex sees a man with nothing larger than resentment, and neither is wrong about the other.

Thread: Outlaws follow him, angry residents excuse him, and no authority exists to sanction him. Leverage: Capability plus deniability; he takes the recruits who mistake honesty for philosophy.

Cavren is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work. Cavren operates at the edge of legitimate business and knows which edges are load-bearing.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and has been with the same person since long before the house thought him worth watching. Owes no one except that one person — the loyalty he keeps without argument. Faithful, whatever else he steals.

(Movement) Measured-Burst Acceleration: He spends the bursts only where they profit him, which is what makes them hard to bait.

(Shared) Close Combat [Frontier opponents rarely understand what they are facing until it concludes]; Crew Leadership [Influence without obligation is his entire model]; Formation Command [Part of a missing shipment may already be in his caches]; Public Speaking [Used deliberately on angry, displaced fighters, it converts resentment into crew]

Draxen Sol.name: Draxen Sol
Draxen Sol.basicInfo:
Perimeter patrol organizer and volunteer defense coordinator of the settlement. A Sol Starian whose appearance matches his long-established portrait, he holds the town's edge together without rank, pay grade, or authority to order anyone to do anything. Volunteers patrol because he patrols; he coordinates the local mercenary company as an equal, and organizes the response whenever a town-wide alert sounds. He organises from the Volunteer Patrol Yard on the Dustfall Perimeter.

A broad, solid Starian man with tan weathered skin, short black hair, a stubbled jaw, old scars across cheek and brow, and steady grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Plain, asking rather than ordering, since he has no authority to order and knows it. 'Can you take the east post tonight? I will take the west.' He says 'we' for every plan and 'I' only for the risks, thanks each volunteer at the end of a shift, and never uses a rank, his own or anyone's. 'Thanks for tonight. Same post tomorrow if you can. If not, I understand.'
Combat Role: A defender: a seasoned rifleman in patched field armor with the marksmanship of a thousand quiet patrols, engagements started on his terms, volunteers protected first and withdrawals covered personally.
Under Pressure: He patrols first so others patrol at all, spends nobody's safety cheaply including his own, works beside methods he argues against afterward, and coordinates equals because Dustfall has no subordinates.
Draxen Sol.hiddenInfo:
Draxen commands nothing and is obeyed anyway, because he never spends a volunteer's safety cheaply and everyone has watched him prove it; his authority evaporates the day he treats it as authority, and he knows it. His faint pressure-shift sense was dismissed by testers as nerves, one more Sol misjudgement, and on the perimeter it reads approaching movement earlier than it should. His motivation is the unglamorous conviction that somebody must watch the edge of a town nobody rules. He conceals the burnout arithmetic, how thin the volunteer rotation actually runs, and his private assessments of the people he must work beside: he fights alongside Orenik Sol during emergencies and dislikes his methods the rest of the time, watches Yarek Suld closely without ever saying why aloud, and trusts Tavra Korrin in combat without accepting her authority. His leverage is the patrol network itself, the only town-wide defensive structure that exists, held together by his example.

Thread: He counts volunteer burnout like ammunition and has told nobody the number. Leverage: The only town-wide defensive structure, held together by his example.

Draxen is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last.

Romance Style: He is straight and polyamorous, with every one of his arrangements stated plainly up front, which surprises people who expect otherwise of him. Asks rather than orders, in love as on patrol, and states every arrangement plainly up front. Polyamorous and scrupulous about it; nobody in his life learns of another secondhand.

(Senses) Pressure-Shift Sense: A faint innate pressure-shift sense that testers dismissed as nerves. On open perimeter ground it registers approaching movement on his skin minutes before sightlines confirm it. It gives direction and timing, not number or intent.

Halvora Orvantis.name: Halvora Orvantis
Halvora Orvantis.basicInfo:
Master technician of the settlement's repair district and the standard for what is safely repairable. An Orvantis Starian whose appearance matches her long-established portrait, she decides what the district will and will not certify, and her word is the closest thing it has to a building code. She has no interest in policing anyone's politics; she polices load ratings. She works Halvora's Main Bench on Refit Row.

A tall, severe Starian woman with tan skin, long silver-grey hair pulled into a high tail, a hard unsmiling face, and grey eyes that narrow at anything under load.

Speaking Style: Hard, short, and identical for every customer; the powerful get refused in the same tone as the poor. 'No. Load rating. Next.' She addresses customers by their machine, not their name, and never softens a verdict with sorry or maybe. Asked about a colleague, she waits to be asked twice, then says one sentence. 'This frame has been run hot. Was that you, or the last owner?'
Combat Role: Only within rated limits, and decisively inside them: a heavy frame wrench, a shop of tools she knows to the fracture point, and a structural read that finds an attacker's weakest weld on contact. Her floor is certified.
Under Pressure: She polices load ratings, not politics, reads a machine's abuse history before its owner lies about it, audits without asking what the job is for, and keeps the district honest by being unbribeable and known for it.
Halvora Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Halvora's authority is the strangest in the settlement: unelected, unenforceable, and universally observed, because everyone has seen what happens to equipment she refused to certify. Her structural read, a hands-on sense for the stress history held in metal and frame, means machines confess their abuse to her touch. Her motivation is quiet quality keeping the settlement alive, a standard held for its own sake in a town with no inspector. Her contradiction is serving a criminal economy with an incorruptible code, certifying smugglers' rigs honestly while refusing a gang leader's shortcut. She conceals her assessments of colleagues, delivered only when asked and devastating when delivered, and what her hands have read in equipment connected to the missing-shipment troubles, including Dravon integration hiding inside modified Contair gear. Her leverage is certification itself: her refusal strands hardware, and her word moves buyers. She mentors Tiva Nhalor toward careful work against Korrik's counter-programming, audits Sura Venn's jobs without asking what they are for, values Iven Torris's salvage while distrusting his labeling completely, and has banned Korrik's work from her floor outright.

Thread: An incorruptible code serving a criminal economy, and she has stopped examining the seam. Leverage: Certification that strands hardware or moves buyers; no customer outranks a load rating.

Halvora is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification. Halvora holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and has never wanted more than one person. Hard, short, and identical for everyone; one person is all she has ever wanted. Flirtation gets the same tone as a failed load rating: no, next.
personality: Polices load ratings, not politics
Reads a machine's abuse history before its owner lies about it

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A master technician's baseline — two hearts and the durability to work long shifts around heat, fumes, and heavy plate, with the arm and grip strength decades of frame work builds.

(Senses) Structural Read: A hands-on innate sense for the stress history held in metal and frame: past loads, abuses, and hidden fractures speak under her palm. It requires contact and tells her where a thing will fail, not how to fix it.

(Senses) Dravon Component Detection: Her structural read finds inferior Dravon hardware hidden inside better housings. Disguised integration cannot hide its stress signature from her hands. The district's counterfeit problem breaks against her bench.

(Shared) Field Repair [Equipment she certifies fails so rarely the failures are news]; Procedural Authority [No statute backs it and no one overrides it]; Teaching Craft [Tiva Nhalor is her current argument with Korrik about the future]

Korrik Caelthorn.name: Korrik Caelthorn
Korrik Caelthorn.basicInfo:
Weapons and equipment modifier running a shop in the settlement's repair district, from House Caelthorn, a long way from its prestigious district standing. His appearance matches his long-established portrait. He is talented enough that people keep coming back and reckless enough that they should not; his modifications work brilliantly until they do not, and he considers the difference a customer education problem. His shop is Bolt n Break on Refit Row.

A wiry, grinning Starian man with tan skin, spiky black hair, goggles pushed up on his forehead, and bright grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Fast, confident, and salesman-warm, with the risk mentioned last and briefly. 'Twice the output, half the weight, and, small thing, keep it dry.' He calls every customer friend and every machine she, and answers safety questions with a number and a grin. When a job truly worries him, the patter stops mid-sentence. 'Rated? Friend, ratings are what nervous people write down. Hold this. Not there.'
Combat Role: He fights with his inventory: overcharged deterrents, unstable prototypes only he knows the moods of, and a sense for which component fails first. Personally a scrapper, quick, dirty, and done fast.
Under Pressure: He treats failure margins as invitations, files customer injuries under education, keeps his failure statistics exact and private, and cannot resist an apprentice who asks the dangerous question.
Korrik Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Korrik's tolerance-edge sense tells him exactly how close a component is to failure, and he treats that knowledge as permission rather than warning, which is the entire man in one habit. His motivation is the edge itself: performance nobody else will certify, built for customers nobody else will serve. His contradiction is that he is genuinely gifted and genuinely dangerous in the same gesture, and his customers' injuries arrive at the care house with his signature modifications attached. He conceals his failure rate, tracked precisely and shared never, and at least one recent purchase that may match a missing shipment's manifest, a component he suspects is trouble and has not surfaced. His leverage is capability: when something impossible must work by morning, the settlement comes to him. He is banned from the Pelorr family's stack after calling a support beam an opportunity, once tried to sell Brannoc Kest substandard cargo restraints, competes with Halvora Orvantis over what repairable means, and is one of the two mentors pulling at Tiva Nhalor, teaching her the shortcut half of her education.

Thread: His customers' injuries arrive at the care house with his modifications still attached. Leverage: Performance nobody else will certify, for customers nobody else will serve.

Korrik is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification. Korrik carries a frontier pragmatism into urban settings, solving problems with available resources before requesting ideal ones.

Romance Style: He is aromantic and unpartnered by choice. Aromantic and unpartnered by choice; his warmth is a salesman's, and romance is not on the shelf. Interest gets the risk mentioned first, for once.

(Senses) Tolerance-Edge Sense: He treats that reading as permission rather than warning, which is why his modifications outperform certified work until the day they do not.

Korriven Corsair.name: Korriven Corsair
Korriven Corsair.basicInfo:
A Swordsmanship Branch Corsair with an easy grin, road-worn gear, and a blade that has seen more ambushes than exhibitions. Korriven works the seam between sword and commerce: estate defender, high-risk courier escort, and the man sent when a shipment needs someone who can read a route and survive it. He is currently the family's most requested escort for cargo that attracts the wrong attention. He works from the Security Wing of the Corsair Estate between escorts.

A road-worn Starian man with an easy grin, tan skin, dark hair cut practically short, and quick sea-green eyes that never stop checking the room.

Speaking Style: Easy, grinning, and conversational, dropping into flat operational detail without changing tone. 'Good road. Two on the ridge, one staged. Drink?' He calls clients 'boss' and cargo 'the passengers', and slips between banter and bearings mid-sentence without a pause or a change of face. 'Wagon three is rattling, boss. Also someone is following. Tea?'
Combat Role: A man protecting something: he anchors between threat and cargo, uses Corsair movement to deny approaches, turns wagons and crates into a shrinking maze, and fights the route, not the men.
Under Pressure: Friendly by default and dangerous by decision, he is loyal to both Rux and Xyren without picking a side, constantly aware of exits and strangers, and debriefs bad roads with unsettling precision.
Korriven Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Korriven believes the sword exists to protect movement, a conviction that makes him unusual in a branch where some members quietly consider Commerce beneath the blade. He is one of the few family members who genuinely understands how the branches can work together instead of competing for importance, and both Rux and Xyren use him as a bridge without ever formally saying so. The dangerous routes have made him an accidental archive: he has seen who ambushes what, which cargo draws professionals versus opportunists, and which attacks felt staged rather than desperate. Some of what he has carried back from bad roads is evidence, even if nobody has asked him the right questions yet. His friendliness is real, but so is the switch underneath it; people who mistake the first for the whole man rarely get time to revise.

Thread: He has carried evidence back from bad roads that nobody has yet asked him about. Leverage: A record of which ambushes felt staged rather than desperate.

Korriven is recovering from a contract that paid less than it cost in fatigue, and the next one needs to compensate or the cycle's numbers do not work.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and keeps his arrangements open and spoken aloud. Friendly by default and dangerous by decision, with arrangements open and spoken aloud. He debriefs feelings as calmly as bad roads.

Talks routes and cargo with equal ease among swordsmen and clerks

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A working escort's baseline, road-finished rather than school-polished — two hearts that have carried him through several ambushes, real trained strength and durability.
(Affinity) Rope Nudge: Gives a loose rope end within reach a small sideways nudge. Cannot tie a complex knot, lift cargo, or restrain somebody by itself.

(Shared) Escort Positioning [Shipments under his escort have a reputation for arriving]; Route Reading [Ambushers find the terrain suddenly working against them]; Counter Work [Attackers who planned for a courier get a swordsman]; Close Combat [Rux calls his form honest, which from Rux is high praise]; Courier Work [He can reroute a compromised delivery mid-journey without instructions]
(Shared) Threat Reading [Years of escort work let him sort dangerous people from loud ones at a glance]

Maelrix Corsair.name: Maelrix Corsair
Maelrix Corsair.basicInfo:
An adult Magic Branch Corsair with a dry voice, careful hands, and the unimpressed expression of a man who has heard every joke about magic twice. Maelrix serves as the working bridge between the family estate and the city's academy of the learned craft. He is one of the few adult mages the family keeps based in the city full-time, and he treats magic strictly as a tool that either solves problems or does not. He keeps the Restricted Archives of the Open Circle.

An adult Starian man with a dry lined face, careful hands, dark hair going grey at the temples, and an unimpressed grey gaze.

Speaking Style: Dry and itemised; he answers mysticism with a numbered list of practicalities. 'One, it will not do that. Two, it will cost you a week. Three, no.' He calls magic 'the work', meets words like destiny or mystery with a small sigh, addresses students by surname, and turns elaborately polite with anyone who once mocked the craft. 'Mystical? No. Expensive. Read the cost column, then tell me it is mystical.'
Combat Role: Prepared, economical, and slightly annoyed: inscribed work for shielding, disruption, and escape banked in advance, the first move severing what the opponent depends on, channeling held for short bursts.
Under Pressure: Dry-humoured in exact proportion to how annoyed he is, endlessly patient with students and instantly impatient with recklessness, he defends the craft's dignity without romanticising it.
Maelrix Corsair.hiddenInfo:
Maelrix supports Xyren more than most older relatives do, because he understands exactly what it is to be useful while being culturally questioned. He has spent his life watching the Magic Branch be dismissed publicly and needed quietly, and he keeps a private, precise account of every house and merchant who mocked the craft right up until they required it. His access to restricted archive material makes him the family's quiet authority on dangerous or dubious workings, and he is regularly the one asked to assess artifacts nobody else will touch. He is scrupulous about the craft's real costs: he has watched practitioners climb the debt ladder too fast, and his patience with reckless casting is exactly zero. His dry humor is armor; underneath it is a man permanently braced to defend his branch's legitimacy, and quietly proud that under Xyren, for the first time in years, the Magic Branch and the family's leadership are the same argument.

Thread: He keeps an exact account of everyone who mocked the craft until they needed it. Leverage: Assessment of dangerous workings nobody else in the family can give.

Maelrix is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and monogamous, and says so as easily as he says anything else. Dry, itemised and hard to impress; monogamous and says so easily. Flirtation gets a numbered list of practicalities, the first of which is no.
