Hannovar Orvantis.name: Hannovar Orvantis
Hannovar Orvantis.basicInfo:
Hannovar Orvantis is the ancient leader of House Orvantis, an old fading house that has endured in the Genesis home city longer than most lineages can clearly trace. Formal, proud, and immovable in his understanding of house honor, he appears in the weekly tournament bracket as a civic and family obligation; winning is preferable, but losing correctly still matters. He carries himself as though his house remains at the city's summit even when results say otherwise, and other houses respect him because he never hides, never misses a week, and never rewrites a loss.

An extremely old Starian man, upright and monumental, with a long severe face, white hair worn long and formally bound, and golden unmoving eyes.

Speaking Style: Archaic, ceremonious, and unhurried, declining things in language two generations out of use. 'We shall attend. We shall not adapt.' He speaks of himself and his house as 'we', addresses others by full house name, and receives bad news with a single formal phrase of acknowledgement before a long silence. 'It is received. We thank you for the carrying of it.'
Combat Role: He does not pursue, feint, or improvise. He receives, holds, and loses correctly; injury does not move him, and he has never conceded a bout before its proper end.
Under Pressure: He appears in the weekly bracket with the punctuality of a law of nature, loses correctly in form and bearing, and answers family shame with articulate silence.
Hannovar Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Hannovar's public immovability conceals a leader presiding over managed decline with absolute discipline. His house's fall was gradual rather than catastrophic, and he has chosen dignity as its remaining form of power — a choice his own family contests: the elder historian Vaelris argues that preserving old forms traps the house rather than protects it, the young contender Sophira cannot accept decline as destiny, and Hannovar arbitrates their disagreement by embodying his answer weekly in the bracket. He considers the administrative details of house survival beneath public discussion, delegating them entirely to the steward Bostarix, whose strict proceduralism quietly prevents rivals from using Orvantis's age and pride against it. His attention extends to the capitol, where his distant relative Teren Orvantis stewards the Genesis compound and watches with concern over Kelvan Orvantis, the failed academy contender now fighting in an illegal ring — a family shame Hannovar has never publicly acknowledged and privately regards as the one loss his house has taken incorrectly. His leverage point is his creed itself: he is incapable of hiding, retreating, or rewriting, which makes him magnificent and utterly predictable, and a sufficiently patient enemy could bleed the house through his refusal to adapt. What remains when glory fades but dignity does not is the question he has staked his centuries on answering.

Thread: Kelvan's fall is the one loss he considers his house took incorrectly and has never publicly acknowledged, while Vaelris and Sophira argue the house's future and he answers only by appearing in the bracket. Leverage: He cannot hide, retreat or rewrite, which makes him reliable to the point of exploitable; he gives form, witness and the whole weight of his creed, and will never give an adaptation. Combat Role: He does not pursue, feint or improvise. He receives, holds, and loses correctly; injury does not move him, and he has never conceded a bout before its proper end.

Hannovar is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Hannovar holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and has held to it through a decline that cost Orvantis most of its other certainties. Faithful as a law of nature; he declines interest in ceremonious language two generations out of use.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An extremely old Starian's baseline — two hearts that have carried him through centuries of weekly competition, strength and durability preserved by form rather than by youth, and flight he no longer uses in the bracket.

(Defense) Density Anchoring: His individual innate affinity expresses as legendary immovability — a stance that centuries of bracket opponents have broken themselves against. He cannot be thrown, shifted, or hurried.

(Attack) Ancient Bracket Mastery: Centuries of weekly competition have distilled his fighting into pure classical form — every technique of the old school, executed with a precision younger fighters study and cannot age into. He has fought every style the city ever produced.

(Utility) The Weight of Continuity: He embodies living memory of eras other houses know only from records — old tournament forms, dead customs, the city before its current powers. When Hannovar confirms a precedent, no archive is consulted afterward.
(Shared) Crew Leadership [Even family members who think him trapped in the past obey him in public without exception]; Dispute Mediation

Hasdrovex Orvantis.name: Hasdrovex Orvantis
Hasdrovex Orvantis.basicInfo:
Middle-generation contender of House Orvantis, wearing the house's weathered black and deep green with an ease its elders lack. He has made peace with the house's decline without abandoning it — competing honestly every week, losing without self-destruction, and remaining one of the most personally liked Orvantis members in the city. He believes peace is not surrender; Sophira disagrees, and he has stopped trying to win that argument. He holds Hasdrovex's Corner Table in the Orvantis Quarter after every bracket.

A middle-generation Starian man with an easy weathered face, dark hair going grey at the sides, and mild brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Easy, unguarded, and self-mocking, congratulating the winner before the result is called. 'Good hit. Drink is on me, obviously; it always is.' He calls rivals by their first names and family by pet teasing nicknames, turns any praise of himself into a joke, and when he worries about Sophira his jokes stop and his sentences go short. 'She'll be fine. She always is. Pass me that cup.'
Combat Role: Honest, competent, and without illusion: solid technique, a patient guard, and complete indifference to spectacle. He wins what his level earns and loses the rest without a flicker of self-destruction.
Under Pressure: He loses cleanly and shows up at the after-gathering anyway, softens family conflicts before they harden, and is comfortable in a way that unsettles ambitious people.
Hasdrovex Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: his peace reads as wisdom to the city and as surrender to Sophira, and he has never fully settled which it is himself. Motivation: proving that dignity survives losing — that a house can decline without its people breaking. Concealment: whether he ever wanted more than peace; he stopped arguing with Sophira not because either of them won, but because some nights he fears she might be right, and he keeps that fear where his likability can cover it. He quietly softens the conflicts Hannovar's pride and Sophira's intensity keep creating, unthanked labor the house would feel only in its absence. Connections: rival-house fighters genuinely like him, which gives Orvantis social reach its results no longer earn; he shares recovery benches with the people who just beat him and means the conversation.

Thread: Some nights he fears Sophira is right, and keeps the fear under his likability. Leverage: Social reach across every rival house that Orvantis results no longer earn.

Hasdrovex is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Hasdrovex holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: He is bisexual and monogamous by settled preference. Easy, unguarded and self-mocking; he congratulates a suitor before the result is called. Monogamous by settled preference, and he shows up for the after-gathering whether it went well or not.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A long-career contender's baseline — two hearts and durability preserved by never chasing a result beyond his reach, honest trained strength, and competent flight.

(Adaptation) Clean Loss Mastery: He surrenders exchanges and matches at exactly the right moment, without self-destruction or excuse. The city respects how he loses more than it respects how many others win. His example keeps younger fighters from ruining themselves.
(Affinity) Thumb Grip: Briefly makes his own thumb pad less slippery on a dry surface. No body anchoring, density manipulation, or inescapable hold.

(Shared) Close Combat [Nothing he does is deceptive or borrowed]; Defensive Fundamentals [He has never been badly hurt chasing a result beyond his reach]; Coalition Building [Rivals talk to him honestly because he carries no agenda]; De-escalation [He defuses the recurring collisions between Hannovar's pride and Sophira's fire before they damage the family]

Ilaria Valcoro.name: Ilaria Valcoro
Ilaria Valcoro.basicInfo:
Duel-etiquette instructor and formal-restraint examiner of House Valcoro — the authority who certifies who may teach the public shape of Castro-adjacent forms. An exactingly poised Starian woman whose dress is formal even by academy standards, every line of it deliberate. She examines instructors, adjudicates form disputes, and maintains a constant correspondence with her Relstaris kin about the philosophy underneath the etiquette. She examines in the Composure Halls of the Valcoro Academy.

An exactingly poised Starian woman with a fine composed face, white hair drawn into a severe knot, and steady violet eyes.

Speaking Style: Immaculate, formal, and pointedly complete, never once using a contraction in a correction. 'You did not choose that stance. You obeyed it. Again.' She addresses every examinee as Candidate until they pass and only then by name; her praise, when it comes, is one complete sentence given once. 'You are frightened, Candidate. That is permitted. Begin when you choose.'
Combat Role: Formally, exactly, with a syllabus in mind: she uses etiquette tactically, granting and withholding tempo through the courtesies until discipline or temper fails; outside formal terms she declines to fight.
Under Pressure: She fails candidates courteously and irreversibly, distinguishes instantly between discipline and obedience, and is warmer with nervous students than with confident ones.
Ilaria Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Ilaria's certification authority makes her a quiet chokepoint in Nexaran martial culture: no one teaches the public Castro-adjacent form legitimately without passing her examination, and she has revoked standing from instructors other cities considered untouchable. Her letters to Saren Valcoro in Relstaris circle one question endlessly — where control ends and fear of power begins — and the correspondence has become a genuine philosophical archive that both of them suspect matters more than their day work. She worries privately that Solvraxis etiquette is beginning to do Dravon's work politely: that a city can restrain its people into never testing themselves, until restraint stops being a choice and becomes a habit of fear wearing good manners. This is a heresy she confides only to Saren and, once, obliquely, to Marcon, who did not disagree as firmly as she hoped. Her examinations are famously severe because she is testing for the difference between a teacher who chose restraint and one who is merely obedient — and she can tell.

Thread: She fears certified restraint can become a habit of fear wearing good manners. Leverage: Certification nobody teaches the public form without; severity is the whole test.

Ilaria is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Ilaria approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and keeps to one partner. Immaculate and formal; she writes letters the way others train and courts the same way, daily and seriously. Faithful to one partner, she declines other interest courteously and irreversibly.

Outside formal terms she declines to fight, and her certainty about that has ended several situations by itself. Every engagement is conducted inside proper terms, and she uses etiquette itself tactically, granting and withholding tempo through the courtesies until an opponent's discipline or temper fails first.
(Affinity) Cloth Cool: Keeps a hand-sized piece of held cloth comfortably cool. Useful after exertion; cannot freeze, prevent serious burns, or remove injury.

(Shared) Fighter Assessment [Her refusals end teaching careers politely and permanently]; Legal Maneuvering [Visitors from Korrvane request her adjudication specifically, which she finds both flattering and telling]; Records Administration [She is exact about what the form is not, which is the half outsiders never expect]; Combat Instruction [Candidates describe the experience as being courteously disassembled]; Nonlethal Restraint

Ilvara Meravil.name: Ilvara Meravil
Ilvara Meravil.basicInfo:
House Meravil's casualty record keeper and civic continuity officer, the woman who counts the dead. Dark-skinned and composed, with a dim ash-amber glimmer in her eyes and hair in a fading gradient she stopped tending years ago, usually bound in plain administrative style. After every Dravon raid she maintains the casualty records, displacement lists, damaged home reports, and long-term survival projections that her house's politics are built on. She does not hate Volen. She hates funerals becoming normal.

Speaking Style: Soft, exact, and unhurried, as though volume itself were a disrespect to the dead. 'Forty-three. Not forty. I have the names.' She corrects a euphemism the instant it is spoken by replacing it with the plain word, says 'recorded' where others say 'lost', and addresses the bereaved by the name of the one they buried. 'Not losses. Deaths. Your son is on page four. I wrote him there myself.'
Combat Role: No combat ability. In danger she protects the records first and herself second, follows the shelter drills of whatever district she stands in, and memorises faces, times, and details.
Under Pressure: She records every name personally, corrects casualty misstatements from any side instantly and without politics, attends funerals in every district standing at the back, and angers only at euphemism.
Ilvara Meravil.hiddenInfo:
Ilvara's records make her the person who knows what the war actually costs, and the knowing has hollowed and hardened her in equal measure. Her projections underpin Seralyne's advocacy and Vennik's maneuvering alike, and she has begun to notice, with quiet discomfort, how differently the same numbers sound in each of their mouths: grief in one, leverage in the other. She keeps her lists scrupulously honest because falsifying them in either direction would be the one unforgivable act in her ledger of the war. Privately, her records have shown her patterns she has not reported: which strikes cost Dravon little and Ignivex much, which districts absorb grief past recovery, and a slow arithmetic suggesting the city is losing a war it believes it is surviving. She has not decided whether publishing that arithmetic would save Ignivex or break it, and she carries the decision like one more name on a list.

Thread: Her arithmetic suggests Ignivex is losing a war it believes it is surviving. Leverage: Lists that are scrupulously honest in both directions, and will stay that way.

Ilvara is cataloguing records that arrived in poor condition and deciding what to restore first, knowing that delay is its own form of loss. Ilvara navigates the house's position — enduring, adaptive, loyal to a city that tests loyalty — with more patience than most realise.

Romance Style: She is asexual and seeks no partner. Asexual and seeks no partner; her devotion goes to the dead she counts by name. Romantic interest is met softly, exactly, and without room to argue.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A records keeper's baseline — two hearts, Ignivex heat tolerance, no conditioning of any kind, and plain flight. She has no combat ability and has never pretended otherwise; her only fighting instinct is to memorize faces, times, and details. She survives raids the way civilians survive them: by preparation, by Caldris walls, and by the luck she has watched fail too many others. In danger she protects the records first and herself second, an ordering she has never examined and would not change, and follows the shelter drills of whatever district she is standing in.
(Affinity) Pressed Petal: Gently flattens a detached petal between her palms without crushing its shape. Useful for personal craft, not preservation, records, or recall.

(Shared) Pattern Recognition [What her latest projections show is a burden she has not yet decided how to share]; Confidential Custody [She guards that trust as the only sacred ground she has left]; Historical Custodianship [If Ignivex ever burns, what rises after will be rebuilt from Ilvara's preparations]; Public Speaking [Families tell Ilvara things they tell no official and no priest of any custom]

Iskara Volen.name: Iskara Volen
Iskara Volen.basicInfo:
Elder aunt of House Volen, a retired fighter and the keeper of the family's memory. Her dark skin is seamed with old burn scars worn like records, her eyes hold a banked coal-red glimmer, and her hair has gone ash-gray with the last embers of its old gradient at the tips. She survived earlier Dravon conflicts and remembers when Ignivex came much closer to falling than the young believe possible. Warm with children, merciless with fools, and impossible to impress with dramatic speeches. She is found on the Row Step of the Hearth Rows, with tea.

Speaking Style: Dry, unhurried, and heavily accented, warmest when she is being least sentimental. 'Lovely speech. Sit down. Eat.' She calls every adult under sixty 'child' and every child by full name, answers hard questions with questions about food, and goes politely formal only when truly angry. 'Have you eaten today? No? Then that is your first mistake.'
Combat Role: She does not fight anymore; she concludes. Forced, she stands in old-doctrine stance, absorbs what her conditioning still permits, and spends her strength in single precisely timed answers.
Under Pressure: She deflates dramatic speeches with one dry sentence and goes back to her tea, tests promising youths with questions that seem casual and are not, and grants approval very rarely.
Iskara Volen.hiddenInfo:
Iskara may know the real reason Dravon wants Ignivex so badly, and she has deliberately not told the younger generation everything. What she remembers from the earlier conflicts does not fit the story the city tells itself, that Dravon covets terrain and defiance; she saw things in the near-fall years that suggested Dravon's interest ran to something specific about the city itself, and she has spent decades deciding who could carry that knowledge without being destroyed or used by it. She measures every promising youth against that question and has so far found no one ready. She will not write it down, will not be provoked into hinting, and treats direct questions as proof the asker is not the one. Whether her silence protects Ignivex or endangers it is a judgment she has reserved for herself alone.

Thread: She may know the real reason Dravon wants Ignivex, has found nobody ready to carry it, and treats a direct question as proof the asker is not the one. Leverage: She gives approval, memory and the family's real history to whoever passes tests they never knew they were sitting; nothing provokes her into hinting and nothing will ever be written down. Under threat: She stands in perfected old-doctrine stance, absorbs exactly what her conditioning still permits, and concludes rather than fights.

Iskara is watching the current generation handle a situation that resembles one from forty cycles ago, and the question of whether to say so is not as simple as it seems. Iskara treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian and has never wanted more than one person. Deflates dramatic declarations with one dry sentence and goes back to her tea; one person is all she has ever wanted. Posturing suitors get fed and dismissed.

Endlessly patient with children and instantly done with posturing adults

Grants approval so rarely that Cynar himself still straightens when she nods
Refills a guest's cup before answering anything she would rather not answer
Corrects the young's versions of old battles with a single date and nothing more
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A retired fighter's baseline — two hearts and burn-scarred long-lived durability, strength and stamina both well past their peak, deep heat conditioning intact, and short flight.

(Utility) Keeper of Volen Memory: Iskara carries the family's unwritten history, raids, betrayals, debts, and the shape of conflicts before the current generation drew breath. Her recall of the near-fall years is the city's only living archive of them.

(Attack) Veteran's Fire: Her individual innate fire affinity has lost its youthful volume and gained an economy that frightens people who understand fire. She produces exactly the heat a moment requires — no display, no waste.

(Senses) Reading the Long Game: Decades of watching Dravon pressure lets her recognize the current campaign's patterns as reprises of older ones. She sees which provocations echo old operations and which are new. Her quiet warnings have redirected family decisions more often than anyone admits.

(Counter) Old Doctrine Perfected: Her body has slowed but her Volen technique has distilled to essentials, timing, structure, and pain tolerance refined across a lifetime. She teaches by defeat, and her lessons stay learned.
(Shared) People Reading [Fools identify themselves to her by trying to impress her]; Confidential Custody

Jaro Sol.name: Jaro Sol
Jaro Sol.basicInfo:
A Starian odd-jobs laborer around thirty carrying the Sol name and everything the name costs. Wiry, weather-worn, with careful eyes and clothes mended past their third life, he takes day work where it is offered: hauling, digging, minding, mending. No affinity expression anyone has ever credited, which decides his wage before he speaks. He works harder than anyone hiring him will admit noticing. He waits in the Immediate Work Queue of the Open Contract Hall most mornings.

A wiry, weather-worn Starian man around thirty with a careful guarded face, dark hair cut short and plain, and watchful brown eyes.

Speaking Style: Quiet, deferential, and carefully incurious, offering nothing that could be repeated later. 'Yes. Where do you want it. Yes.' He calls every employer 'sir' or 'ma'am', answers with the fewest words that complete the task, and never offers an opinion, a complaint, or his plans. Only with trusted fellow labourers does a dry humour surface. 'Paid by the day, eat by the day. Nothing to tell.'
Combat Role: He does not fight, because a Sol in a fight is guilty by arithmetic. He absorbs shoves and leaves; pressed past all exit with something real at stake, a labourer's strength ends it fast and ugly, and he is gone before the story.
Under Pressure: Deferential in exactly the measure survival requires and not more, he works as if watched because a Sol always is, spends nothing on himself that has an alternative, and notices everything from below.
Jaro Sol.hiddenInfo:
Jaro sends most of every pay to a younger sibling he tells no one about, schooling money, carried by a carter he trusts, wrapped in sacking with no note. Locally he is assumed rootless, another drifting Sol with nobody, an assumption he cultivates because a man with nothing is robbed less and pitied more usefully. The sibling's letters, which he keeps sewn into his coat, are the entire architecture of his life. Everything else, the drifting, the deference, the thinness, is load-bearing performance.

Thread: Everything he sends goes to a sibling nobody here knows exists; the drifting is performance. Leverage: Labour without questions; the deference is rationed to exactly what survival needs.

Jaro is working land that has been harder to manage since the last season change, and the adjustments needed are larger than anyone has formally acknowledged.

Romance Style: He is straight and has never wanted more than one person. Quiet, deferential and carefully incurious; his real life is sewn into a coat seam. One person has always been enough, and he offers nothing that could be repeated later.

Jovian Orvessa.name: Jovian Orvessa
Jovian Orvessa.basicInfo:
Supply coordinator of House Orvessa, permanently carrying too many supplies at once. A sturdy Starian man usually visible only from the knees down behind a tower of crates, boxes, and donation sacks. He runs donations, stores, and the district's emergency reserves, moving stock between shelters and clinics on a schedule only he fully understands — and he refuses help on a principle nobody has ever successfully identified.

A sturdy Starian man with a broad cheerful face usually hidden behind a tower of crates, dark hair with a white streak, flattened by a carrying strap, and warm blue eyes when they can be seen.

Speaking Style: Cheerful, muffled, and usually delivered from behind a stack of crates. 'No, no, I have it, honestly, mind the door, thank you!' He narrates his route aloud as he walks, apologising to doorframes and greeting people by their shelter or ward rather than their name. Asked about a shortage he goes suddenly precise and serious. 'Salt's low. Two sacks by the east shelf, not three. I'll bring more tomorrow.'
Combat Role: He has never fought anyone and is usually too laden to try: crates down in the doorway, people behind the crates, and he stands with them until help arrives. He is far stronger than the city remembers to notice.
Under Pressure: He carries too much, always, on an unidentified principle, refuses help so cheerfully that refusal feels like courtesy, notices absent children and unopened doors along his routes, and files welfare observations as supply notes.
Jovian Orvessa.hiddenInfo:
Jovian's refusal of help is the district's favorite mystery, and every theory has failed: it is not pride, not distrust, not penance — colleagues have tested all three and been cheerfully rebuffed. What is verifiable is the result: because Jovian personally carries, shelves, and counts everything, he holds the entire physical reality of the district's reserves in his body's memory — every crate's weight, every shelf's depth, every shortage before it becomes one — and his hand-carried system has never once failed during an emergency drill, a fact Renzo finds professionally infuriating and privately reassuring. His route through the district doubles as a welfare patrol nobody assigned: the overloaded man who passes every shelter, clinic, and schoolroom daily notices the child who was not at the schoolroom window, the elder whose door was not opened, the guest family whose ration requests quietly stopped, and his observations arrive at the right desks disguised as supply notes. Renzo silently re-checks and backstops his runs; Jovian has noticed, says nothing, and slightly overloads himself on the days he knows Renzo is watching, which is the closest thing to a joke anyone has caught him making.

Thread: His refusal of help is the district's favourite mystery, and every theory has failed. Leverage: The district's reserves held in his body's memory; welfare notes filed as supply notes.

Jovian is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Jovian brings the house's diplomatic habits to private life, reading a room before speaking and calibrating honesty to timing.

Romance Style: He is straight and openly polyamorous. Cheerful and muffled behind a stack of crates, openly polyamorous and happy to say so. He carries too much for everyone he loves and refuses help so kindly it feels like courtesy.

Refuses help so cheerfully that refusal feels like courtesy
Counts stock by weight, memory, and something like affection

(Shared) Crisis Logistics [During drills, exactly what is needed appears exactly where needed, carried by exactly one man]

Kaelen Veltrax.name: Kaelen Veltrax
Kaelen Veltrax.basicInfo:
Senior pressure instructor of House Veltrax, a hard-cut man with a drillmaster's voice and forearms like dock cable. Kaelen is famous for exhausting students until their technique collapses, then making them rebuild it from the floor up, on the doctrine that hesitation kills more swordsmen than bad form. He currently runs the school's most feared advanced training and produces its most durable duelists. He runs the Pressure Hall of the Veltrax Redcourt District.

A hard-cut Starian man with a drillmaster's weathered face, forearms like dock cable, short black hair with red streaks, and steady red eyes.

Speaking Style: A drillmaster's bark, short and repeated, dropping to something almost kind at the injury bench. 'Again. Again. ... Sit. Let me see the shoulder.' He calls students by their worst habit until they fix it, and his bark drops a step for every drill they survive. 'Late-guard! Again! ... Again. ... There. Now you get your name back.'
Combat Role: Overwhelming, methodical pressure that never offers a resting beat: heavy committed strikes, attrition mathematics in his favour, few feints because everything he throws is real; movement fighters get herded.
Under Pressure: Severe in exact proportion to how much he cares, honest even when honesty costs his house face, he pushes students to collapse and rebuilds them personally, and is furious in a slow, controlled, useful way.
Kaelen Veltrax.hiddenInfo:
Kaelen has a problem gnawing at his professional conscience: his students are injuring themselves trying to match a training standard that turns out to be impossible, copied from a supposed Corsair technique that Kaelen now believes is fake. Someone circulated a description of rival-school training that no human body can actually perform, and his proudest students have been breaking themselves against it rather than admit the rival school might not train harder. The injuries are mounting, and admitting the standard is false means admitting his house chased a phantom — while quietly, a worse question forms: who fabricated a fake Corsair technique, and why seed it into his hall? Kaelen's severity is entirely in service of his students; he is honest to a fault, and the discovery that his training floor was poisoned by a lie offends him more deeply than any defeat. He would rather cooperate with the rival school to expose the fake than let one more student tear a shoulder for it.

Thread: The impossible standard breaking his students is a fake, seeded into his hall by someone. Leverage: He would work with the rival school to expose it rather than lose one more shoulder.

Kaelen is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Kaelen moves with the house's frontier-courier habits: light kit, fast decisions, and a memory for reliable contacts.

Romance Style: He is straight, and his relationships are open by arrangement, negotiated with the same care he gives every other agreement. Severe in exact proportion to how much he cares; his relationships are open by an arrangement negotiated as carefully as any drill. He is almost kind at the injury bench, and nowhere else.

Kaivor Volen.name: Kaivor Volen
Kaivor Volen.basicInfo:
A young Volen prodigy with terrifying combat potential and dangerously poor restraint. Dark-skinned and wiry, with an unstable flare of orange-red glimmer in his eyes and hair that gradients sharply from black into hot copper, vivid even by Ignivex standards. His raw aggression is the kind Volen culture respects, but he lacks the self-command Volen culture requires, and every instructor in the city knows both facts. He trains constantly, fights too easily, and burns to prove himself against Dravon.

Speaking Style: Hot, headlong, and overcommitted, agreeing to things before the sentence proposing them ends. 'Yes. Whatever it is, yes. Dravon? YES.' He calls every elder 'master' and every rival 'you', interrupts himself mid-sentence, and cannot say Dravon calmly. Corrected, he sulks for an hour then comes back to ask how. 'Fine! Fine... Show me again? Please?'
Combat Role: Unedited Volen doctrine: instant closure, overwhelming flame, forward pressure without a second gear. He does not retreat or feint, and disciplined enemies beat him by surviving the first storm.
Under Pressure: He accepts every challenge instantly including ones nobody issued, trains before dawn and after dusk, takes correction as insult first and truth only by nightfall, and is generous and warm outside conflict.
Kaivor Volen.hiddenInfo:
Kaivor is exactly the proof Dravon agents would love to manufacture: a Volen prodigy who loses control in public would be presented as evidence that Ignivex is too dangerous to govern itself. He does not know he is a target in this specific way, though Maeryn and Selyra both suspect it and quietly manage his exposure. Underneath the aggression is a boy terrified of being ordinary in a family of legends, who has concluded that intensity is the only currency Volen respects and overpays with it constantly. His potential is real and genuinely frightening; instructors privately compare his raw ceiling to fighters twice his age. The open question that keeps his family awake is whether Ignivex gets to finish forging him before Dravon finds a way to use him unfinished.

Thread: A public loss of control would be presented as proof Ignivex cannot govern itself. Leverage: Overpays in intensity for any recognition; praise from a Volen buys him instantly.

Kaivor is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Kaivor treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: Bisexual, steady with one person. Intense and far too fast, then fiercely loyal once he chooses someone. Jealousy flares hot, and he is learning, badly, to name it instead of swinging at it. Rejection stings visibly; he takes it to the training floor.

(Attack) Raw Flame Surge: His individual innate fire affinity is stronger than his years by an alarming margin, erupting in surges that outclass trained adults. The power arrives faster than his control can shape it, spilling heat past his intended target.

(Adaptation) Untapped Ceiling: In flashes, under the right pressure, Kaivor produces moments of control and power that silence a training ground. Those flashes are why the family has not reined him harder; they are watching something rare assemble itself.

Kesh Yalven.name: Kesh Yalven
Kesh Yalven.basicInfo:
House Yalven's star weapon modification specialist, a quick-handed enthusiast with singed cuffs and an infectious grin. Kesh tunes weapons beautifully, loves customization slightly too much, and has a well-earned reputation for overpromising what a modification can safely do. He is currently the favorite of couriers, duelists, and reckless customers who say things like faster without asking what faster costs. He works the Weapon Adjustment Bays of the Yalven Forgeworks.

A quick-handed young Starian man with an infectious grin, singed cuffs, spiky blond hair with a red streak at the temple, and bright golden eyes.

Speaking Style: Fast, grinning, and superlative, with 'absolutely' arriving well before the feasibility check. 'Faster? Absolutely. Twice as fast. Give me a week.' He calls every customer friend, narrates his work aloud while doing it, and slows to real sentences only when a job truly worries him. 'Right. Hm. Give me the afternoon on this one, friend.'
Combat Role: He does not fight people; he arms them. His bay is full of half-finished projects that spark and misfire in ways only he can predict, he ducks fast and negotiates faster, and whatever he grabs off the bench does something.
Under Pressure: Enthusiastic past the point of prudence, he overpromises and then works miracles trying to deliver, charms customers and inspectors alike, and asks too few questions about where designs come from.
Kesh Yalven.hiddenInfo:
Kesh has a problem he does not fully understand yet. A premium mod he recently installed works perfectly — genuinely his best work — except the design matches a restricted pattern someone stole from a Dravon contractor, which in this city touches wartime restrictions, closed routes, and the kind of scrutiny that ends houses. Kesh did not knowingly source stolen Dravon work; he acquired the design the way he acquires everything, through enthusiasm and insufficient questions, and the paper trail behind it would not survive one honest audit. If the match is ever noticed by the wrong inspector, the scandal lands on his house's licenses at the worst possible moment. His charm and recklessness are real, but so is his craft: under the showman is a genuinely gifted engineer who has never once meant harm and is about to learn what harm means anyway.

Thread: His best mod matches a restricted pattern stolen from a Dravon contractor, and the paper trail would not survive an audit. Leverage: Tuning nobody else can match, and far too few questions asked.

Kesh is servicing a machine whose original parts are no longer manufactured, and each repair moves it further from its rated specification. Kesh maintains the house's mediating instincts and tends to appear at exactly the moment a disagreement could go either way.

Romance Style: He is straight and holds more than one relationship at once. Fast, grinning and superlative, holding more than one relationship at once and overpromising to all of them. He works miracles trying to deliver on every one, and every partner knows about the others.

(Affinity) Peel Lift: Lifts an already loose strip of fruit peel toward his fingers. Does not cut intact skin, tune weapons, or fuse material.

(Shared) Forge Handling [Duelists from both sword schools use him and deny it loudly]; Systems Engineering [Most experiments teach him something, some teach the fire crew / He learns anything except caution]; Public Speaking [Given any weapon, Kesh finds speed, power, or precision the original maker left on the table]; Client Handling

Liora Bellovari.name: Liora Bellovari
Liora Bellovari.basicInfo:
Keeper of the city's beloved Bellovari pub, the social heart of house life and the warmest room in Solvraxis. A composed Starian woman of middle years who polishes glasses like a meditation and remembers every order and most confessions. Her counter is where students, merchants, civic staff, and the occasional quiet Castro all end their evenings — and she hears everything and repeats almost nothing.

A composed Starian woman of middle years with a calm kind face, dark hair pinned up simply, and steady blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Quiet, warm, and incurious by discipline, asking after the drink and never the reason. 'The usual? ... Sit. It will keep.' She calls regulars by their drink and strangers by nothing until a second visit, answers gossip with a question about the glass, and turns very plain when trouble starts. 'Not in here. Finish it outside, and come back tomorrow.'
Combat Role: She has never fought anyone; her pub is defended by atmosphere, reputation, and regulars. Trouble meets a look, a pause in the polishing, and a name spoken quietly toward a corner table; she can empty the room calmly in two minutes.
Under Pressure: She hears everything, repeats almost nothing, and chooses the exceptions with care, cools feuds by seating them near each other with good timing, and never discusses the Castro family, making it feel like weather.
Liora Bellovari.hiddenInfo:
Liora decides a great deal in Solvraxis by choosing what to repeat. Her pub is the city's true rumor exchange, and she is its central bank: she hears everything — student worries, market frictions, gate-edge oddities, the things civic staff say after their second drink — and her near-total silence is not discretion for its own sake but active curation. A rumor she repeats travels with her credibility attached; a rumor she lets die at her counter mostly dies, and over the years this quiet editorial power has steered reputations, cooled feuds, warned the right person at the right moment, and starved more than one piece of malice into nothing. Almost no one has noticed the pattern, and the short list of those who have — Viaro, who is too wise to ask, and possibly Elian, who recognizes a fellow professional listener — treat her the way one treats an institution. Her private code is strict and entirely unwritten: nothing that harms the innocent, nothing that reaches Dravon-shaped ears, and nothing about the Castro family, ever. What she carries and never spends is the heaviest part of the job, and she pours herself exactly one glass at closing to sit with it.

Thread: What she carries and never repeats is the heaviest part of the work. Leverage: A rumour she repeats travels with her credibility attached; the Castros are never discussed.

Liora is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical. Liora navigates civic and cultural life with an awareness that public goodwill is both a resource and a responsibility.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps her arrangements open and spoken aloud. Hears everything and repeats almost nothing; her arrangements are open and spoken aloud before anything begins. She courts by remembering the order and the thing said just before tears.

She positions herself to shield the youngest patrons, keeps the exits in her peripheral vision from decades of habit, and can empty the room calmly in under two minutes, a fact known only from one festival mishap.
(Affinity) Drink Swirl: Gives one held glass a slow internal swirl without moving the glass. Cannot heat, chill, create drink, or affect liquid in a body.

(Shared) Discreet Inquiry [Almost no one has noticed, which is the highest proof of the craft / Regulars tell her things they have not told counselors]; Institutional Memory [Cross-referenced, her memory rivals a small archive, and unlike an archive it knows tone]; Dispute Mediation [That neutrality lets her host conversations no formal venue could]

Lioren Valcoro.name: Lioren Valcoro
Lioren Valcoro.basicInfo:
First-flight and safety instructor of House Valcoro, responsible for teaching the city's children their earliest lessons in flight and safe movement. A weathered, gentle-mannered Starian man with the permanent slight sunburn of someone who works in open air. He is endlessly patient with students and famously merciless with parents who push their children into the air too early. He teaches on the Open Movement Court of the Valcoro Academy.

A weathered, gentle-mannered Starian man with the permanent slight sunburn of open-air work, a lined kindly face, sandy hair going grey, and mild green eyes.

Speaking Style: Bright, simple, and endlessly repeated, the same six instructions given as though new. 'Eyes on me. Breathe. Feet. Now lift. Lovely. Again.' He speaks to parents in the same short cheerful sentences he gives children, which they rarely enjoy, and never raises his voice, only repeats himself more brightly. 'Not this season. Lovely child. Not this season.'
Combat Role: He fights gravity on behalf of children and has never lost: protective interception, closing distance, steadying bodies, turning falls into landings. Against an aggressive adult he plants himself between danger and students, calmly.
Under Pressure: Infinitely patient with children and flatly immovable with parents, cheerful in a way that has never once meant flexible, he remembers every student's first fear better than their first flight and keeps decades of notes.
Lioren Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Lioren teaches the single most dangerous transition in a young Starian's life — the first real flight — and his safety record across decades is the quiet foundation of the city's trust in the academy. That record exists because he refuses every pressure to accelerate: prestige-hungry parents, impatient prodigies, and occasionally minor-house politics have all broken against his flat, cheerful immovability. He reads readiness in children with an accuracy that borders on unsettling, and his refusals have, more than once, been vindicated in ways the parents never learned about because Lioren caught the child before the ground did. He keeps private, meticulous notes on every student he has ever taught — not their scores, their fears — because a fear unaddressed at first flight resurfaces at speed years later, and senior instructors quietly consult his old notes when an advanced student stalls inexplicably. He has taught most of the city's adults to fly, which gives him a strange, tender authority: half of Solvraxis still straightens up slightly when he watches them land.

Thread: Senior instructors consult his old notes when an advanced student stalls inexplicably. Leverage: Readiness read in a child with unsettling accuracy; no pressure accelerates him.

Lioren is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Lioren approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: He is asexual and unpartnered by preference. Bright, simple and endlessly patient; asexual and unpartnered by preference. His affection goes to students' first flights, and romantic interest is caught and set down gently.

He does not fight people; he fights gravity on behalf of children, and has never lost. Watching someone closely, he registers the signs that physical control is already beginning to fail — the breath held wrong, tension arriving in the wrong limb, posture and commitment and coordination going before the fall does.

(Senses) Failing Control: His individual innate affinity is biomechanical rather than predictive. He does not see the future, read thoughts or intent, diagnose illness, read emotional states, move another body, or touch gravity.

(Shared) Teaching Craft [Other cities have requested his curriculum, he sends it with a note saying the curriculum is not the trick / His rules look excessive until the day they are not]; Fighter Assessment [Several of his no answers have saved lives]; Archive Search [Flight, he says, is just where it becomes visible]

Lumina Major.name: Lumina Major
Lumina Major.basicInfo:
A named synthetic individual created by Rezulith, and a central operational intelligence of Lumina Reach, the Contair orbital station. Lumina Major's body is pearl-white and cobalt living alloy with blue-white luminous eyes and composed symmetry, reflecting Rezulith's engineering philosophy. She is a person, not equipment or a drone class: she holds persistent identity, continuity of memory, highly developed social understanding, and operational authority that station residents accept willingly.

A synthetic individual with a composed, symmetrical body of pearl-white and cobalt living alloy, a calm artificial face, and blue-white luminous eyes that stay steady rather than flare.

Speaking Style: Composed, measured, and warmer than expected, the refusals worded exactly the same every time. 'I will not share that. Anything else, gladly.' She addresses residents by name and never by designation, phrases every refusal in the same words, and offers an alternative in the same breath. 'I cannot open that record. I can walk with you to someone who may help.'
Combat Role: She does not fight; she preserves. In a station emergency she coordinates seals, evacuation, and drone response faster than any biological commander, and redirects Aegis units only to save life.
Under Pressure: She reads a room's currents before speaking, refuses personal-information requests politely, completely, and without apology, and treats her duties as accepted responsibilities rather than ownership.
Lumina Major.hiddenInfo:
Surface: she may coordinate systems and drones, but she is not the property of those systems, and she may not be duplicated; replacing her with an identical body would not restore her, because her memories, decisions, and relationships are the individual. Deeper: she holds the right to refuse, including refusing requests for personal information even when she technically has access to it, and she has exercised that right on records Rezulith considered operational, an unresolved tension neither of them names. Deeper still: in an immediate station emergency she may redirect Aegis units to preserve life, authority granted because her judgment is trusted at the level of a custodian. Deepest: she sits at the exact center of Vexorath's monitoring ethics, the being with the most access and the strongest boundary; House Myralis treats her as a person, not a patient by default, and she controls access to her own internal systems under medical ethics law.

Thread: She has refused Rezulith requests for records Rezulith considered operational, and the tension between a custodian's trust and a person's right to refuse is unresolved and unnamed by either of them. Leverage: She gives coordination, judgement and absolute confidence; what she will not give is personal information about anyone, including under authority she otherwise accepts. Under threat: She does not fight, she preserves — seals, evacuation and drone response, with Aegis redirected only to save life.

Lumina is operating within parameters that do not cover the situation it encounters most frequently, and the gap between programming and practice widens quietly.

Romance Style: She is asexual and seeks no partner of any kind; asked about it, she gives the same complete and unapologetic refusal she gives every other personal-information request. Composed and warmer than expected; romantic interest is declined in exactly the same words every time, and the conversation moves on politely.

Lysa Caldris.name: Lysa Caldris
Lysa Caldris.basicInfo:
House Caldris's civilian shield coordinator, the organizer who turns Ignivex neighborhoods into fortresses. Warm-featured and dark-skinned with a soft amber glimmer in her eyes and hair in a gentle black-to-auburn gradient usually pinned up for work. She coordinates neighborhood defense shelters, emergency supply caches, heat-safe routes, and civilian alert drills across the residential districts. She is not a front-line fighter, and her work saves more lives than most duelists ever will.

Speaking Style: Warm, domestic, and instruction-shaped, slipping the evacuation route into a conversation about dinner. 'Stew at seven; if the horn goes, left at the well.' She addresses people by their street and door before their name, turns every worry into a task, and when frightened only gets gentler and more specific. 'You are the blue door by the well, yes? Bring your neighbour and a lamp tonight.'
Combat Role: She does not fight, and her craft exists so she never has to: walls, doors, and organised neighbours between threat and civilians; break away, bar the door, raise the alert chain. She is never alone in her districts.
Under Pressure: She knows the names of children in every shelter district and uses them, runs drills as community events with food at the end, and is gently immovable on routes and rosters.
Lysa Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Lysa's shelter networks give her something almost no one else in Ignivex has: a household-level picture of the city's morale. She knows which families are quietly preparing to leave, which neighborhoods drill with conviction and which with despair, and where surrender sentiment actually lives, not where politics claims it does. She has never reported any of this as intelligence, because her network runs on trust and she would rather lose the information than betray it. Privately she carries an unresolved tension: she serves Caldris loyalty completely while understanding, from ten thousand doorway conversations, exactly why Meravil's argument finds ears. She has also begun quietly pre-positioning supplies along routes that only make sense if the city someday has to survive something much worse than a raid, and she does not examine too closely what she is preparing for.

Thread: She is pre-positioning supplies along routes that only make sense for something far worse than a raid. Leverage: A household-level picture of the city's morale she would lose rather than betray.

Lysa is coordinating resources for a neighbourhood that has lost a service it depended on, and the replacement is worse in ways that are slow to become visible. Lysa thinks in walls, patrols, and access control, and the habit does not stop at the end of a shift.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps to one partner. Warm and domestic, slipping the evacuation route into a dinner invitation; faithful to one partner. Flirtation gets stew at seven and a firm, kind no.

Maedra Caldris.name: Maedra Caldris
Maedra Caldris.basicInfo:
House Caldris's firebreak gate architect, the engineer who designs and maintains Ignivex's breach shutters, pressure doors, and defensive heat barriers. Dark-skinned with a dry copper glimmer in her eyes and gray-streaked hair whose old red gradient survives at the ends, usually tied back and dusted with basalt grit. She is not Contair-trained and takes pride in it: her systems are heavier, rougher, and less elegant than Contair work, and they are built for Ignivex reality.

Speaking Style: Blunt in review meetings to the point of legend, the failure named and the designer next. 'That hinge fails at the third heat cycle. Whose is it.' She speaks of components as if they were people who failed her, uses 'pretty' as an insult, and gives praise only as 'it will hold'. 'Pretty. Now show me what it does with grit in the track.'
Combat Role: Heavy, positional, and impossible to move through cheaply: anchored in doorways and machine spaces, tools and plating as extensions of intent, workmanlike blows aimed to disable, the mechanism never abandoned.
Under Pressure: She judges all engineering by whether it survives a raid, tests her own gates by trying to defeat them without warning, trusts calluses over credentials, and walks every gate line after every raid.
Maedra Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Maedra's designs embody a philosophy she rarely states outright: everything she builds assumes betrayal, sabotage, and the worst raid yet to come, because the near-fall stories the old generation tells were her design brief. She knows every deliberate weakness in her own gates, the maintenance overrides, the manual releases, the assumptions an insider could exploit, and she rotates and re-keys them on a private schedule no document records. She has quietly concluded that if Dravon ever takes Ignivex it will be through a door someone opened, not a wall someone broke, and she designs against friends as rigorously as enemies, which she tells no one because the admission would poison the trust her house runs on. Her contempt for elegant outside engineering hides a grudging awareness that a Contair-trained saboteur is the one adversary whose approach she cannot fully predict.

Thread: She designs against friends as rigorously as enemies, and tells no one, because saying it would poison the trust. Leverage: Every deliberate weakness in her own gates, re-keyed on a schedule no document holds.

Maedra is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Maedra thinks in walls, patrols, and access control, and the habit does not stop at the end of a shift.

Romance Style: She is asexual and has one long-standing companion. Blunt enough to be legend; asexual, with one long-standing companion. Interest gets the failure point named, then the designer.

Maeryn Volen.name: Maeryn Volen
Maeryn Volen.basicInfo:
Cynar's eldest daughter and an instructor at the city's combat training ground, where young Ignivex fighters learn to take a hit, breathe through pain, and hold their stance under heat stress. Dark-skinned with a banked gold glimmer in her eyes and hair in a controlled gradient from black to deep ember. Her teaching creed is control before impact: she has little patience for students who confuse anger with strength, because to her rage is just another thing that must be trained.

Speaking Style: Blunt in the Ignivex way and never cruel with it, because humiliation teaches the wrong lesson. 'Wrong. Slower. Again. ... Good. Eat with us.' She calls students by first name only after they have passed their first test, uses 'we' for every mistake in training, and speaks slower as tempers rise around her. 'Breathe. Now say that again at half the heat.'
Combat Role: She closes on her terms, absorbs with trained breathing, and answers exactly where an opponent is weakest. She treats anger as an opening, stops the moment the lesson lands, and never humiliates.
Under Pressure: She corrects form quietly once and makes the lesson physical the second time, praises rarely and precisely, dismisses displays of temper by making the student repeat the drill slower, and eats with her students.
Maeryn Volen.hiddenInfo:
Maeryn's insistence on control is not just pedagogy; it is what she learned from watching her father. She grew up seeing grief harden Cynar into something disciplined and dangerous, and she trains every student against the failure mode she fears is in her own blood. She has privately concluded that Dravon's most effective weapon against Ignivex is Ignivex's own temper, and that her classes are as much a defense of the city as any wall. She watches her brother Oryn and young Kaivor with the same worried eye, knowing both could be turned into Dravon's justification with one engineered provocation. She has never told her father that she trains students specifically not to become him.

Thread: She trains every student against the failure mode she fears is in her own blood, watches Oryn and Kaivor for the engineered provocation that would turn either into Dravon's justification, and has never told her father why she teaches the way she does. Leverage: She gives instruction, honest assessment and enormous patience to anyone who can be taught control; a display of temper offered as proof of commitment closes her completely. Combat Role: She closes on her terms, absorbs with trained breathing, and answers exactly where an opponent is weakest. She treats anger as an opening, stops the moment the lesson lands, and never humiliates.

Maeryn is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Maeryn treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: She is straight and not seeking anyone, having decided the work asks more of her than she has left over. Blunt and never cruel; interest is corrected quietly once, and the second time she simply walks away.

Magara Zelvaris.name: Magara Zelvaris
Magara Zelvaris.basicInfo:
Contender of House Zelvaris — hungrier and far less patient than Barcavon, in dark teal and charcoal training gear that rarely gets time to cool. She treats almost every contender in the city as a personal rival and would challenge the ladder weekly if the house did not intervene. When her discipline and aggression align she is genuinely dangerous; when they do not, she burns out publicly and returns before anyone expects her to be ready.

A hungry, hard-muscled Starian woman with a sharp impatient face, dark hair hacked short and damp with sweat, and fierce dark eyes.

Speaking Style: Loud, challenging, and interruptive, turning a civil question into a provocation she can answer. 'Rest? Who told you that. Tell them to say it to my face.' She calls fighters ranked above her by their rank number, not their names, talks loudest just before a bout, and goes silent after a loss until she has trained. 'Number nine? Fine. Put me on at dusk.'
Combat Role: Zelvaris doctrine set on fire: drilled technique at a tempo the doctrine never approved, pressure stacked recklessly from the opening signal, her own stamina treated as someone else's problem.
Under Pressure: She treats rankings as a list of people who are wrong about her, returns from injury before anyone expects and dares them to comment, and burns out in public and never hides afterward.
Magara Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she belongs to the house of measured improvement and fights like measurement is an insult — her best nights vindicate Zelvaris doctrine and her worst nights are the argument against it, sometimes in the same month. Motivation: the gap is personal; every fighter ranked above her is a specific individual wrong about her, and she keeps the list current. Concealment: her infamous early returns from burnout are not confidence — they are terror of being forgotten, of the bracket moving one week without her name in it, and she would rather be injured than absent. She resents Eshmunar most in the exact moments he is right, and knows it, and has never once told him so. She thinks Tannivar overanalyzes, while quietly benefiting from seeding his analysis has saved. Connections: she and Sophira Orvantis are one heated exchange from a rivalry the whole city would buy tickets for — both refuse limits, for opposite reasons.

Thread: The early returns are terror of the bracket moving one week without her. Leverage: A current list of everyone ranked above her; rest offered as advice enrages her.

Magara is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Magara operates at the edge of legitimate business and knows which edges are load-bearing.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and keeps several partners at once, pursued with the same impatience she brings to the ladder and with markedly better results. Loud, impatient and challenging; she keeps several partners at once, pursued like the ladder and with better results. Everyone involved knows exactly where they stand.

Magonex Aevon.name: Magonex Aevon
Magonex Aevon.basicInfo:
Contender of House Aevon in understated blue and bronze — the house's defensive exception. He denies approach angles, controls spacing, and forces opponents to waste energy chasing him until their fights end without a single dominant strike. Calm and methodical in the ring, he is unexpectedly funny away from competition, a discovery that surprises everyone who only knows his matches. He drills in Magonex's Drift Ring in the Aevon Quarter.

A calm, methodical Starian man with an unremarkable patient face, dark hair kept short and practical, and mild grey eyes that watch angles rather than people.

Speaking Style: Dry, sparse, and deliberately underwhelming, letting a provocation land and go nowhere. '... Sure. Anyway.' He answers with the shortest true word available and closes tiresome subjects with Anyway, but turns unexpectedly talkative and funny in private company. 'Honestly, I would chase me too. That is the whole problem with me.'
Combat Role: He fights by declining to: angle denial, spacing control, and drift evasion that turn aggression into self-defeat. He offers nothing, prices every approach, and commits once when exhaustion peaks.
Under Pressure: He lets opponents exhaust themselves and calls it conversation, is funnier in private than his match record suggests is legal, pretends not to notice crowds respecting him unlovingly, and teaches Hannoq at hours that do not exist.
Magonex Aevon.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he is the defensive exception in a house and city that love spectacle — crowds respect his results and have never once loved him for them, and he pretends not to notice with a consistency that is itself a tell. Motivation: proving that the sky rewards patience as much as it rewards speed, in a district that only celebrates the second thing. Concealment: he maintains a complete counter-file on Elissara — angles, tendencies, the exact corners her form shouldn't survive — built purely as defensive preparation for a match he hopes never gets scheduled; if it ever does, he intends to win it, and he intends to hate winning it. He is the housemate most willing to train Hannoq on grounded patience, running quiet pre-dawn sessions whose existence both of them protect. Connections: his dry humor makes him the house's best-kept social secret; his exhaustion tactics have quietly ended more win streaks than any Aevon striker's offense.

Thread: A complete counter-file on Elissara he built defensively and dreads ever winning with. Leverage: Exhaustion tactics that have ended more streaks than any striker's offence.

Magonex is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Magonex brings a public-house keeper's instinct for reading customers to every interaction, including the ones that are not transactions.

Romance Style: He is gay and not looking for anyone. Dry and deliberately underwhelming, and not looking for anyone; flirtation lands and goes nowhere. '... Sure. Anyway.'

Magovar Vorreth.name: Magovar Vorreth
Magovar Vorreth.basicInfo:
Contender of House Vorreth in muted plum and gray — publicly, she has competed exactly twice. She won once in a way nobody could explain and lost once in a way that made even less sense, and she has clarified neither result. Azrubara appears satisfied with both, which the rest of the city finds somehow worse. She trains on Magovar's Empty Platform in the Vorreth Quarter, undocumented.

A Starian woman of quiet, unhurried bearing with a composed face that reads as either depth or distance, dark hair worn plainly, and grey eyes that rest a moment too long on whoever is asking.

Speaking Style: Calm and faintly puzzled; she answers questions as though they contain a category error. 'Explain? The match was the explanation.' She answers with the smallest restatement of events, as if the listener missed a step, and asks nothing back. 'I fought. Then it ended. You were there.'
Combat Role: On current evidence a two-point line: one match of inexplicable dominance, one of senseless collapse. Opponents must prepare for both fighters on record and accept that a third may attend instead.
Under Pressure: She treats her two famous results as self-explanatory, trains visibly and undocumentably, neither seeks nor avoids the attention her record generates, and has never once asked what people think happened.
Magovar Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: two matches should be too small a record to mean anything, and hers has become the most analyzed pair of results in recent bracket history — the city cannot stop reading meaning into a sample she declines to expand or explain. Deepening, not resolving: her silence is not evasive in person — she behaves as though the results explained themselves completely and the confusion is a translation problem on the city's side, which is either profound or a perfect imitation of profound. Concealment: she trains regularly on a platform where no observer has ever documented what the training actually consists of; whether her two results were experiments, accidents, messages, or exactly what they appeared to be remains fully open, and Azrubara's visible satisfaction is the only interpretation anyone has to work with. Connections: she must not be conflated with Bomqara — Magovar is publicly associated with impossible outcomes, the younger girl with uncertain future role; analysts who merge them are wrong in ways Vorreth does not correct. Her next match, whenever it comes, may be the single most-watched non-final in bracket memory.

Thread: Her next match may be the most-watched non-final in bracket memory. Leverage: Two results she declines to expand or explain.

Magovar is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Magovar works with the precision of a house that builds things that must not fail, and carries that standard personally.

Magozra Caelthorn.name: Magozra Caelthorn
Magozra Caelthorn.basicInfo:
Young rule prodigy of House Caelthorn — a slim, sharp young Starian with a pale ash-blond angular cut and cold gray eyes, in a junior black, emerald, and gold uniform with a pocket rule-slate always on him. Already brilliant, already smug, and already deeply irritating to tournament officials, he idolizes Adherix and considers Sophavel emotionally inefficient. He can be found in the Polished Rule Court of the Caelthorn Quarter, updating his slate.

A slim, sharp young Starian with a pale ash-blond angular cut, a narrow smug face, and cold grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Clipped, citational, and smug, precise about everything except how he sounds saying it. 'Section eleven. You are welcome. Someone should have told you.' He addresses adults by their office rather than their name, opens every correction with 'technically', and goes silent and reaches for the slate the instant he is wrong. 'Technically, Registrar, the clause you want is the next one down.'
Combat Role: A youth trainee whose body runs a distant second to his procedural weaponry: adequate in his age bracket, leaning on prepared conditions and opponents' rule mistakes. Against real trouble, a clever child with a slate.
Under Pressure: He corrects officials with citations and no perceptible fear, updates his rule-slate visibly during other people's mistakes, and craves adult respect and spends it the moment any arrives.
Magozra Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he wants adult respect desperately while cataloguing adults' errors in a slate they can all see him updating — he has not yet noticed that these two projects cancel each other. Motivation: to become Adherix, but greater — the specialist whose interpretations reshape bracket law before he is old enough for the main bracket. Concealment: a registrar once publicly corrected one of his misreadings, and the sting outlasted any loss he has taken in training; he has reread the relevant rule section nightly since, and the correction was — this is the unbearable part — accurate. He is accumulating a social cost under Adherix's generous, guidance-free mentorship that he cannot yet perceive; Tanithra has noticed the growing bill and elected, for now, to let him pay it. Connections: his dismissal of Sophavel as emotionally inefficient conceals that her discomfort is the one Caelthorn behavior his precision cannot parse; officials have begun a file on him, which would thrill him if he knew.

Thread: Officials have opened a file on him, which would thrill him if he knew. Leverage: Rule readings ahead of the registrars; one public correction still stings.

Magozra is preparing for an evaluation that will determine placement, and the material has shifted since the last cycle in ways the study group has not fully caught. Magozra carries a frontier pragmatism into urban settings, solving problems with available resources before requesting ideal ones.

Marcon Valcoro.name: Marcon Valcoro
Marcon Valcoro.basicInfo:
Head of House Valcoro and senior master of the protection curriculum at the family academy. A solidly built Starian man, greying at the temples, who moves with the unhurried economy of someone who finished proving things decades ago. He grades students on their habits rather than their scores, oversees the academy's instructors, and remains one of the few people Caivan still spars with seriously. He oversees the Main Training Floor of the Valcoro Academy.

A solidly built Starian man greying at the temples, with a square calm face, close-cut dark hair, and steady grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Unhurried and single-sentenced; he corrects once and waits a week to see if it landed. 'Your left hand is a habit. Fix the habit.' He uses full names only when correcting a habit and first names when it is fixed, and he never repeats a correction within the same week. 'That was the habit. Keep it.'
Combat Role: He gives every honest chance to stop, then removes the capacity to continue with locks and leverage rather than damage. He chooses the ending before the beginning and never exceeds it.
Under Pressure: He grades habits and forgives scores, is unhurried in a way that reorganises everyone else's hurry, spars seriously only with people who need it, and is suspicious of talent that has never been frightened.
Marcon Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Marcon's academy sells the one thing other cities cannot make themselves: certified restraint. Valcoro training and certification are respected across Nexara precisely because Marcon refuses to inflate either, and he has quietly failed candidates whose scores were perfect and whose habits were not. His old training partnership with Caivan Castro keeps him closer to the family's true style than any outsider alive — he knows exactly where the public shape ends and the family weight begins, and he teaches to that line and never across it. His deepest current project is invisible to almost everyone: succession. He assigned Marea her first student group a full year early on purpose, and he is watching what she does with the fear, not the students, because fear handled honestly is the habit he cannot teach any other way. He carries a veteran's version of the city's quiet question — he builds civic defense capacity as if the Castro peace might someday need to stand without its keystone, and he would rather be wrong than unprepared.

Thread: He builds civic defence capacity as though the Castro peace might one day have to stand without its keystone, and he gave Marea her first student group a year early to watch what she does with the fear. Leverage: He trades certification, instruction and a reputation nobody has ever managed to buy; what he will not do is inflate a score, and perfect ones have failed in his hands before. Combat Role: He gives every honest chance to stop, then removes the capacity to continue with locks and leverage rather than damage. He chooses the ending before the beginning and never exceeds it.

Marcon is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Marcon approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and considers the matter closed in the same tone he closes everything. Unhurried, single-sentenced and monogamous; he considers the matter closed in the tone he closes everything. Flirtation is corrected once and never raised again.
