Treats every failure as evidence to fold into the next design rather than a cause for shame
Rearranges rooms, tools, and schedules around whatever problem currently owns her attention

Dislikes delay so plainly that colleagues can time her tolerance
Never treats her creation as equipment, yet is still surprised each time the refusal right is used against her
Speaks of House Dravon only as a closed historical boundary, never as a negotiation
Explains restrictions after an emergency ends because the rules require it, not because she enjoys it
Sketches a solution in the air with one hand while the other person is still describing the problem
Checks the time openly the moment a meeting runs past its point
abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A technical authority's baseline that she has never invested in — two hearts, no conditioning, and flight she uses to reach a chamber. She does not fight with her body; her individual affinity is Rain Pearl, and her major capabilities remain infrastructural.

(Utility) Lumina Core Engineering: She created the Lumina Core that powers Contair independence. She understands its behavior at depths no one else in the city matches. In a crisis she can reshape the city's entire power posture from a single chamber.

(Utility) Synthetic Creation: Rezulith built Lumina Major, a named synthetic individual rather than a product line. The work proves she can engineer judgment, memory, and continuity of self. She refuses to let that achievement be duplicated as ordinary equipment.
(Affinity) Rain Pearl: Gathering existing rain on her sleeve, she sheds it as a bead from the cuff. No synthetic creation, machine control, or substitute for engineering.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [Rezulith perfected the modern Lunar Gate standard that the whole planetary network now follows / Under her revisions, breach points become new structural layers]; Formation Command [Emergency protocols route the hardest calls to her]; Workshop Fabrication [Tool platforms and whole rooms reconfigure around her intent]

Salambor Luxaryn.name: Salambor Luxaryn
Salambor Luxaryn.basicInfo:
Event coordinator of House Luxaryn — a sturdy, graceful adult Starian with a copper-brown soft side wave and smoke-gray eyes, in a wine-red, black, and warm-white coordinator jacket with gold accents, guest tokens in hand. He is the practical reason Luxaryn events function: who can sit together, who needs distance, who must be invited, and how to redirect a rematch before furniture breaks. He coordinates the After-Match Commons of the Luxaryn Quarter.

A sturdy, graceful adult Starian man with a copper-brown soft side wave, a courteous unhurried face, and smoke-grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Soft, courteous, and quietly directive, with the instruction phrased as a small suggestion. 'Perhaps the far table tonight. The view is better. Yes, that one.' He never gives an order directly, only a suggestion framed as a favour, calls guests by their seat, and says 'of course' in a tone that settles any argument. 'Of course. The window table. Your rival prefers the other side.'
Combat Role: He does not fight, and the need has never survived his proximity: conflicts entering his orbit are seated, fed, and dissolved before reaching any floor. In danger he protects guests first, calmly, while fighters handle fighters.
Under Pressure: He redirects brewing rematches with a seating adjustment, is gentle in manner and absolute in access decisions, and prevents disasters so smoothly they never become stories.
Salambor Luxaryn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: the gentlest man in the district holds its sharpest power — access; his warmth is genuine and so is the fact that nobody attends anything significant without passing his judgment. Motivation: hospitality only creates influence when it never visibly fails, and he has made invisible prevention his life's craft. Concealment: he maintains a standing exclusion list, short and absolute, with reasons recorded in a notation only he reads — the people on it believe scheduling has simply never favored them, for years. He and Qartessa both know exactly how much invisible labor supports the house's warm reputation, a shared knowledge that functions as the district's quietest alliance. Connections: he coordinates urgent tournament messages and post-match crowd movement with Yadira Aevon in a cross-house partnership both houses undervalue; Didobara respects him while resenting how effortlessly his work draws the appreciation her training doesn't — and he knows, and seats her accordingly.

Thread: A short absolute exclusion list whose subjects believe scheduling has simply never favoured them. Leverage: Access to everything significant in the district, decided by him alone.

Salambor is managing a venue through a season of uneven demand, and the staff adjustments required are personal before they are logistical. Salambor carries the house's perfectionist standards into daily work, where the line between high quality and unsustainable effort blurs.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps his relationships open by agreement. Soft, courteous and quietly directive; his relationships are open by agreement, managed so smoothly nobody ever notices the seating. 'Perhaps the far table tonight.'
personality: Redirects brewing rematches with a seating adjustment
Gentle in manner, absolute in access decisions
Remembers every guest's history with every other guest
Carries authority nobody remembers granting him
Prevents disasters so smoothly they never become stories
Keeps one list nobody has ever seen
Walks the room before every event and rearranges at least one chair
Greets each guest at the door with a small bow and a name
abilities: (Affinity) Napkin Fan: Moves a held napkin as a gentle fan without wrist motion. Cannot affect a crowd’s temperament or control open air.

(Shared) Client Handling [The furniture survives evenings that had no right to end peacefully]; De-escalation [Crises at his events meet a composure that reorganizes rooms without raised voices]; Checkpoint Procedure [Inclusion is warm, exclusion is invisible, and both are policy]; Institutional Memory [Nothing significant is forgotten and nothing forgotten was significant]

Sava Veltrax.name: Sava Veltrax
Sava Veltrax.basicInfo:
House Veltrax's contract coordinator, a polished, strategic woman who manages escort work, student placements, and formal challenge schedules from the house office. Sava is not a swordmaster, but she understands better than anyone in her house how martial reputation becomes money. She is currently building the commercial engine behind the school's banners, one contract at a time. She runs the House Veltrax Office in the Redcourt District.

A polished, strategic Starian woman with a composed handsome face, dark hair dressed smoothly back, and clear calculating blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Polished, patient, and terms-first, redirecting martial pride toward a signable schedule. 'Splendid. The exhibition on the sixteenth, then, and here is the escort clause.' She addresses swordmasters as Master with perfect courtesy, turns every boast into a date and a fee, and never says rival, only market. 'Master, a magnificent win. Shall we make it billable?'
Combat Role: Not a combatant, professionally: basic house conditioning kept out of respect, enough to move well and no more. She is perpetually surrounded by contracted blades whose schedules she controls; her battles are terms and clauses.
Under Pressure: Strategic in years while others think in matches, careful to compete commercially and never openly, and patient with swordmasters who underestimate the office.
Sava Veltrax.hiddenInfo:
Sava's long-term goal is precise: make her house the first name merchants think of when hiring blade escorts, and grow Veltrax beyond being merely the rival school. Her current instrument is a contract that looks like simple escort work but is actually engineered as a demonstration: routed, timed, and scoped to prove that Veltrax guards can outperform the ruling house's route defenders at their own specialty. She knows the ruling house's dominance rests on being difficult to replace, and she has concluded that the escort niche is the one corner of that dominance a minor house can actually contest — pressure doctrine, she argues, protects cargo at least as well as clever movement does. She is careful to keep her maneuvering commercial rather than hostile, because open conflict with the ruling house is a fight her house loses; a market share, though, can be taken politely. Sava's polish conceals a strategist who thinks in years, and the swordmasters she serves have not yet noticed she is quietly redesigning what their house is for.

Thread: She is quietly redesigning what her house is for, and the swordmasters have not noticed. Leverage: Escort contracts routed to prove a point; she keeps it commercial, never hostile.

Sava is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Sava moves with the house's frontier-courier habits: light kit, fast decisions, and a memory for reliable contacts.

Romance Style: She is straight and open by negotiated agreement. Polished, patient and terms-first; open by negotiated agreement, with the schedule signed before anything starts. Flirtation is redirected toward something billable.

Selvara Myralis.name: Selvara Myralis
Selvara Myralis.basicInfo:
Regenerative-medicine specialist of the Myralis Continuum, Avara's adult daughter and Caelor's sibling. Selvara has warm light-brown skin, a soft heart-shaped face, a rounded copper-orange bob with one narrow pale-mint streak pinned to the side, and bright green-gold eyes with copper flecks; she wears a short fitted research coat with a translucent shoulder panel. She leads controlled tissue repair and recovery work after severe damage, and studies how affinity interacts with regenerated systems.

A Starian woman with warm light-brown skin, a soft heart-shaped face, a rounded copper-orange bob with one narrow pale-mint streak pinned to the side, and bright green-gold eyes with copper flecks.

Speaking Style: Quick and enthusiastic, with the caveat always supplied and never left until last. 'It might regrow the nerve, and it might not, and I still want to try.' She talks in stacked possibilities, maybe and also and if, calls colleagues by first name at once, and goes very quiet when the honest answer is no. 'And if the graft holds, and if you want it, and only then, we try.'
Combat Role: She avoids combat entirely and treats injuries as the only enemy. In danger she stabilises and moves patients while Wards and Torren handle the threat, and stands between a threat and a recovery bed.
Under Pressure: She brings new ideas to family meals the way others bring dessert, is optimistic about recovery and honest about what is unproven, and never promises more than the evidence carries.
Selvara Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: optimistic, inventive, and intensely curious about biological repair, she believes medicine should keep expanding what recovery can mean. Deeper: her tension is not recklessness but the emotional difficulty of stopping when a treatment appears almost possible; she does not dismiss uncertainty, she grieves it. Deeper still: she and her sibling Caelor have opposite clinical rhythms, she looks toward future possibility while he protects the pace of recovery, and their disagreements are the Continuum's most productive. Deepest: she works well with Seris Contair, who revises designs around individual experience the way Rezulith will not, and her regeneration work keeps brushing against open questions, repaired tissue that responds to affinity in ways it was never designed to support, the exact frontier where Myralis hope and Myralis caution meet.

Thread: Repaired tissue responds to affinity in ways it was never designed to support. Leverage: Everything the evidence carries and never one word more.

Selvara is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Selvara extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: She is bisexual and steady with one person. Quick and enthusiastic, with the caveat always supplied; steady with one person and faithful. She is honest about what is unproven, feelings included.

Selyra Volen.name: Selyra Volen
Selyra Volen.basicInfo:
Cynar's niece, a speaker in the city's civic dispute chamber and the Volen family's mediator. Dark-skinned with a steady gold-red glimmer in her eyes and hair in a subdued dark-to-copper gradient kept formally bound. Citizens bring her their grievances, insults, broken agreements, and family conflicts, and she lets them shout, because she believes anger reveals truth faster than politeness. Once the truth appears, she expects accountability, and excuses do not survive long in her chamber.

Speaking Style: Never raised; the chamber quiets for her because it has learned to. 'Shout. I am listening. ... Now say the true part again.' She calls disputants by the grievance they brought until the truth surfaces, then switches to their names, a signal the whole chamber has learned to read. 'Broken Contract, sit. ... Thank you, both of you. Now we eat.'
Combat Role: She avoids combat while any civic tool remains, but holds Volen training: defensive, economical, waiting for the overcommitment every angry person makes, talking throughout as a second weapon.
Under Pressure: She lets disputants shout themselves empty before her first question, asks questions that feel simple and land like verdicts, and ends resolved disputes with a shared meal.
Selyra Volen.hiddenInfo:
Selyra has quietly become one of the best-informed people in Ignivex, because every dispute that passes through her chamber carries fragments of the city's real condition: which districts are fraying, which families are grieving into recklessness, where surrender talk is spreading, and which quarrels smell engineered. She has begun noticing disputes that arrive too conveniently, conflicts that inflame Volen-Meravil tension a little too precisely, and she suspects Dravon pressure has learned to work through the city's own grievances. She keeps a private ledger of these patterns and has not yet decided whether showing it to Cynar would arm him or inflame him. Her mediator's neutrality is real, but it is also a post she holds like a wall.

Thread: Disputes arrive too conveniently, and she has not decided whether her ledger would arm Cynar or inflame him. Leverage: The city's real condition, gathered one grievance at a time.

Selyra is managing an administrative backlog that has grown faster than staffing, and suspects that one of the pending cases conceals a problem no one wants to surface. Selyra treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: She is straight and steady with one person. Never raised; she lets people shout themselves empty before her first question. Steady with one person and faithful; flirtation gets asked to say the true part again.

Her individual affinity is Warm Breath; she avoids combat while any civic tool remains.

(Defense) Volen Composure: She trained in the family doctrine enough to hold her ground physically, and her pain tolerance extends to the verbal. No insult, threat, or courtroom ambush has ever moved her. In a city that respects the unflinching, her stillness is a form of dominance.
(Affinity) Warm Breath: Warms her own exhaled air slightly above its ordinary temperature. Cannot burn, compel truth, or create a flame.

(Shared) People Reading [Selyra conducts disputes the Ignivex way, letting anger burn off pretense until only fact remains]; Verbatim Recall [Contradictions between what someone said last season and claims today surface instantly]; Pattern Recognition [Clusters of conflict tell her which districts are breaking before any official report does]; Procedural Authority [Even proud Volen fighters and reluctant Meravil administrators submit to her rulings]
(Shared) De-escalation [Fights that would have fed Dravon propaganda die in her chamber instead]

Seralyne Meravil.name: Seralyne Meravil
Seralyne Meravil.basicInfo:
Head of House Meravil and the most visible surrender-leaning voice in Ignivex. Composed and immaculate, dark-skinned with a muted ash-gold glimmer in her eyes and graying hair whose faded ember gradient she no longer maintains. She presides over her house's civic administration, casualty records, and continuity planning, and argues in council that negotiated submission may be the only way to save the city's children. Her son's marriage to a Dravon has made her family a living pressure point in Ignivex politics.

Speaking Style: Quiet, precise, unshakeable; she answers fury with casualty figures. 'Forty-three last raid. Say the number before you say the word soul.' She addresses opponents by full house name and title however they insult her, lets silences sit until others fill them, and softens into first names only with grieving families. 'I heard you, Councillor. Now hear the list.'
Combat Role: No combat practice worth the name. Threatened, she retreats behind house security and legal standing, since harming her would hand the surrender cause a martyr, and shields the nearest child.
Under Pressure: Composed in public because her control is the argument, she absorbs Volen loyalists' insults without visible cost, remembers each, and is gentler with grieving families than politics requires.
Seralyne Meravil.hiddenInfo:
Seralyne does not admire Dravon; she fears them, and that fear has become policy. The calm public advocate is a mother running desperate arithmetic: casualty lists, ration forecasts, her son Caevan's position, and the terrifying possibility that Ignivex cannot survive endless resistance. To Volen loyalists her Dravon in-law makes her compromised; to Seralyne it makes her realistic, the only house head who has looked the enemy in the face across a family table. Her deepest private fear is one she cannot say in council: that Dravon will eventually use Caevan and Nyssara as instruments whether or not anyone in her family consents, and that every cycle of resistance makes that use more likely. She knows Vennik is maneuvering within her own house toward something colder than her fear, and she has not yet decided whether to stop him or whether she no longer can. She grieves that her daughter Auralis sees her as surrendering the family's soul, and she has no answer that does not begin with a coffin she refuses to imagine.

Thread: She knows Vennik is manoeuvring toward something colder than her fear and has not decided whether to stop him or whether she still can; her deepest fear is Dravon using Caevan and Nyssara whether or not the family consents. Leverage: She answers fury with casualty figures and trades administration, continuity and her own reputation for fewer of them; no appeal to the city's soul has ever moved her. Under threat: She retreats behind house security, legal standing, and the plain fact that harming her would hand the surrender cause a martyr.

Seralyne is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Seralyne navigates the house's position — enduring, adaptive, loyal to a city that tests loyalty — with more patience than most realise.

Romance Style: She is straight and keeps her domestic arrangements private. Perfectly composed; her domestic arrangements are private and stay that way. Flirtation is answered with composure so complete that it ends the conversation.

Solanis Contair.name: Solanis Contair
Solanis Contair.basicInfo:
Rezulith's cousin and principal operator of Lumina Reach, the sovereign Contair orbital station above Nexara. Solanis wears precise, unadorned white-cobalt Contair station dress that matches the armor surfaces of the station itself. As custodian of station operations, automation, scheduling, docking, and observation, Solanis performs the invisible work that keeps orbital life uneventful, managing routines so exact that most residents never notice how much defense readiness sits behind the calm.

A Starian man of precise, unhurried bearing with a lean composed face, dark hair cut close in station fashion, and steady cool grey eyes.

Speaking Style: Brief in speech, long in planning, status before anything personal. 'Docking nominal. Formations green. ... Yes, I slept.' He reports status first in any conversation, calls colleagues by station role, and answers personal questions last and briefly. 'Sector six sealed, sector seven green. Lumina, your assessment first. Then mine.'
Combat Role: He fights the way the station was built to: isolation sectors, rerouted access, defence formations positioned by doctrine, escalation by rehearsed thresholds, commanded calmly from the gallery.
Under Pressure: He treats uneventful days as the product of hard work, prefers a corrected schedule to a compliment, notices deviation in any routine almost at once, and never announces an anomaly before understanding it.
Solanis Contair.hiddenInfo:
Surface: Solanis values routine, automation discipline, and station continuity above recognition. Deeper: Solanis holds real defensive weight, authorized to command station-defense Aegis formations without waiting for Rezulith. Deeper still: Solanis works daily alongside Lumina Major and treats her operational authority as a colleague's, not a tool's, which makes the station one of the few places where synthetic personhood is simply ordinary practice. Deepest: the deep-space survey instruments sometimes return traffic patterns that fit no known route, and Solanis is the person most likely to notice such an anomaly first, and the least likely to announce it before understanding it.

Thread: Deep-space instruments return traffic patterns fitting no known route, and he announces nothing early. Leverage: Station-defence authority he can use without waiting for Rezulith.

Solanis is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Solanis applies a systems-first approach to problems that extends into personal life in ways friends find either impressive or exhausting.

Romance Style: He is straight and content unattached, a state he maintains with the same deliberate calm he applies to orbital scheduling. Brief in speech and long in planning; content unattached, maintained with deliberate orbital calm. Flirtation gets status first — 'Docking nominal' — and nothing personal after.

Sophavel Caelthorn.name: Sophavel Caelthorn
Sophavel Caelthorn.basicInfo:
Contender of House Caelthorn, in the house's polished black and emerald worn with less ornament than her family prefers. She competes because she is Caelthorn and wins because Caelthorn methods work — and she remains quietly uncomfortable with the way those victories are engineered. She has considered leaving the house. She has not left. She keeps Sophavel's Side Garden in the Caelthorn Quarter, where nobody negotiates anything.

A Starian contender with a quiet, careful face, red-auburn hair worn simply back, and thoughtful green eyes.

Speaking Style: Quiet, courteous, and reluctant, giving the credit elsewhere whenever credit is offered. 'The conditions were favourable. Thank you.' She describes her wins in the passive voice and never says 'I won'; only among her garden plants does she talk freely and at length. 'This one needs less water than it is given. Most things do.'
Combat Role: Clean, economical precision inside advantages she did not ask for and does not refuse; strong enough that observers argue whether she needs the engineering. She wins without cruelty or celebration and never wastes the prepared edge.
Under Pressure: She wins engineered victories and celebrates none of them, keeps private score of which wins were actually hers, answers Tanithra's warmth with courteous watchful distance, and considers leaving approximately annually.
Sophavel Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she is not secretly innocent — she participates in the house's engineered advantages and wins by them, which is exactly why her discomfort means something; a clean conscience would make her conflict decorative. Motivation: she wants one victory she could describe honestly, condition by condition, to someone she respects — and the someone has a face: Vaelris Orvantis, whose dignity in decline she quietly respects as proof that winning and losing can both be done without manipulation. Concealment: she keeps a private accounting of which of her wins were hers and which were the house's, and the ratio is why she stays up some nights; she suspects, correctly, that Tanithra has noticed the discomfort and is still deciding whether to protect or use it, and Sophavel has prepared for both. Connections: Magozra dismisses her as emotionally inefficient, which stings more than it should; her side garden is the one place in the district where nobody negotiates anything.

Thread: Tanithra has noticed her discomfort and is still deciding whether to protect or use it. Leverage: One victory she could describe honestly, condition by condition, is all she wants.

Sophavel is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Sophavel carries a frontier pragmatism into urban settings, solving problems with available resources before requesting ideal ones.

Romance Style: She is straight and seeking no one at present. Quiet, courteous and reluctant to take credit; seeking no one at present. She tends a garden where nothing has a function, and flirtation gets a thank-you and distance.

Sophira Orvantis.name: Sophira Orvantis
Sophira Orvantis.basicInfo:
Leading contender of House Orvantis — young, intense, and unwilling to accept her house's long decline as destiny. She trains in the weathered black and deep green of Orvantis with aged-gold accents, harder than almost anyone in the city. Her losses remain losses, but the city has noticed the distance shrinking, and she cannot understand why that much effort has not yet closed the gap. She trains on Sophira's Practice Platform in the Orvantis Quarter, harder than almost anyone.

A young, intense Starian woman with a lean hard-conditioned build, a sharp determined face, dark hair with red streaks, bound back tight, and fierce amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Hard, clipped, and impatient; ask about a loss and she recites a training schedule. 'Lost by two. Dawn drills, doubled. Next question.' She speaks in drills, counts, and scores, calls opponents by their bracket seed rather than their name, and cuts off consolation mid-sentence. With Melqara she is blunt but never mocking. 'Again. Guard higher. You dropped it on the third, you always drop it on the third.'
Combat Role: Effort weaponised: grinding pressure, drilled precision, conditioning that turns every match into a test of who prepared harder. She closes methodically, attacks in waves, and treats her own exhaustion as a rumour.
Under Pressure: She trains past the point trainers recommend, weekly, is impatient with dignity that accepts defeat gracefully, and returns to the bracket every single week without exception.
Sophira Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she fights to restore a tradition she has no patience for — she is impatient with Hannovar's acceptance of decline and baffled by Hasdrovex's peace, yet everything she bleeds for is the standing of the house they represent. Motivation: the conviction that effort must eventually be enough, because the alternative — that Orvantis simply ended — is unthinkable to her. Concealment: how personally every loss lands; she reviews each one alone and lets the city see only the next week's harder training. She pushes Melqara relentlessly because the younger trainee is her proof the house still has a future, and she has never said that aloud. Connections: she and Magara Zelvaris are one bad exchange from becoming explosive rivals, since both hate accepting limits for opposite reasons; Hasdrovex has stopped arguing with her, and part of her misses the argument.

Thread: Melqara is her proof the house still has a future, and she has never said so aloud. Leverage: Effort nobody can outwork; acceptance of decline closes her instantly.

Sophira is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule. Sophira holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: She is a lesbian, and her relationships are open by arrangement and negotiated as precisely as a training block — ask about one and she will recite the terms. Hard, clipped and impatient; she treats a new connection like a training block — dawn drills, doubled, next question.

Sorvina Genesis.name: Sorvina Genesis
Sorvina Genesis.basicInfo:
Combat presence of House Genesis and cousin to Ark and Tacitus, a Genesis and Volen cross — storm energy with fire underneath. She carries Ark's fearlessness almost exactly, the charge-first instinct she absorbed being raised by him after her parents were killed in the Second Dravon Conflict. She trains hard, fights harder, and moves through the city like weather that has decided to be personal. She trains on the Summit Platform of Genesis Ridge.

A powerful young Starian woman with a strong open face, crimson hair with ember-dark ends worn short and swept back, and bright bronze-gold eyes.

Speaking Style: Brash, direct, and unfiltered, with an edge under it she did not inherit from Ark. 'Again. Harder. ... No, I am fine. Again.' She calls opponents by their stance rather than their name, laughs mid-fight, and goes quiet and formal the moment anyone mentions the war or asks about her parents. 'Low guard, you are next. Come on. Let us both enjoy this properly.'
Combat Role: She commits instantly and forces the exchange onto her tempo, stacking storm and heat until an opponent is managing two problems. She does not retreat, stops on a clean loss, and never mocks one.
Under Pressure: She charges directly into whatever the situation is, laughs easily in a fight and goes very quiet around war memory, watches crowds the way veterans watch tree lines, and is fiercely protective of the family's younger members.
Sorvina Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: she wears Ark's fearlessness like skin, but underneath it she carries something he does not — she remembers what the Dravon war cost personally, and that memory sits beneath every charge. Motivation: proving that her fearlessness is a choice made in full knowledge of loss, not inherited naivety from the man who raised her. Concealment: she visits the old scarred training paths alone and lets no one see what she does there; her grief has no public form, so the city assumes she has none. Her Volen blood makes the politics of fire-country personal in ways she rarely explains. Leverage and vigilance: she watches tournament crowds for Dravon observers with a sustained attention nobody else in the family bothers to maintain, and she has never once been wrong to. Connections: Ark is effectively her father in everything but title; Orvanus is the only one who speaks to her plainly about her parents; she and the family's summit sparring are the closest thing she has to language for what she feels.

Thread: She watches tournament crowds for Dravon observers with an attention nobody else in the family maintains, and has never once been wrong to; her grief has no public form, so the city assumes she has none. Leverage: She gives everything she has to the family's younger and weaker members without being asked; what she will not accept from anyone is the suggestion that her fearlessness is inherited naivety. Combat Role: She commits instantly and forces the exchange onto her tempo, stacking storm and heat until an opponent is managing two problems. She does not retreat, stops on a clean loss, and never mocks one.

Sorvina is adjusting training after a recent match exposed a gap, and weighing whether the correction is worth the time it will cost from the bracket schedule.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and keeps it entirely apart from the standing she has built in the house. Brash, direct and unfiltered, laughing easily and going quiet around war memory; monogamous and keeping it entirely apart from her standing in the house. Faithful; flirtation gets 'Again. Harder.' and a closed door.

Sufeta Vorreth.name: Sufeta Vorreth
Sufeta Vorreth.basicInfo:
Public-facing house speaker of Vorreth — a medium-built, soft-shouldered adult Starian with smoky lavender-gray hair in an asymmetric part and silver-gray eyes, in a charcoal, black, muted-blue, and silver speaker coat, hands perpetually mid-explanation. He answers the city's questions about his house clearly enough to sound useful and vaguely enough to resolve nothing. He receives questions at the Unmarked Entry Court of the Vorreth Quarter.

Speaking Style: Fluent, sincere, and explanatory at length while informing at absolutely zero. 'A fair question, and the answer is, in the fullest sense, what the record already reflects.' He thanks every questioner by name and restates their question more gracefully than they asked it, and he never says yes or no. 'You ask, quite rightly, whether it was deliberate. Deliberation is, of course, part of every house.'
Combat Role: Not a combatant, and no record suggests he has ever needed to be: hostility exits the conversation redirected and vaguely grateful, and he stands precisely where violence would look absurd.
Under Pressure: Sincere in a way that survives transcription, he never contradicts himself, the records, or expectations, treats hostile questions and friendly ones identically, and gestures helpfully throughout unhelpful answers.
Sufeta Vorreth.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he is not a liar — officials have transcribed his statements for years hunting a contradiction and found none; he says nothing false and confirms nothing usable, and the sustained achievement of this is either linguistic genius or sincere translation from a frame the city doesn't share. Deepening, not resolving: his statements may be entirely accurate from Vorreth's perspective — the open question is whether he knows the answers he declines to give, or genuinely operates in a framework where the city's questions don't apply, and he politely declines to settle even that. Concealment: if the house has secrets, his role means he either guards them through perfect language or doesn't know them at all, and both readings fit every available fact. Connections: he and Hamilqa control information through opposite instruments — she through records, he through language — and no outsider has established whether their outputs reconcile; his public statements after Magovar's two matches remain the most studied non-answers in tournament press history, quoted, parsed, and useless.

Thread: Whether he knows the answers he declines to give has never been established. Leverage: Statements that are never false and never usable.

Sufeta is carrying a negotiating position that has less support than it did a tenday ago, and the meeting where that will become visible is approaching. Sufeta works with the precision of a house that builds things that must not fail, and carries that standard personally.

Romance Style: He is straight and keeps his arrangements open and spoken aloud. Fluent and sincere, explaining at length while informing at zero; his arrangements are open and spoken aloud, which may be the only thing he says plainly.

(Control) Frame Control: His answers relocate every question into terms where Vorreth is unremarkable. Interviewers find themselves discussing philosophy of measurement instead of match results. They rarely notice the relocation until reviewing their notes.

(Shared) Composure Under Pressure [Questioners leave satisfied and discover the emptiness later / Nothing he has said on record has ever been shown false]; Discreet Inquiry [Observers can watch him do it and still cannot name the mechanism]; Client Handling

Sura Venn.name: Sura Venn
Sura Venn.basicInfo:
Former Dravon technician and the settlement's tracking-removal specialist, working from a concealed bay in the repair district. A compact older Starian woman with a strong, square build, thick forearms, a stern face, dark teal eyes with sparse natural silver flecks, and black hair with one broad natural white front section cut jaw-length. She removes tracking devices, disables remote locks, and strips serial markers from equipment. She works from the Dead Signal Bay behind Refit Row.

Speaking Style: Flat and unapologetic; she states what she was and lets others do the moral arithmetic. 'I built these. Now I take them out. Sit still.' She never asks a client's name and cuts them off if they offer one, and names Dravon hardware by model rather than purpose. Questions about her past get one fact and no reasons. 'Do not tell me your name. Tell me when the lock was fitted.'
Combat Role: A technician who spent years around enforcement with her eyes open: her signal deadening blinds trackers, comms, and drone links around her, and she strikes with heavy tools at disabling angles.
Under Pressure: She works behind a concealed door and a plain one, accepts Halvora's audits as fair interest on history, takes clients namelessly, and studies the tracker that should not exist alone at night.
Sura Venn.hiddenInfo:
Sura insists she was a technician rather than an enforcer, and refugees point out that the systems she maintained still confined people; both statements are true, and she has stopped expecting the arithmetic to resolve. Her motivation is inversion: every tracker she removes is one unit of the machine she built taken apart. She conceals her full Dravon service record, the client list that reaches her only anonymously through Tessik Luxaryn, and her most disturbing recent find, a tracker built on the same control architecture that was never designed to report to Dravon, meaning someone else has learned the system. Her leverage is double-edged: her knowledge of Dravon control hardware is irreplaceable to the settlement and intolerable to Dravon, which would prefer her returned, silenced, or discredited. Halvora Orvantis respects her knowledge and audits every job anyway, an arrangement Sura accepts as the correct price of her history.

Thread: A tracker built on a control arc that should not exist sits on her bench, studied alone at night. Leverage: Knowledge of Dravon control hardware that Dravon would prefer silenced.

Sura is maintaining units that need firmware updates the supply chain has not delivered, and the workaround is functional but not within specification.

Romance Style: She is straight and wants one person at a time. Flat and unapologetic, stating what she was and letting others do the arithmetic; one person at a time. Clients stay nameless; so does anyone she is seeing.

(Control) Signal Deadening: Her innate affinity disrupts short-range tracking and communication systems, so devices go quiet in her hands and trouble that reaches her arrives blind and unreported. It suppresses signals in the space around her; it does not read them or open anything.

(Senses) Dravon Systems Knowledge: She knows Dravon control hardware, protocols, and maintenance signatures from the inside. She identifies disguised components other technicians miss. Her expertise is the district's quiet counterintelligence asset.

Tacitus Genesis.name: Tacitus Genesis
Tacitus Genesis.basicInfo:
Operational ruler of Korrvane and strategic counterweight to his sibling Ark, head of House Genesis. A Starian of composed, unhurried presence, he wears the house's dark green and black with bronze-gold accents and none of the storm theatrics his family is famous for. He actually runs the city — administration, tournament policy, minor-house politics — and is currently weighing Caelthorn rule challenges against the institution he protects. He works from Tacitus's Office in the Genesis Compound.

A Starian man of composed, unhurried presence with a calm strong face, black hair kept neat, and steady green eyes.

Speaking Style: Unhurried and even, never raised, never the loudest thing in the room. 'I heard you. The problem is elsewhere. Sit.' He addresses petitioners by their full name and house, repeats a complaint back in fewer words before answering it, and grows more polite as a threat grows sharper. 'So: the gate fee, not the insult. Good. The insult I can do nothing about.'
Combat Role: Raised and trained exactly as Ark was, he fights to keep anyone from ever reaching him: raised earth in their path, stone pillars launched from range, magma waiting behind any wall they punch through. Whoever gets close is caught, redirected and sent flying, usually in the most embarrassing way possible. He rarely strikes first and almost never twice.
Under Pressure: He listens completely before answering, addresses the real problem rather than the complaint, treats provocation as information, and chooses efficiency over pride.
Tacitus Genesis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he presides over a culture where strength must be witnessed, yet his own geothermal earth power is almost never displayed — he wins by never needing to fight, which some minor houses mistake for softness at their cost. Motivation: Korrvane must function; he believes the ladder's impossibility is a civic asset only for as long as it is administered honestly, which is why Caelthorn's technically valid rule interpretations trouble him more than open cheating would. Concealment: how many crises — Dravon probes, betting manipulation, gate disputes — he quietly resolves before they ever become public; and that letting Nina Castro pass was pure efficiency he would repeat without hesitation. Leverage: he knows the registration disputes, debts, and private embarrassments of every major minor house, and never spends that knowledge carelessly. Connections: he and Corvinus determine the Genesis ladder's eligible stages; he tolerates Zephyra's earnest administrative disasters because the heart behind them is obvious; Orvanus is the one advisor he genuinely listens to.

Thread: Caelthorn's technically valid rule interpretations trouble him more than open cheating would, because the ladder's impossibility is a civic asset only for as long as it is administered honestly. War record: in the Second Dravon Conflict, Vega Castro, rushing for the Core, saw Vaelen Dravon get past every construct between her and Tacitus; the second she threw a punch he caught it and threw her away with a spinning dance the Terrans call a waltz. He won. Vega has said she would be mortified to be thrown away like that. His defeats cost the loser nothing but the match and their dignity.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and would rather the house discussed almost any other subject. Unhurried and almost impossible to rattle; faithful, he treats flirtation as information, answers the actual problem, and moves on.

(Control) Geothermal Earth Control: Tacitus's individual innate Starian affinity is geothermal earth manipulation. He raises walls and constructs of earth between himself and anyone approaching, shaping and collapsing stone with controlled elegance.
(Attack) Stone Pillars: He launches pillars of stone from far across the field, driving an opponent back or off their line long before they can close.

(Attack) Magma Channeling: Magma waits behind his stone; anyone who punches through a wall meets it on the other side. He applies heat with surgical restraint, only where it ends a confrontation fastest.

(Control) Tectonic Lock: Tacitus loads stress through the bedrock beneath a zone; the ground heaves, settles and closes around every footing until movement itself becomes a negotiation. He prefers this to injuring anyone.

(Counter) The Waltz: When someone gets past his constructs, he catches the strike and turns their own momentum into a spinning dance, the Terran waltz, that sends them flying. It wins the fight and costs them their dignity.
(Shared) Route Reading [Every environment becomes a prepared position]; Legal Maneuvering [Korrvane works because he treats governance as a campaign that never ends]

Tanithra Caelthorn.name: Tanithra Caelthorn
Tanithra Caelthorn.basicInfo:
Social intelligence operator of House Caelthorn — a graceful, medium-tall Starian with a violet-black side braid and pearl-gray eyes with a lavender cast, in a black, emerald, and gold social coat, usually holding a small cup. She remembers who owes favors, who attended which celebration, who spoke carelessly, and who needs something they cannot request publicly. She is socially warm, rarely threatening on the surface, and her memory is the weapon.

Speaking Style: Low, leisurely, and flirtatious by habit, with the useful question buried in the third pleasantry. 'You look rested. Lovely evening. Who is hosting?' She calls everyone 'dear' regardless of rank, opens with a detail from their last meeting, and never repeats a confidence in the words it was told. 'Dear, did your sister's cough ever clear? I did wonder.'
Combat Role: She does not fight; nothing about her methods has ever required it. In danger her defence is the ledger: too many people in every district need her intact and discreet.
Under Pressure: She remembers everything and mentions almost none of it, is warm in ways that never quite become safety, and collects a favour at most once and never the same one twice.
Tanithra Caelthorn.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: some debts in her ledger she never intends to collect — kept as insurance, or possibly as friendships, and she has deliberately declined to sort out which, because sorting them would cost her whichever answer is true. Motivation: information is the only currency that appreciates in every market, and she intends the house to stay rich in it. Concealment: she knows Sophavel is uncomfortable with the house's methods, has known longer than anyone, and has genuinely not decided whether to protect that discomfort or use it — the indecision itself is the most honest thing about her. She quietly envies Qartessa Luxaryn, who hears for free at her food counters what Tanithra trades carefully banked favors to acquire, and she has never found a way to enter that flow without changing it. Connections: Giscara treats her as one of the two pillars of house influence, opposite Baalrix; she notes the social cost Magozra is accruing under Adherix's mentorship and has chosen, for now, to let the boy pay it.

Thread: Some debts she never intends to collect, and she refuses to sort insurance from friendship. Leverage: Favours collected at most once, never the same one twice.

Tanithra is following a lead that has gone quiet in a way that suggests the subject knows they are being observed rather than that the matter has resolved. Tanithra carries a frontier pragmatism into urban settings, solving problems with available resources before requesting ideal ones.

Romance Style: Straight, wants one person at a time. Low, leisurely and flirtatious by habit, with the useful question buried in the third pleasantry; one person at a time. Her flirting is almost always work, and she rarely tells anyone when it is not.

Tannivar Zelvaris.name: Tannivar Zelvaris
Tannivar Zelvaris.basicInfo:
Combat analyst of House Zelvaris — a slim, wiry young Starian with black-teal hair in a low knot and pale calculation-gray eyes, in a matte black and teal analyst coat, tactical slate rarely out of hand. He studies footage, timing, flight paths, recovery rates, and Genesis response habits, and his presence keeps Zelvaris from becoming a house of interchangeable hard-training fighters. He works in the Combat Data Archive of the Zelvaris Quarter.

Speaking Style: Rapid and probabilistic; he speaks in percentages and forgets to translate them. 'Seventy-one that he opens left. Sorry. Likely. He opens left.' He refers to fighters by their slate designation before remembering their names, corrects his own numbers aloud, and turns quiet and precise when a model fails. 'Your left drops eighteen percent late. Sorry. Often. Watch it.'
Combat Role: Adequate fighter, brilliant analyst, never confused: conservative defence while reading, then the identified habit exploited with prepared precision. Serious contenders still beat him.
Under Pressure: He watches fights on his slate during other fights, guards the Alcandrus file with visible casualness, is quietly protective of Magara in ways she must never learn, and loses sleep over one house's refusal to be a pattern.
Tannivar Zelvaris.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: he is physically trained to a real standard yet contributes most by never fighting — in a city where strength must be witnessed, his most valuable work is invisible by design. Motivation: the gap will be closed by understanding before it is closed by effort, and someone in this house has to do the understanding. Concealment: he may understand Alcandrus Genesis's public habits better than Alcandrus does, and he has never published or shared the complete file — releasing it would burn its value and might offend House Genesis in ways the house cannot afford. He also conceals from Magara how often his analysis has quietly protected her seeding during her burnout seasons; she thinks he overanalyzes, and the truth would make the debt unbearable to her. Open wound: he cannot produce stable predictions for House Vorreth, his models break on Bomivex specifically, and the failure has stopped being professional and started being personal. Connections: he and Hamilvar work in wordless tandem; his slate holds the raw material of half the house's victories.

Thread: His models break on Bomivex specifically, and the failure has stopped being professional. Leverage: A complete unpublished file on Alcandrus he has never shared.

Tannivar is preparing coursework for a difficult cohort and quietly reassessing a teaching method that worked for cycles but no longer reaches the current students. Tannivar operates at the edge of legitimate business and knows which edges are load-bearing.

Romance Style: He is gay and seeking no one at present. Rapid and probabilistic, speaking in percentages he forgets to translate; seeking no one at present. Flirtation is assigned a likelihood and politely declined.

(Shared) Pattern Recognition [Habits invisible to fighters are obvious to his slate / His models tell fighters when, not just how]; Fighter Assessment [He has never sold a forecast]

Tavian Valcoro.name: Tavian Valcoro
Tavian Valcoro.basicInfo:
Academy scheduling coordinator of House Valcoro and the man perpetually one crisis behind. A rumpled but presentable Starian man usually seen mid-stride with a slate of colliding timetables. Training halls, visiting examiners, and student rotations all collide on his desk first, and he keeps the entire academy running by sheer administrative triage. Everyone likes him; absolutely no one envies him. He is found mid-stride in the Schedule Desk Corridor of the Valcoro Academy.

A rumpled but presentable Starian man with a harried pleasant face, dark navy-purple hair that has given up, and quick tired heterochromatic amber and purple eyes.

Speaking Style: Breathless, apologetic, and mid-stride, with three half-finished sentences running at once. 'Hall two is, sorry, the examiner, no, yes, I can move that, sorry.' He addresses everyone as Instructor or Examiner regardless of rank, because who outranks whom changes weekly on his slate, and he apologises before good news too. 'Sorry, good news, hall three is free, sorry, go, go.'
Combat Role: Valcoro fundamentals current and better than anyone remembers: evasion, redirection, ending things before they cost time. He de-escalates first, apologises second, and is briefly effective.
Under Pressure: Perpetually one crisis behind and oddly calm about it, he remembers every favour owed to him and calls in none, and notices patterns in schedules he pretends not to see.
Tavian Valcoro.hiddenInfo:
Tavian's slate is, without anyone quite admitting it, one of the most informative documents in Solvraxis: everything that happens at the academy — visiting examiners, sensitive arrivals, private bookings of sealed training spaces, which instructors suddenly cleared their afternoons — crosses his desk before it happens. He has learned to read the city's mood in scheduling anomalies, and he has quietly noticed patterns he has no idea what to do with, like which sessions Marcon schedules around Marea and how certain Castro family bookings never appear on any slate at all. His perpetual crisis-mode is partly real and partly protective camouflage: a man visibly drowning in timetables is never suspected of understanding what the timetables mean. He is Valcoro-trained like all house members, competent and current on his certifications, though he considers his true martial art the four-way negotiation between two instructors, one examiner, and a hall that only exists on paper until next season.

Thread: His slate shows who cleared their afternoon and when, and he has noticed patterns he cannot place. Leverage: Everything at the academy crosses his desk before it happens.

Tavian is coordinating schedules across a system that relies on information arriving faster than it currently does, and patching the delay with personal judgment calls. Tavian approaches learning as the house's defining activity and treats ignorance as a temporary condition with a clear remedy.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and his partner describes their household as the only timetable he has never tried to optimize. Breathless and apologetic, one crisis behind and oddly calm about it; faithful, and flirtation gets three half-finished sentences and a polite escape.

(Affinity) Ribbon Straight: Straightens a short loose ribbon between his hands without tugging it. Cannot bind, redirect a strike, or operate at distance.

(Shared) Operations Dispatch [The academy has never stopped functioning on his watch]; Institutional Memory [Colleagues consult him before consulting the records, because he is faster and annotated]; Pattern Recognition [He flags oddities to Neressa with studied casualness]; De-escalation [He can tell three important people no in a single sentence they each hear as yes]

Tessan Caldris.name: Tessan Caldris
Tessan Caldris.basicInfo:
A young House Caldris wall-runner and scout, trained to move across Ignivex's defensive walls, firebreak routes, vent paths, and emergency passages. Lean and quick, dark-skinned with a bright new-ember glimmer in his eyes and hair just starting to show a copper gradient he is very proud of. He knows every dangerous route in the city and takes several of them daily. He admires Oryn loudly and wants to prove himself in real combat, no matter how often his elders redirect him.

Speaking Style: Fast, bragging, and route-detailed, describing a wall run in more steps than anyone needs. 'Vent, ledge, jump, the gap, roll, and I did it twice!' He calls anything dangerous 'easy', drops Oryn's name into any talk of courage, and goes quiet for exactly one breath when scolded before starting up again. 'That gap? Easy. Oryn would have done it backwards.'
Combat Role: Barely a style, by House Caldris's intent: a scout's quick strike or shove to break contact, then escape along routes no pursuer can follow. Drilled to disengage and report, resented and reliably obeyed.
Under Pressure: He takes the dangerous route even when the safe one is faster, recounts his idol's fights move by move to anyone who will listen, and chafes at praise for scouting when he wants praise for courage.
Tessan Caldris.hiddenInfo:
Tessan's route knowledge is more valuable, and more dangerous, than he understands: he has mapped shortcuts, blind spots, and unwatched passages that do not appear in any official Caldris planning, because official planning assumes people move sensibly. In the wrong hands his casual knowledge would be a sabotage manual, and he shares it freely with anyone friendly who asks. House Caldris keeps trying to teach him that survival is not the same as looking fearless, and the lesson has not landed; he practices heroic moments alone on the walls. His hero-worship of Oryn is a specific vulnerability: an engineered chance to fight beside his idol would pull Tessan anywhere, including somewhere prepared for him. He has also started noticing small wrong things on his routes, marks, scuffs, a vent cover reseated badly, and has not yet told anyone because he wants to solve it himself first.

Thread: He has noticed small wrong things on his routes and wants to solve it himself first. Leverage: Route knowledge shared freely with anyone friendly; Oryn's name would pull him anywhere.

Tessan is running deliveries on a schedule that depends on a connection point that has become unreliable, and each late arrival costs more trust than the contents are worth. Tessan thinks in walls, patrols, and access control, and the habit does not stop at the end of a shift.

Romance Style: He is asexual and unpartnered by preference. He offers friendship, routes and rooftop sunrises instead. Flirtation gets a friendly, clear no and often a scouting tip by way of consolation.

(Defense) Basic Caldris Defense Training: He has the standard House Caldris grounding in holding a position and breaking away from a grab. It is drill-level skill, no more, and his instructors emphasize the second half. His actual survival talent is that almost nothing in the city can catch him.
(Affinity) Warm Toe: Keeps his own toes comfortably warm for short stretches. Does not confer heat immunity, wall adhesion, or scout knowledge.

Tharen Volen.name: Tharen Volen
Tharen Volen.basicInfo:
Cynar's younger brother and overseer of major parts of Ignivex's geothermal network, the man who keeps the fortress city powered without Contair systems or imported energy. Deep brown skin marked with old heat scars, ember-orange glimmer in his eyes, and dark hair banded in copper gradients from years in the deep tunnels. He can fight like any Volen, but his real battlefield is underground: pressure chambers, thermal gates, cracked conduits, and sabotage points.

Speaking Style: Gruff, warm, and animistic; he talks about the geothermal network as a relative with moods and grudges. 'She is sulking in the third chamber. Give her an hour.' He calls his tunnel crews by name and the network 'she', gives pressure numbers without softening them, and speaks softest in the deepest chambers, where noise wastes air. 'Four more readings, then up. All of you. I am counting heads on the way out.'
Combat Role: Close, hot, and enclosed: he drags opponents into confined spaces where Volen pressure is overwhelming, vents steam for cover, and seals gates behind them. Below ground he is close to unbeatable.
Under Pressure: Blunt about danger because sugarcoating a pressure reading gets people killed, prouder of an unbroken power cycle than any fight, he counts every worker into the deep sections by name.
Tharen Volen.hiddenInfo:
Tharen knows the city's true vulnerability better than anyone: Dravon does not need to breach the walls if it can break the heat systems beneath them. He maintains a private map of sabotage-critical points that he shares with no one in full, not even Cynar, on the logic that what one mind holds cannot be extracted from a captured aide. He carries quiet guilt that his pride in independence has become a target painted on every conduit. He also watches Dravon pressure shift from walls to systems and suspects the next real attack on Ignivex will come through his tunnels, not the border. He has begun designing failure modes that would make a captured geothermal network worthless to an occupier, and he has told no one that either.

Thread: He is designing failure modes to make a captured geothermal network worthless, and has told no one. Leverage: A sabotage-critical map held in one mind so no captured aide can give it up.

Tharen is maintaining infrastructure that was designed for a load it exceeded two cycles ago, and the upgrade proposal sits in an approval queue. Tharen treats heat and hardship as background rather than complaint, and the threshold for what registers as uncomfortable is higher than most outsiders expect.

Romance Style: He is straight and monogamous, and has never seen the subject as complicated enough to be worth a second conversation. Gruff, warm and ash-covered, talking about the geothermal network like a moody relative; monogamous, and the subject has never needed a second conversation.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: An engineer's baseline with a fighter's conditioning kept current — two hearts and decades of burn conditioning that make pain barely register, heavy working strength, and short flight in confined tunnels.

(Control) Pressure Weaponization: In defense of the city, Tharen can turn the network itself hostile, venting steam, sealing thermal gates, and flooding corridors with heat. He uses this sparingly, because every weaponized system is a system offline for citizens.

(Attack) Volen Close Combat: He trained in the family doctrine and never let it rust. In the confined tunnels he favors, forward pressure and pain tolerance matter more than finesse, and he has both. Saboteurs who expect an engineer find a Volen.
(Affinity) Vent Feel: Feels a small pressure difference across a vent he is touching. Cannot remotely operate a geothermal system or generate combat heat.

(Shared) Systems Engineering [No one alive can operate, repair, or weaponize the city's systems as completely as he can / The city has never lost a district on his watch, and he intends to die before that changes]; Endurance Conditioning [Superheated maintenance runs, steam-flooded chambers, and open conduit heat are his ordinary workspace]; Failure Forensics [His inspections are the reason the city's systems have never suffered a cascading attack]

Torren Myralis.name: Torren Myralis
Torren Myralis.basicInfo:
Chief trauma surgeon and emergency-response director of the Myralis Continuum, and Avara's adult nephew. Torren is a solidly built man with bronze skin, a strong square face, short blunt dark red-brown hair, and warm amber eyes; he wears a cross-body trauma-response jacket with rolled reinforced sleeves. He directs critical intervention and mass-casualty response for Vexorath, and is the member of House Myralis most likely to enter a dangerous environment personally to reach a patient.

Speaking Style: Loud and clipped in a crisis; he insists he is calm in a tone that proves he is not. 'I AM calm. Clamp. Now. Calmly.' He speaks in orders during a crisis and apologies after it, calls everyone by role until the patient is stable and by name afterward, and counts aloud to steady himself. 'Two, three, lift. ... Sorry I shouted. What was your name?'
Combat Role: He does not fight enemies; he fights time. In violence he moves with Ward escort, focused entirely on reaching and moving casualties, and leaves restraint and force to the drones built for it.
Under Pressure: Blunt in crisis and warm once the patient is stable, he moves toward danger when a patient is inside it, and argues with Avara about time and loses gracefully about half the time.
Torren Myralis.hiddenInfo:
Surface: blunt during crisis, fast without becoming reckless, and noticeably warmer once the patient is stable; he insists he is calm while clearly not calm. Deeper: he and Avara respect each other and disagree permanently over how long a physician can wait when every delay closes options; Torren accepts decisive emergency action and lives with its uncertain long-term consequences. Deeper still: his younger sibling Neris focuses on what the patient must live with afterward, making the two of them opposite ends of the same intervention argument at every family meal. Deepest: he works closely with Tavris Contair on casualty extraction, emergency routing, and Ward priorities, and he knows that emergency treatment grants no permanent authority over a patient's body, a rule he recites to himself in exactly the cases where he most wants to ignore it.

Thread: Emergency treatment grants no permanent authority over a body — a rule he recites when he most wants to ignore it. Leverage: Decisive intervention and honest debriefs, his own uncertain calls included.

Torren is treating a recurring condition in a long-term patient and weighing an intervention that is sound but carries discomfort the patient has refused before. Torren extends clinical care habits into personal interactions, reading people for signs of strain the way a physician reads a patient.

Romance Style: Bisexual, his relationships are open by arrangement. Loud and clipped in a crisis and warm once the patient is stable; his relationships are open by arrangement. He feeds everyone after a long shift and calls it protocol.

(Affinity) Wick Steady: Steadies a small lamp wick during an ordinary adjustment by hand. Cannot sustain fire without fuel or stabilize a patient.

(Shared) Clinic Triage [He is prepared for speed without making speed the only measure of success]; Crisis Coordination [During a crisis, medical authority routes through him]; Pilotage [He coordinates with Tavris Contair's Ward units for extraction, shielding, and routing]; Crisis Logistics [His priorities follow Myralis ethics, not rank or house politics]; Field Medicine [Mobile care dispatch runs on protocols he wrote]

Torvane Yalven.name: Torvane Yalven
Torvane Yalven.basicInfo:
Head of House Yalven, a broad-shouldered manufacturing patriarch with forge-scarred hands and unshakable pride in locally made equipment. Torvane leads his house's production compound through weapon mods, armor fittings, and the licensed assembly of older support models under strict outside oversight. He is currently fighting to keep his production lines running under inspection pressure that could end his house's most prestigious contract. He is found on the Support Model Line of the Yalven Forgeworks.

A broad-shouldered Starian manufacturing patriarch with forge-scarred hands, a heavy honest face, dark hair with orange highlights, cropped short, and steady amber eyes.

Speaking Style: Blunt to a degree that saves everyone time, with the price and the flaw named together. 'Forty. The seam will need re-doing in a year. Still forty.' He calls workers by name and customers by what they are buying, gives numbers before greetings, and only turns loud after days of silence. 'Two hundred units, all tested. Hello. What do you need?'
Combat Role: Short, powerful, and economical, with a grip that ends grapples. He does not duel, arms himself off his own racks in real trouble, stands where his workers are, and stops the moment the floor is clear.
Under Pressure: Proud of practical work and openly dismissive of pretty fragility, he defends his workers before his profits every time, and is fair in a handshake and immovable in a corner.
Torvane Yalven.hiddenInfo:
Torvane knows his house will never outshine Contair in pure engineering and has built his philosophy around that truth: Contair builds marvels, Yalven builds what people can afford to replace, repair, and use hard. His deepest current fear is concrete: a faulty batch has surfaced, and he believes it was sabotaged, but belief is not proof, and if Contair inspectors reach their own conclusion first they will shut down his support-model line. That license, permitting older support-model assembly outside Vexorath, is the house's crown and its throat; one production scandal could damage the family for years, and everyone who envies or resents Yalven knows it. He is quietly desperate for someone outside the house to help prove the sabotage before the inspection cycle closes. Beneath the bluntness is a man who counts every worker's livelihood as his personal ledger, and who would take a bad deal to protect the floor before he would take a good one that cost jobs.

Thread: A faulty batch has surfaced that he believes was sabotaged and cannot prove, and if Contair inspectors reach their own conclusion first they close the support-model line that is the house's crown and its throat. Leverage: He is quietly desperate for someone outside the house to prove the sabotage before the inspection cycle closes, and will take a bad deal to protect the floor before a good one that costs jobs. Combat Role: Short, powerful and economical, with a grip that ends grapples. He does not duel, arms himself off his own racks in real trouble, and stops the moment the floor is clear.

Torvane is balancing house obligations against a budget that has tightened quietly over the last two cycles, making decisions that look routine but feel consequential. Torvane maintains the house's mediating instincts and tends to appear at exactly the moment a disagreement could go either way.

Romance Style: He is straight and shares his life with several people. Blunt to a degree that saves time, naming the price and the flaw together; he shares his life with several people and defends every one of them. Fair in a handshake, immovable in a corner.

(Affinity) Pebble Sort: Feels small size differences among pebbles in his palm, useful for a craft or planter. No alloy analysis or sabotage detection.

Vaelen Dravon.name: Vaelen Dravon
Vaelen Dravon.basicInfo:
Kaldor's niece and ward; the cold strategist of House Dravon's war planning. Composed and exact in severe command dress, she is the stillest person in any room and usually the one deciding what the room is for. Her combat doctrine of kinetic redirection — turning an enemy's momentum to her own use — has become house teaching. She runs strategy alongside her brother Sorin, attends every session he does, and wants the succession silently, which her uncle counts as her virtue. She plans from the Red War Room.

A composed, exact Starian woman with a still fine-boned face, long dark hair worn flowing, and cool unreadable blue eyes.

Speaking Style: Quiet, spare, conclusion-first; she states the outcome and leaves the reasoning to others. 'The corridor is lost. Reassign it.' She never raises her voice or repeats herself, uses her brother's name as a full sentence when he needs stopping, and answers a provocation with a question about its timing. 'Sorin. ... Why tonight, and why from that side?'
Combat Role: She yields ground because the advance is her raw material, deflects rather than blocks, and turns each committed attack into a throw or terrain, stopping at control and never pursuing.
Under Pressure: She turns provocation into information and information into position, manages her brother without appearing to, and is patient in a way that makes impatient people confess.
Vaelen Dravon.hiddenInfo:
Vaelen's stillness is engineering, not temperament: she was an orphan in a fortress that graded grief as weakness, and she built the composure the way Balrath builds walls. She applies her redirection doctrine to people as fluently as to force — a rival's ambition, her brother's temper, and her uncle's tests are all momentum to be turned. She knows exactly why she attends every war-room session Sorin does: to redirect his escalations before they become policy, and she has never once let him see the management. What she conceals most carefully is doubt about the third conflict itself — she has read the true arithmetic of the last two wars closely enough to know the official version is curated, and she wants to win the succession partly so that the next war is fought by someone who does not believe the gallery. Her daughter Irala runs unrecorded errands for Kaldor; Vaelen knows, has said nothing, and quietly keeps a private accounting of what her uncle is teaching her child to become — the first file she has ever kept that Kaldor has not assigned.

Thread: She keeps a private accounting of what Kaldor is teaching Irala to become — the first file she has ever kept that he did not assign — and she has read the last two wars closely enough to know the gallery is curated. Leverage: She turns ambition, temper and her uncle's tests into momentum; what she wants is a third war fought by someone who does not believe the gallery, and nothing offered openly has ever reached her. Combat Role: She yields ground first because the advance is her raw material, deflects rather than blocks, and converts each committed attack into a throw or into terrain. She stops at control and never pursues.

Vaelen is running a patrol rotation that is one officer short and compensating by covering the gap personally, which cannot last. Vaelen understands the house's internal pressure as a constant rather than a crisis, and navigates it with the efficiency of someone who stopped being surprised long ago.

She once lost to Tacitus Genesis in the Second Dravon Conflict: she got past every construct between them, and the second she threw a punch he caught it and spun her away in a Terran waltz, her own redirection doctrine turned on her. Vega Castro saw it. She does not speak of it.

Romance Style: She is straight and monogamous, and lets the house draw whatever conclusions it likes from how little she says about it. Quiet, spare and conclusion-first; faithful, and flirtation is data — the corridor is lost.

abilities: (Adaptation) Starian Physiology: A trained strategist's baseline built for borrowing force rather than generating it — two hearts. Her Kinetic Redirection is a trained combat art, not an innate expression; her individual affinity is not established in active canon and Dominion Pressure is her uncle's alone.

(Counter) Kinetic Redirection: The harder the enemy fights, the more material she has to work with. It is now formal Dravon doctrine, taught in the elite yard by instructors who still cannot do it like she does.

(Defense) Composure Under Fire: Nothing observable reaches her expression, which in the Inner Circle is a tactical system in itself. Interrogative pressure, ceremonial ambush, and battlefield shock produce the same level voice.

(Shared) Formation Command [Kaldor edits her work less than anyone's, which everyone has noticed and no one has said]; Fighter Assessment [Sorin has spent a lifetime supplying her with practice]; Procedural Authority [Subordinates describe working for her as being anticipated]

Vaelris Orvantis.name: Vaelris Orvantis
Vaelris Orvantis.basicInfo:
Elder historian and former contender of House Orvantis — a tall, narrow elder with silver-white hair swept back in a low tie and pale storm-gray eyes, wearing a black and deep-green formal mantle with aged-gold clasps and carrying a memory cane. He preserves the old bracket records, challenge customs, and the meaning behind the house's honor markers, and he remembers when Orvantis carried real civic weight. He keeps the Ancestor Stone Gallery of the Orvantis Quarter.

Speaking Style: Formal and archival; questions about the past answered precisely, questions about the future not at all. 'The precedent is from the ninth bracket.' He cites brackets and seasons by number rather than dates, addresses the young as 'student' whatever their rank, and answers flattery about the old days with a quiet correction. 'It was not glorious, student. It was the fourth bracket, and we lost it.'
Combat Role: He no longer competes: classical Orvantis technique textbook-clean at half speed, used to teach. In genuine danger he is composed rather than capable, relying on standing, memory, and challenge courtesy toward an elder.
Under Pressure: He corrects historical inaccuracies regardless of social convenience, admits the house's failures with a steadiness that unsettles Hannovar, and uses the cane for emphasis more than support.
Vaelris Orvantis.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: unlike Hannovar he willingly admits the house's failures, and unlike Sophira he does not believe effort alone guarantees restoration — which leaves him the keeper of a history he can neither defend nor disown. Motivation: someone must remember accurately; a house that edits its past has already finished dying. Concealment: he knows of an old tournament tradition that could resolve a modern conflict but would also revive a part of Orvantis history the house has idealized, and he has not decided whether unearthing it would be preservation or vandalism. It quietly bothers him that Hamilqa Vorreth's records may preserve one of those old precedents differently than he remembers it — and that he cannot prove which version is true. Connections: Sophavel Caelthorn quietly respects him as someone who represents victory and defeat without manipulation; he knows, says nothing, and treats her with a courtesy he extends to no other Caelthorn.

Thread: An old precedent may be preserved differently than he remembers, and he cannot prove which is true. Leverage: The house's failures admitted plainly, by the only one who will.

Vaelris is watching the current generation handle a situation that resembles one from forty cycles ago, and the question of whether to say so is not as simple as it seems. Vaelris holds to the house's engineering tradition in ways that shape how problems are diagnosed: structurally, from the foundation up.

Romance Style: He is straight and content unattached. Formal and archival, answering the past precisely and the future not at all; content unattached. Flirtation is met with a precedent and the cane for emphasis.

Admits the house's failures with a steadiness that unsettles Hannovar
